10.title: The Best Movie I Have Ever Seen.
10.content:
The Shawshank Redemption (1994) - Watched via HBO Max - Starring Tim Robbins & Morgan Freeman - Runtime of 142 mins. A.k.a. 2 hours and 22 minutes - Genre: Crime and Drama

Part 1: Why I Watched This Film

Normally, Crime, nor Drama aren't my type of movies, always was a fan of Action movies, for example, the MCU. So, what exactly motivated me to watch this? To be honest, boredom. That, and the fact this is #1 on IMDB Top 250.

I'm aware that this film isn't for everyone, but even if you aren't too much a fan of the crime and/or drama genre, I still recommend going for it, I'm gonna explain in this review what The Shawshank Redemption is about, the execution of the ideas, and more. Here we go.

Part 2: The Story

Portland, Maine. 1947. Banker, Andy Dufresne (played by Tim Robbins) is arrested for the crime of murdering both his wife and a man who she cheated on Andy with. Andy is given two life sentences at the Shawshank Prison, in which he meets Ellis Redding (played by Morgan Freeman), a contraband smuggler. However, not everything is peaceful at the prison. Andy is constantly assaulted by a group entitled, "The Sisters", and their leader, Bogs Diamond (played by Mark Rolston).

1949. Andy hears the captain, Byron Hadley (played by Clancy Brown, yes, Mr. Krabs.) complaining about taxes on an inheritance. After the sisters almost kill Andy, Byron cripples Bogs, who is now transferred to another prison upstate. Andy is reassigned to the library by the Warden, Samuel Norton (played by Bob Gunton) for assisting Brooks Hatlen (played by James Whitmore). Andy begins to write one letter a week to the state senate, requesting funds for the library.

1954. After 50 years, Brooks is finally released, but sadly takes his life after trouble to adjusting to the outside world, leaving the message "Brooks was here". Andy's mission to get funds for the library is a success, Andy decides to play, "The Message of Figaro" over the intercom, and unsurprisingly, is punished with one month of solitary.

1965. Tommy Williams (played by Gil Bellows) is brought into the prison for B&E (Breaking & Entering). Andy helps him pass his GED exam, but here comes the big part. Tommy begins to explain that Andy had been framed by Elmo Blatch (played by Bill Bolender), a serial killer who had actually murdered the golf pro and Andy's wife.

The next day, Andy is nowhere to be found at the prison, after they rip out the poster, everyone finds out that Andy had dug a tunnel with a rock hammer to escape from the prison. An investigation goes on.

The following year, Red is finally released from parole, and decides to break it by moving to Texas, to cross the border to Mexico. Andy and Red both reunite in Zihuatanejo, and the movie ends.

Part 3: Theatrical Run

Before the release of the movie, there was a test screening of the film. Most of the marketing did not include Stephen King's name, because the studio wanted to attract to a "more prestigious audience", who might not be too happy about it as he is also responsible for works such as The Shining, and Cujo.

The film had opened to a $2.4 million opening weekend in its wide release, and it had closed with $73.3 million at the box office, with a $25 million budget.

Part 4: Conclusion

So, after all that, is the film worth watching? In conclusion, short answer: Yes. Long Answer: HELL. YES. If you have an HBO Max subscription, definitely watch this film. I would recommend this to everybody, even if they aren't into the crime or drama genre. I'm personally not too into it, but this film was able to be the best film I've ever seen.

10.title: Shawshank Redemption
10.content:
Shawkshank Redemption

That name, Shawshank Redemption, has always been around since I was born. I never really understood why everyone watched and spoke of great things about that movie until now. After watching Shawshank Redemption, it really opened my mind to a lot of different things. This movie not only provided, the drama and crime, but it also provided action and even a mystery. This movie is about a man who had a successful career as a banker; however, one day he came home to find out that his wife was having an affair with him. In anger he decided to pull out a revolver and fix the problem himself. So later on he is then accused of first-degree murder and sentenced to two life terms in prison. While in prison the banker had a series of obstacles he had to overcome, especially being a rich guy who had everything he wanted to be a convict who is stripped away from their life. After a few years in Shawshank Prison, the banker finally began to get acclimated. Later on, it did not take long for the banker to hear that he may be innocent and then try to devise a plan to show his innocence that just may or may not work. The main characters in this film were played as, Morgan Freeman and Tim Robbins; thus in my opinion, were outstanding actors and really portrayed their characters as if it were them living that life. I believe that the director of this film did a great job in producing such an awesome movie. This review is actually very hard to write because there is so many emotions I feel after watching the movie. How be ever, the movie offered a great deal of implied metaphors such as when Morgan Freeman uses slang to describe his feelings towards other inmates which allowed the audience to constantly sit on the edge of their seat not knowing what might happen next. This movie may not be your modern era film, but it definitely made an impact on the reality of life. The director, Frank Darabont, definitely put a lot of emphasis on how Tim Robbins' character was influenced by others throughout the movie. Same goes with Morgan Freeman, his character in this movie impacted a lot of people either in a negative way or even a positive way.

In Shawshank Redemption, I think by the setting taken place in a prison really presented a more "harsh times" feel to the movie such as sexual harassment and brutal beatings by guards. Also I really enjoyed how every little phrase or word, both by an inmate or a guard, stood out and brought a different meaning to the movie. When you watch this movie you must pay attention to every little detail. If you don't, then you will be lost and continue to ask yourself, "What is going on?" That's just how it is with Shawshank Redemption. In this movie you would think it would be just your average prison film but it's not. I would recommend this movie to anyone that is interested in a good mystery/action and even a drama. This is an outstanding movie and I'm so glad I watched it because it definitely opened my mind about the reality of life's struggles.

10.title: One of the best movies
10.content:
**Title: A Timeless Masterpiece of Hope and Redemption**

"The Shawshank Redemption" is more than just a film; it is an unforgettable journey of hope, friendship, and the human spirit's resilience. Directed by Frank Darabont and based on Stephen King's novella, this 1994 classic continues to captivate audiences with its powerful storytelling and exceptional performances.

At the heart of the film is Andy Dufresne, portrayed by the brilliant Tim Robbins, a banker wrongfully imprisoned for the murder of his wife. His stoic demeanor and unwavering determination to maintain his innocence and dignity amidst the grim reality of Shawshank State Penitentiary set the stage for an emotionally charged narrative. Robbins delivers a nuanced performance, embodying Andy's quiet strength and indomitable spirit.

Equally compelling is Morgan Freeman's portrayal of Ellis "Red" Redding, a long-term inmate who becomes Andy's closest ally. Freeman's deep, resonant voice as the narrator and his portrayal of Red provide the film with its emotional core. The chemistry between Robbins and Freeman is palpable, making their characters' friendship genuine and heartwarming.

The film's pacing is deliberate, allowing viewers to fully immerse themselves in the prison's oppressive atmosphere while also witnessing the small moments of triumph and humanity that punctuate Andy's journey. Darabont's direction is masterful, creating a balance between the bleakness of prison life and the underlying message of hope.

One of the film's greatest strengths is its ability to evoke a wide range of emotions. From the poignant scenes of camaraderie among the inmates to the exhilarating moments of Andy's secretive endeavors, "The Shawshank Redemption" keeps audiences engaged and invested in the characters' fates. The screenplay is rich with memorable lines and profound themes, exploring the concepts of freedom, justice, and the enduring power of hope.

The cinematography by Roger Deakins is visually stunning, capturing the stark contrast between the drab prison environment and the moments of beauty and liberation. Thomas Newman's hauntingly beautiful score further enhances the film's emotional depth, perfectly complementing its narrative arc.

"The Shawshank Redemption" is a timeless masterpiece that resonates with viewers on a deeply personal level. It is a testament to the human spirit's ability to persevere against all odds and find redemption even in the darkest of places. This film is not just a story of one man's journey, but a universal tale of hope and the transformative power of friendship. Decades after its release, it remains a beloved classic and a must-watch for anyone seeking an inspiring and uplifting cinematic experience.

On Sept. 23, 1994, after a premiere at the Toronto film fest, The Shawshank Redemption hit theaters nationwide. The Morgan Freeman film eventually nabbed seven Oscar nominations. The Hollywood Reporter's original review is below:

Castle Rock has tapped into the wellspring of yet another Stephen King novella, from the same collection as Stand by Me. While it seems unlikely that this well-wrought film about hope and friendship in a maximum security prison will do Stand by Me-level business, The Shawshank Redemption should appeal to a mature audience. The marketing challenge will be to lure a mainstream audience to this dark drama starring Tim Robbins and Morgan Freeman with, to boot, an enigmatic title.

Covering a span of time from 1946 to 1967, Shawshank focuses on the plight of a Maine banker, Andy Dufresne (Robbins), sentenced to two life terms for the murder of his wife and lover. Laconic and a bit chilly, Andy is somewhat of an outcast among the uneducated, macho thugs who make up the main brunt of the prison population.

Admittedly, he's not an easy guy to get to know and only comes to enjoy a prison friendship when he makes a deal with the prison black-market supplier, Red (Freeman), to get him a tiny hammer for his rock collection. Red is also an enigma to most of the inmates. He keeps his nose clean and his hopes up even though the parole board routinely denies him pardon, obviously a racial antagonism.

While the story roils with some rousing prison-type action and is coarsened by an overpowering sense of frustration, The Shawshank Redemption is really about the unlikely friendship between Andy and Red: Each nurtures the other and serves as a touchstone for keeping their sanity intact.

Frank Darabont's writing and direction are generally crisp, but Shawshank is a tough watch and audiences could use some time cut from its 142 minutes.

The Shawshank Redemption" is a classic film directed by Frank Darabont, released in 1994. Based on Stephen King's novella "Rita Hayworth and Shawshank Redemption," the movie has garnered widespread critical acclaim and has a dedicated fan base. It's often regarded as one of the greatest films ever made, and for good reason.

Plot: The film tells the story of Andy Dufresne (played by Tim Robbins), a banker who is wrongly convicted of murdering his wife and her lover. He is sentenced to life in Shawshank State Penitentiary, a maximum-security prison. Inside Shawshank, he forms a unique friendship with a fellow inmate, Ellis "Red" Redding (played by Morgan Freeman). The film follows their journey over several decades as they navigate the harsh realities of prison life, all while Andy maintains his innocence and plans an extraordinary escape.

Key Themes: "The Shawshank Redemption" explores several themes, including:

Hope: The film is a poignant exploration of the enduring power of hope. Andy's unwavering belief in his own innocence and his determination to escape Shawshank serve as a source of inspiration for the other inmates.

Friendship: The deep and unlikely friendship between Andy and Red is at the heart of the story. Their bond offers solace and companionship in the bleak environment of the prison.

Redemption: The title itself speaks to the theme of redemption. Many characters in the film seek redemption, whether it's through personal growth, acts of kindness, or seeking forgiveness for past mistakes.

Performances: Tim Robbins and Morgan Freeman deliver outstanding performances. Robbins portrays Andy with a quiet dignity, while Freeman's narration and portrayal of Red add depth and soul to the film. The supporting cast, including Bob Gunton as the cruel warden, is also exceptional.

Direction and Cinematography: Frank Darabont's direction is masterful, capturing the essence of King's novella and bringing it to life on screen. Roger Deakins' cinematography beautifully captures the contrasting tones of despair and hope, with memorable scenes like Andy's escape through the sewage pipe.

Impact: Upon its initial release, "The Shawshank Redemption" wasn't a huge box office success but found a second life on home video and cable television. Over time, it gained a massive following and became a beloved classic. Its enduring popularity can be attributed to its powerful storytelling, memorable characters, and its ability to resonate with audiences on a profound emotional level.

Conclusion: "The Shawshank Redemption" is a timeless and emotionally resonant film that continues to captivate viewers with its themes of hope, friendship, and redemption. Its exceptional performances, direction, and cinematography make it a must-see for any film enthusiast. It's a testament to the enduring power of cinema to touch the human soul and leave a lasting impact.

10.title: Best Movie of all Time
10.content: Adapted from a Stephen King novella, The Shawshank Redemption takes a prison drama and twists it into a fascinating existential treatise on how to approach the business of day-to-day life in the face of a desperately Sisyphian reality. As the film's signature line suggests, "Get busy livin' or get busy dyin'." Filmed on location in an Ohio prison, the film occasionally lapses into familiar formulas and well-known stereotypes of the prison-drama genre, but overcomes them due in no small part to a pair of transcendent performances by Morgan Freeman and Tim Robbins. Director Frank Darabont and cinematographer Roger Deakins (a Coen brothers collaborator) recreate the drudgery and hopelessness of prison life in both the look and the details of dreary rituals of daily life. Spanning twenty years in the lives of its protagonists, Darabont's screenplay and direction allow us the luxury of getting to know these men -- hardened criminals, with little hope for the future -- through a series of quietly captivating scenes that slowly build atmosphere and tension without sacrificing characterization and thematic integrity. A critical success but a box office failure when it was first released, the film was nominated for seven Oscars, but won nary a one. Only when Shawshank was released on video did it steadily garner full-fledged public reverence.

10.title: Briliiant
10.content:
I admit it, not being a fan of prison movies and being puzzled by the strange title, at first glance this film wasn't very appealing to me, but it ranks #1 on IMDb and that made me curious.

I also admit that at first I was disappointed, the beginning seemed like another Hollywood cliché: man falsely convicted for murder, and it all looked like yet another fight-for-your-proper-rights movie. But after the first half hour I started realising that this is not a prison movie, neither is it a movie about hope or friendship. The background story is irrelevant for the main point of the film and could be exchanged with any other story where someone finds himself in a place of desperation. What is the true beauty of this movie is that it comprises the wisdom of thousands of years of human history, starting with the philosophical school of the ancient Greek and Roman Stoics and Cynisists and leading to the modern work of psychologists like Viktor Frankl. The film even plainly states the message in one scene, where Andy says that the one thing they cant take away from you is the freedom of thought and the freedom to chose your attitude. The first night in prison, Andy does not utter a syllable, although everybody expects him to break down as the apparent wimp he seems to be. Andy truly lives Stoic principles, never loosing it, always ahead of everybody's games. Because he is focused, not trying to change the things he cannot change, like the sadism of the wards or the fact that he most probably never will get parole, but step by step changing the things he can, while being observant of the little tweaks and holes he can exploit to his own advantage. At the end of the movie you realise that he had a plan from day one, and with endurance and focus managed to pull through. Also he never lets go of his guiding principles, which makes him incredibly strong in such a harsh environment. Andy does not simply hope to get released one day, he does everything in his power to regain freedom, and through this attitude creates a leverage so strong that he is even able to crush his enemies in the end.

At the end also Red gets it, instead of trying to manipulate the committee into giving him parole by telling them what he thinks they want to hear, he speaks of the only thing he had the power to change, his attitude towards life, and promptly gets released.

The topic alone would be sufficient to propel this movie into the top ten of the best films ever made, but it is further enhanced through a captivating story and narrative, wonderful photography, and a superb acting performance of practically every actor involved. Morgan Freeman sticks out for me, because I admittedly have a weak spot for him, but that does not diminish the contribution of the rest of the cast.

I guess it will always remain debatable which movie is "the best", I think one should not taint the extraordinary contribution of this movie to film history with such petty discussions. Without the slightest doubt this is one of - if not the - best movie(s) I've ever seen.

10.title: "The Price of Freedom: A Review of "The Shawshank Redemption"
10.content:
"The Shawshank Redemption" is a timeless classic that has captured the hearts of movie lovers for over 25 years. Directed by Frank Darabont, this film tells the story of Andy Dufresne, a successful banker who is wrongly convicted of murder and sent to Shawshank State Penitentiary. Throughout the movie, Andy forms a friendship with fellow inmate, Ellis "Red" Redding, and together they navigate the harsh realities of prison life while Andy works to clear his name.

What makes "The Shawshank Redemption" so powerful is its ability to delve into the deepest human emotions, such as hope, friendship, and perseverance. Despite being trapped in a bleak and oppressive environment, Andy never loses sight of his dream of freedom, and this unwavering spirit is both inspiring and moving. Similarly, Red's transformation from a cynical prison veteran to a true friend and confidant, highlights the transformative power of hope and friendship.

The film's talented cast, led by Tim Robbins as Andy and Morgan Freeman as Red, delivers outstanding performances that bring the story to life. Their chemistry on screen is exceptional, and their portrayal of the deep friendship that develops between Andy and Red is both heartwarming and genuine. Additionally, the film's cinematography and musical score are masterful and enhance the overall viewing experience.

In conclusion, "The Shawshank Redemption" is a must-see movie for anyone who appreciates a well-told story, outstanding acting, and masterful filmmaking. Its timeless themes of hope, perseverance, and friendship will leave a lasting impression on viewers, and its universal appeal makes it a classic that will be enjoyed for generations to come.

10.title: A Redemption Like No Other: The Timeless Triumph of Shawshank
10.content:
In a world saturated with cinematic masterpieces, it takes something truly exceptional to stand out. "The Shawshank Redemption" (1994), directed by Frank Darabont and adapted from Stephen King's novella, is a shining beacon of such rarity. With its evocative storytelling and unforgettable characters, this epic drama transcends genres and cements itself in the annals of film history. It is not just a movie, but a symphony of emotions - one that will make you laugh, weep, and ultimately, revel in the indomitable human spirit.

The plot unwinds in the confines of Shawshank State Penitentiary, a place where hopes and dreams go to wither and die. But for Andy Dufresne (Tim Robbins), an enigmatic and falsely accused banker, this prison serves as a crucible of metamorphosis. His journey of self-discovery and friendship with fellow inmate Ellis "Red" Redding (Morgan Freeman) is the heart and soul of the movie. Through their eyes, we are shown a world where friendship blooms in the harshest conditions, and hope becomes an act of defiance.

As the prison walls close in on the inmates, the film's cinematography takes our breath away. The sweeping shots of the imposing penitentiary and the iconic scene of Andy standing triumphant in the rain will forever be etched in our collective memory. The movie paints a vivid portrait of the inescapable human condition; our laughter is juxtaposed with heart-wrenching tears, and our fears are confronted by the resolute power of hope.

But what truly sets "The Shawshank Redemption" apart is its mastery of storytelling. The narrative is at once a riveting tale of camaraderie and an allegory of the human spirit's resilience. With every seemingly inconsequential detail weaved into the fabric of the story, Darabont brings King's novella to life with a finesse that leaves the audience spellbound. The movie's dramatic crescendo - the masterful escape of Andy - is a cinematic tour de force, an exhilarating testament to the power of hope and determination.

The ensemble cast is nothing short of extraordinary, led by Robbins and Freeman, who infuse their characters with quiet dignity and raw vulnerability. Their performances are imbued with grace and gravitas, making their friendship a beacon of light in the abyss of despair. The supporting cast, including Bob Gunton as the merciless Warden Norton and Clancy Brown as the brutal Captain Hadley, offers a compelling portrayal of the darker side of human nature.

As the end credits roll, one cannot help but be left awestruck by the film's hauntingly beautiful score, composed by Thomas Newman. His melodies linger long after the screen fades to black, serving as a poignant reminder of the emotional odyssey we have just witnessed.

In the pantheon of great cinema, "The Shawshank Redemption" stands proud as an enduring testament to the power of friendship and the unyielding resilience of the human spirit. It is a story that transcends time and space, a tale of redemption that reaches into the very depths of our souls. As you laugh and cry, remember that in the darkest of times, hope will always find a way. This film is not just a masterpiece; it is the quintessential human experience, immortalized on celluloid for eternity.

10.title: Genuine Work of Art
10.content: Film Appreciation is a course that many college students will take throughout their educational journey in hopes to pass time in an interesting manner while fulfilling an elective. That is my purpose of this review; to fulfill a requirement. However, choosing this film was very deliberate. Upon seeing the list of films to choose on a weekly basis of the course, I knew I would save the best for last. The Shawshank Redemption is one of the best films I have ever had the pleasure of watching. Giving special care to camera angles, costume design, lighting, transitions, sound effects, and Morgan Freemans god-like voice the creators have produced a film that will stand the test of time. Fulfilling my first requirement I will introduce our notable characters; Tim Robbins plays the mysterious main character Andy Dufresne, next we have the renowned Morgan Freeman playing Ellis Boyd "Red" Redding, and Bob Gunton starring as the Warden. Each character does an outstanding job making you believe you are experiencing a real-life tale. They possess human-like qualities that are relatable for all which aids in the emotional connection the audience is sure to form with this film. Andy has the will and drive that most people can only hope to possess in their lifetime, while Red is down-to-earth but extremely resourceful. The Warden is cruel, blinded by greed and power which most people in his position would likely succumb to regardless of what they think they would do. These three powerful characters are aided by many background characters who offer humor, softness, or harsh reality. The central theme of this film is that hope exists for all, we just need to never give up enduring life along the way. Peculiar theme to standout in a film encompassing the life of prisoners, but regardless it is my personal take away. We primarily follow the flashback of Andy who is serving two life sentences for the murder of his wife and her lover, but along the way there are other characters who receive special focus in order to evoke unavoidable emotions. We see the different sides of Andy throughout his journey, though much of the time he remains stoic as to not give away key plot points to the audience or even the characters within the film. Given the heavy dialogue and emotion there are many ideas to take- away from this film; you will just have to watch it yourself to experience them all. The most important factors of this film are the use of transitions and sound effects. Since the film takes place over a span of many years it is important to allow the audience to experience the passage of time correctly or the illusion is lost. Changing between slow motion and fast paced transitions, the film layers sound perfectly to the changes whether it is off-screen sound or visible sound made by objects on the screen. Some scenes fade away to aid emotional response, while others flash through quickly in order to give the audience of sense of the effect of the entire action going on in the scene. Combining the believable acting, with an emotional yet oddly- relatable theme and brilliantly done editing/sound effects, The Shawshank Redemption is a film that every person should watch at least once in their life-time (though I recommend more than once to really take it all in). It is a genuine work of art which I will gladly watch any day. (Especially gratifying when it can be used to fulfill a college requirement).

10.title: Hope is a good thing

The story takes place in a prison in New England and revolves around two prisoners, Andy Dufresne (played by Tim Robbins) and Ellis "Red" Redding (played by Morgan Freeman). The story unfolds and you will never expect how this is going to end.

The movie also touches on themes that I find relatable as someone from India. It emphasizes hope and friendship. Morgan Freeman as Red brings wisdom and warmth to the character, and his narration adds an extra layer of connection.

The visuals and cinematography effectively capture the emotions of the characters.

The movie's music, composed by Thomas Newman, complements the story beautifully. I love the opera scene, It made the prisoners feel an inch of freedom, symbol of hope and it gives them something from the outside world to connect to. This shows that the prisoners can connect with things that belong in the outside world.

In conclusion, "The Shawshank Redemption" is a timeless masterpiece that has a universal appeal. Its themes, performances, storytelling, and artistic presentation create a memorable movie that continues to stay with me.

10.title: A Timeless Masterpiece: "The Shawshank Redemption" Review
10.content:
Released in 1994 and directed by Frank Darabont, "The Shawshank Redemption" stands tall as an everlasting masterpiece that continues to captivate audiences with its powerful storytelling, brilliant performances, and profound themes. Adapted from Stephen King's novella, this film effortlessly weaves a tale of hope, friendship, and redemption, leaving an indelible mark on the annals of cinema.

"The Shawshank Redemption" takes place within the confines of Shawshank State Penitentiary, where Andy Dufresne (Tim Robbins), a falsely accused banker, finds himself serving a life sentence. As Andy navigates the harsh realities of prison life, he forges an unlikely friendship with Red (Morgan Freeman), a seasoned inmate known for his resourcefulness and wisdom. Together, they embark on a journey that challenges the limitations of their circumstances and explores the depths of the human spirit.

One of the film's greatest strengths lies in its exceptional storytelling. Frank Darabont's screenplay strikes a perfect balance between tension, drama, and heartfelt moments, ensuring that every scene serves a purpose in advancing the narrative. The pacing is deliberate, allowing the characters to develop organically and the emotional weight of their experiences to resonate deeply with the audience. Each twist and turn in the plot is executed with precision, keeping viewers on the edge of their seats and emotionally invested until the very end.

The performances in "The Shawshank Redemption" are nothing short of extraordinary. Tim Robbins delivers a tour de force performance as Andy Dufresne, capturing the character's resilience, intelligence, and quiet determination with finesse. His transformation over the course of the film is both believable and inspiring. Morgan Freeman's portrayal of Red is a career-defining role, as he effortlessly exudes warmth, wisdom, and empathy. Freeman's narration, with his distinctive voice, adds an additional layer of depth to the storytelling, drawing audiences further into the narrative.

The supporting cast is equally commendable, with memorable performances from Bob Gunton as the ruthless prison warden Samuel Norton, and William Sadler as the tragic Brooks Hatlen. Each actor brings a distinct presence to their roles, adding depth and complexity to the ensemble. Their performances serve as a testament to the film's casting choices and the talent involved.

Visually, "The Shawshank Redemption" captures the starkness and claustrophobia of prison life, juxtaposing it with moments of breathtaking beauty. The cinematography by Roger Deakins is masterful, utilizing lighting, composition, and framing to convey the emotional tone of each scene. The film's color palette ranges from muted and desaturated tones within the prison walls to vibrant hues symbolizing hope and freedom. This visual juxtaposition reinforces the central themes of the story and enhances the overall viewing experience.

The musical score composed by Thomas Newman is evocative and adds another layer of emotional depth to the film. It seamlessly blends with the narrative, accentuating key moments and heightening the viewer's emotional response. From poignant piano melodies to stirring orchestral arrangements, the music perfectly complements the film's themes and elevates the storytelling.

"The Shawshank Redemption" transcends its prison setting and becomes a universal tale of the resilience of the human spirit. It explores profound themes of hope, friendship, and the pursuit of freedom, reminding us of the inherent capacity for redemption within each individual. The film's enduring message continues to resonate with audiences, prompting introspection and inspiring a renewed belief in the power of hope and the strength of the human will.

In conclusion, "The Shawshank Redemption" is an unparalleled cinematic masterpiece that deserves its place among the greatest films ever made.

10.title: The Shawshank Redemption: A Timeless Classic That Celebrates the Power of Hope and Friendship
10.content:
The Shawshank Redemption is a 1994 drama film based on Stephen King's novella Rita Hayworth and Shawshank Redemption. It tells the story of Andy Dufresne (Tim Robbins), a banker who is wrongly convicted of murdering his wife and her lover, and sentenced to life imprisonment at Shawshank State Penitentiary. There, he befriends Ellis "Red" Redding (Morgan Freeman), a fellow inmate and smuggler, and uses his skills and intelligence to cope with the harsh realities of prison life.

The film is a masterpiece of storytelling, character development, and cinematography. It explores themes such as hope, friendship, justice, corruption, and redemption, and shows how one man can make a difference in a seemingly hopeless situation. The film is also a tribute to the power of the human spirit, as Andy never gives up on his dreams and plans, despite the obstacles and challenges he faces.

The film is directed by Frank Darabont, who also wrote the screenplay. He does a remarkable job of adapting King's story to the screen, capturing its essence and expanding its scope. He also elicits superb performances from the cast, especially Robbins and Freeman, who create a memorable and believable bond as Andy and Red. The film also features excellent supporting roles from Bob Gunton as the cruel and hypocritical warden, James Whitmore as the elderly and tragic librarian, and Clancy Brown as the brutal and sadistic guard.

The film is enhanced by the beautiful and atmospheric music composed by Thomas Newman, who creates a score that reflects the mood and tone of the film. The film also boasts of stunning and realistic visuals, thanks to the cinematography by Roger Deakins, who uses natural light and shadows to create a contrast between the gloomy and oppressive prison and the bright and liberating outside world.

The Shawshank Redemption is a film that deserves its reputation as one of the greatest films of all time. It is a film that moves, inspires, and uplifts the viewers, and leaves them with a lasting impression. It is a film that celebrates the resilience and dignity of the human soul, and the power of hope and friendship. It is a film that everyone should watch and appreciate.

I'm trying to save you money; this is the last film title that you should consider borrowing. Renting Shawshank will cost you five bucks... just plunk down the $25 and own the title. You'll wind up going back to this gem time and time again. This is one of few movies that are truly timeless. And it's entertaining and moving, no matter how many times you view it.

Forget about what others (including myself) might suggest you'll discover in "The Shawshank Redemption;" when you watch it, you'll identify something very personal in your own life with a scene, a character, or a moment in this uncomplicated movie. When you need hope, you'll look for Shawshank. When you want to believe in the will of overcoming even the greatest obstacles, Shawshank will uplift you in ways that you can't find in movies today.

Some liken the film to some kind of spiritual awakening. Of course, some can go to a church or mosque to find enlightenment and Faith in humanity, but most places of worship are open only certain days or times. But when you need affirmation of the lasting bond of friendships that prevail over the most dire circumstances, Shawshank will give it to you. It makes grown men (like me) cry, still. I wonder whether Shawshank was truly meant for viewing in the privacy of the home, because it is a personal experience that really makes you look inward. Nominated for seven, this is the best film that never one a single Oscar.

How ironic that an innocent man winds up being surrounded by the corruption of the legal system. Shawshank itself is similar to the character of Andy Dufresne. Prejudging this classic film, critics couldn't get past the title. The public followed suit, initially dismissing Shawshank, which failed in the box office just like "It's a Wonderful Life" and "Citizen Kane." It could have just whithered away on the store shelves, like Andy Dufresne could have in his own cell. But the characters prevailed, because Andy -- And Shawshank -- stayed true. Now, these movies are right up there as the most popular films of all time.

Anyone who has yet to watch Shawshank may be so jaded of movies, or the film's title, or how a 2-1/2- hour movie set inside the walls of a prison can manage to tap the soul of such a wide range of people. Shawshank has not one explosion. I wonder if it even has a single special effect or digitally- enhanced frame.

But every aspect of Shawshank fit together. The acting from the top to the bit part. The musical score. The editing. The.

10.title: My favorite movie even after becoming a movie buff.
10.content: I think a lot has been said about this movie and it deserves its cult following that it earned years ago. For me I watched it around a year and a half ago and it has still followed me since. It piqued my interest for movies overall which led me to some of the greats like Kurosawa, Tarantino, Kubrick, Wells, Ford, Scorsese, Ray, and many more. While movies like Seven Samurai come close to being my favorite, Shawshank is still superior in my eyes based on a couple of factors. One is that it is mainstream art which is actually more uncommon to get than the movies that feel too "artsy" or on the opposite side of latter where movies feel too shallow. Because it feels mainstream enough, I feel like in part it's able to ground itself and create a more genuine feel with its characters and the prison itself. Granted of course Andy's willpower is something you'll rarely come across in people but we feel it being well established as we see his ups and downs in the story. Reasons like this to paint him as a strong hearted person who can handle the harsh conditions of prison and feel human with emotionally is what makes him my personal favorite character even though Red is the fan favorite. Speaking of Red though I cannot deny Morgan Freeman's narration was nothing less than stellar as we get to see the movie through his lens and it's because we see how Red is affected by Andy. I think another thing people don't talk too much about is the more subtle themes Shawshank has. People obviously know hope is the largest theme which is beautifully done in poignant yet uplifting manner. However, I feel like friendship gives this undertone to the theme of hope that makes it more powerful. I loved all the interactions between the prisoners. They all feel real and human. Andy and Red in particular build this friendship that feels authentic and captivates the audience with looking at one of the positives that keeps these people going in prison. It makes the beach scene all the more satisfying because it fulfills that theme of friendship making the ending amazing and one that doesn't leave you for days.

10.title: iranrich Reviews

"The Shawshank Redemption" is one of the greatest cinematic masterpieces ever created, directed by Frank Darabont and released in 1994. Adapted from a Stephen King novella, "Rita Hayworth and Shawshank Redemption," this film stars Tim Robbins and Morgan Freeman in captivating performances.

The story begins when Andy Dufresne (played by Tim Robbins) is sentenced to Shawshank State Penitentiary for the murder of his wife, a crime he claims he didn't commit. Within the harsh confines of Shawshank, Andy discovers that corruption isn't limited to just the prison guards, but that there is also friendship, hope, and humanity to be found behind its walls. Using his intellectual prowess and cultural knowledge, Andy, with the help of his friend Red (played by Morgan Freeman), strives to reform the inmates and find redemption for himself.

"The Shawshank Redemption" is renowned for its portrayal of hope, humanity, friendship, and redemption. The depth of the story, brilliant performances by the cast, and Frank Darabont's exceptional direction have elevated this film to the status of a cinematic masterpiece.

The film's focus on personal growth and the elevation of humanity in an adverse environment has a profound impact on its audience. It delivers a powerful message that even in the direst circumstances, hope and humanity can still prevail. "The Shawshank Redemption" is an extraordinary work of cinema that continues to thrill and inspire every time it is watched.

10.title: Nice move
10.content: With all of the aesthetic touches and attention to cinematic detail, the most beautiful part of the film lies within its thematic material, such as its focus on the human desires for the most abstract concepts, like hope and freedom. These themes, which concern things the human spirit undoubtedly yearns for, seem so intricately woven into the plot that it easily draws its audience in to its story. Though full of hardened criminals, your heart will go out to these men as they display the most basic of human emotions, and deliver some of the most quotable lines in a film to date. Like a great novel, this film manages to succeed at greater things than simply entertaining an audience. Darabont tells his story most masterfully, illustrating principles and inspiring his audience to think. He leaves us a poignant film with a powerful message of hope, and redemption, something we all seek.

10.title: The Shawshank Redemption
10.content: I have watched this movie in various periods of my life: from just being a kid, to young adult, to now having kids and every single time it hits differently. And yet the throughline here is it's a masterpiece. The cinematography from Roger Deakins still appears better, more powerful and more breathtaking than most movies today. The acting is phenomenal, moving and thoroughly human. There are just so few movies that can transcend what it set out to be (a prison movie) and instead tell the oldest tale of time: the unwavering human spirit. And as someone who loves a good soundtrack: Thomas Newman's score is transformational - you don't merely hear it, you feel it. If you have never watched, I am insanely jealous of you: to be able to experience this masterpiece for the first time is a wonderful treat. Enjoy!

10.title: The Greatest Film of All Time.
10.content:
I wrote my first review of this movie back in 2006. I feel I did not do it the justice it deserved.

I grew up in Mansfield, OH, not very far at all from the Ohio State Reformatory. The old "castle Dracula" Administration building is all that is left now. A new prison (Mansfield Correctional Institution) was built on the site where the other buildings existed along OH-13. I remember the impending demolition just waiting for this movie to finish filming...

...Thank God it waited! The story begins in 1946 when Portland banker Andy Dufresne is tried for and wrongfully convicted of the double murder of his wife and her "lover".

Andy arrives at Shawshank state prison in early 1947 and is greeted harshly by ruthless authority and by thugs who seem to enjoy beating him up. Andy keeps strong and keeps very much to himself for the first two years.

Andy finally decides he needs a hobby to keep his mind occupied. He approaches the well known prison entrepenour, "Red", and asks if Red might smuggle something into the prison for him... This kick starts the relationship between Red and Andy that the movie centers its attention on.

There is a gentle tug of war between the two regarding ideals. Red, guilty of murder and sentenced to life with parole, sees no hope in existence outside of the prison walls. He tries, throughout the film, to convey to Andy that "hope can drive a man insane" and its best to just accept your fate. Opposites must attract because Andy was Red's polar opposite and it began to catch Red's attention. Andy would confront the police guard to ask for beers for his friends. He'd play music over the Shawshank PA system from the Warden's office. He'd write the state once or twice a week for years and years to get funds for a new library. Andy Dufresne dared to dream and he turned the negativity of Shawshank on its head...and just may have changed Red's view on things.

The villain in the movie is Warden Norton. The Warden notices Andy's skills and intelligence early on and took full advantage. He entices Andy to be sort of an "administrative assistant". He started out in doing tax returns for the guards, which he was very good at. In time, the Warden enticed him to use his banking skills to mastermind a money laundering scheme that would make the Warden "a millionaire when he retires". Andy had to "go to prison to be a crook". This kept his mind occupied.

About 2/3 the way through the film, a young kid is admitted to Shawshank who knows who killed Andy's wife 19 years before. Andy is ecstatic and he takes the news to the Warden. At risk of the money laundering scandel being brought to light, the Warden ensures Andy he's not leaving Shawshank. Andy gets two months in the hole. The young kid gets shot.

Andy, the beacon of hope for this movie, decides HE WILL get out. And HE WILL get his freedom.

We go back to Andy's first meeting with Red 19 years before the escape...the little chess piece chiseling 6" rock hammer that he asked for... He'd been chipping away at the concrete wall in his room for 19 years and NOBODY SAW IT COMING.

Andy busts out of that stinkin place, crawls through a 500 yard sanitary line and "comes out clean on the other side". Andy is gone and is free like a bird.

Red, with his inspirational friend gone, does begin to lose that hope that Andy almost convinced him of. Life at the prison begins to suck. Red, after 40 years, gets paroled. He has no idea how to adapt on the outside. He might just commit suicide.

Only one thing stops him...a promise he made to Andy... Determined, Red puts on his hat and suit, clamps his travel case shut. Give busy livin, or get busy dyin...thats god damn right. He bolts town and meets up with Andy on the beach in Mexico. Red, once a young crook, now redeemed old man.

10.title: One of the best, ever

It's one of those films that can be watched again and again, and never get old.

Yes, there are a few flaws, especially one particular continuity error. The film spans over two decades of prison life but the clothes never change. Everyone wears the same baggy 1950's slacks and shirts throughout.

I've always found it easier to find fault than give praise, but this really is a great film. Brilliant in every respect.

One more for the ten-out-of-ten pot.

10.title: Hope is a Good Thing
10.content:
¨Remember Red, hope is a good thing, maybe the best of things and no good thing ever dies. ¨ An uplifting and inspiring movie that reminds us that hope is what keeps us going during difficult situations. The movie ranks at number one in the top IMDb list and it comes as no surprise because many people rank this movie among their all-time favorite. Morgan Freeman and Tim Robbins give an excellent performance in this film directed by Frank Darabont and which is based on Stephen King's short story ¨Rita Hayworth and Shawshank Redemption.¨ It received 7 Oscar nominations in 1995 including Best Picture, but lost to Forrest Gump. Freeman is probably the best actor when it comes to narrating a story and this is one of his greatest roles as he introduces us to Robbins's character, Andy Dufresne. Andy is a banker who has been accused of murdering his wife and her lover and is sentenced to prison for life. In Shawshank prison Andy befriends Red (Morgan Freeman) who serves as the provider in jail because he can get just about anything you ask, yes even Rita Hayworth. The prison is run by Warden Norton (Bob Gunton) with a stern hand, and the prison guards treat the prisoners very violently. Despite how unjust life has been towards Andy he never losses hope because as he puts it ¨You either get busy living or you get busy dying.¨ There is a very positive message we can learn from this movie and if you are among the few that haven't seen it yet then I absolutely recommend this as a must see film! You won't regret it.

10.title: awesome
10.content:
One of the best movies I have seen. A story of survival carried out with artistic and intellectual dignity. The protagonist (Andy) never lost faith in himself, despite the circumstances, and that faith was based on his intellect and imagination. Two human qualities that distinguish us from animals and, in the case of Shawshank Redemption, from their almost human cellmates. About the friendship between Andy and Red, it was calm, calm and full of mutual admiration and trust. Powerful ingredients.

It is not necessary to be in the trena to realize that the modern individual or individual lives imprisoned, for a lot of reasons: that if the routines, the schedules, the family responsibilities, the various obligations... How many people do every day what they do you really want it? Very little, really.

The difference lies in the personality of each one. You can be conformist and attend to your obligations with no other pretension than to go to bed early and rest so that, the next day, you can continue attending to them properly, or you can be a dreamer, an idealist, who keeps your mind and your time busy with a thousand projects and never feel like a prisoner of your routines. In other words, you can be like Red, an "institutionalized" being, or you can be like Andy, a free thinker, a free man.

The film is not only inspiring, but it unravels with a superb sense of narrative time, captivating the viewer, who is led by the hand by all the characters residing in that prison and by their very high sense of friendship.

A jewel. A movie classic, despite its production date. Impeccable work by Frank Darabount, writer and director.

10.title: Truly deserves its high rating.
10.content:
Shawshank is an absolutely amazing film. Its concept is not especially compelling; you might even call it plain, but oh, the execution! Certainly this is how to make a movie.

I saw Shawshank in the cinema, which is always good, but not necessary for a film where the plot and filmatic skill are what draw you in. When I left, I noticed that everyone was sniffling. The film is so beautiful that even the tough people cried. I don't mean that it's a tearjerker either, it doesn't make you cry out of sadness or pull cheap stunts to get the tears flowing. Well, perhaps sadness has something to do with it, but it's a deeper kind of sadness, one that's got tears of joy in it too, not "how could they kill the dog?" sadness. And while it makes people cry, they're glad they saw it. It's not even my kind of movie, but there's no way I can give it less than a 10.

Notice that this movie is loved by all kinds of viewers. From the people who aren't so articulate to the movie snobs, this film hits home on a level that none other I know of does.

10.title: Wonderfull
10.content:
After watching "The Shawshank Redemption," you can easily understand why this film is one of the most beloved of all time. Adapted from a Stephen King short story and brought to life under Frank Darabont's direction, Tim Robbins and Morgan Freeman's extraordinary performances take the audience on a captivating journey from start to finish.

The theme of friendship in the film questions the resilience of the human spirit and the true meaning of freedom. Andy Dufresne's (Tim Robbins) unjust life imprisonment and his enduring hardships without ever losing hope inspire viewers. The deep connection he forms with Morgan Freeman's character, Red, is the heart of the film, reminding audiences of the power of friendship and hope.

The film's music and cinematography also deserve praise. Thomas Newman's compositions enhance the emotional depth, while cinematographer Roger Deakins' shots strengthen the film's atmosphere. "The Shawshank Redemption" is considered one of the best examples of cinematic art not only for its story but also for its technical aspects.

"The Shawshank Redemption" addresses universal themes such as justice, freedom, the human condition, and hope, reminding viewers never to give up in the face of life's challenges. The film offers an emotional experience while also providing an opportunity to dive into deep thoughts. In this way, "The Shawshank Redemption" stands out as a masterpiece that is not only to be watched but to be reflected upon. With each viewing, it's possible to discover something new, rightfully earning its place among the unforgettable in cinema history.

10.title: Brutal Anti-Bible Bigotry Prevails Again
10.content:
Boy, this is a very popular film, and one of the reasons Liberals love it so much - in addition to the fact that it's an interesting story and well-acted - is the anti- Christian bias in here, which is very strong.

You see, the villain, as in almost all modern-day prison films, is the warden. And, they go out of their way to show you that the despised hate-filled warden is a Bible Believer, of course. It's repeated and demonstrated several times as the warden quotes Scripture. And our hero (Tim Robbins) carves out the middle the Bible to use as a place to hide a tool for him to escape. Heaven forbid, the Book would be used for him to actually read! It's no coincidence since this is written by famous author and Christian-basher Stephen King.

Amid the bigotry is an interesting story with two likable lead characters (the other being Morgan Freeman, whose narration in the film is superb) and a very satisfying ending. Along the way we get other clichés, such as the usual sadistic guard (Clancey Brown) who beats up defenseless nice guys.

This movie is so manipulative it's laughable.....but entertaining, especially if you're another Bible basher are another naive Lib who thinks that jails are filled with intelligent, sweet-natured guys like Freeman, Robbins, et al. In the world of film-making, criminals are the real "victims "of our horrible society.

10.title: Incredible!

The Shawshank Redemption" is a cinematic masterpiece that delves deep into the human condition, showcasing resilience, friendship, and the enduring power of hope. Directed by Frank Darabont and based on Stephen King's novella, this timeless film follows the journey of Andy Dufresne, a banker wrongfully convicted of murder and sentenced to life in Shawshank State Penitentiary.

Set against the backdrop of the 1940s and 1950s, the movie captures the harsh realities of prison life while highlighting the indomitable spirit of its protagonist. Andy, portrayed brilliantly by Tim Robbins, maintains his dignity and integrity amidst the brutality and corruption of the prison system. His friendship with fellow inmate Red, played by Morgan Freeman, serves as the emotional core of the story.

As the narrative unfolds, Andy's intelligence and determination enable him to navigate the challenges of prison life, offering solace and inspiration to his fellow inmates. Through acts of kindness and ingenuity, he earns the respect of both prisoners and guards alike.

10.title: A flawless movie
10.content:
I had resisted the temptation to see this movie for quite a while, even though it was recommended to me by many friends, and I was quite impressed by the high rating on IMDB. However, I have finally seen the movie now, and I can only say that I am very impressed.

I can only say that this movie is as flawless as any movie can be. It is amazing to me how a movie with barely any action can grip you like this one just through the story, the acting and the excellent character development. The characters are extremely real and believable, and it is easy to identify with Tim Robbins' character.

Tim Robbins was actually the biggest surprise for me in this movie, and this is by far the best performance I have seen of him. However, it seems that his acting style matches the material very well. Andy Dufresne (Tim Robbins) should not be someone who is overly emotional, and this seems to be the perfect character for Tim Robbins.

However, the most moving performance in the movie came from James Whitmore. I will not spoil the movie by going into details, but even though his character's story is only a subplot, it is one of the strongest points of the whole movie, and his performance is absolutely memorable.

Still, with all the great performances, the star of this movie is its story. It is the story of someone who is objectively innocent when he goes to jail, and who loses a large part of his life in jail, but when he comes out of the jail, he is still a better person, because he has found his true self. The story proves that a person does not have to be guilty of a crime in the first place to find redemption, but that redemption can happen on many different levels.

When Andy decides he wants a rock hammer to carry on his hobby of shaping rocks he meets Ellis Boyd "Red" Reading described as "a man who knows how to get things" Red is also "the only guilty man in Shawshank" as all other inmates claim they are innocent. Andy and Red quickly become friends as Andy repeatedly tries to convince all the other inmates that remembering there are places outside of Shawshank and they should not accept they may never leave the prison. Andy then takes a young high school dropout named Tommy under his wing to help him get his high school qualifications it is this boy that brings forth the revelation of Andy's innocents after telling the story of about a old cell mate who claims to have committed an identical crime which he got away with. After Andy's young friend is shot dead by Hadley Andy asks an inmate to get him a 6ft long piece of rope. the next morning Andy does not show for roll call and Red fears he has committed suicide however the do not find Andy hanging in his cell like Red expected they do not find him at all the night before a plan that took 19 years to get ready took place and Andy had escaped Shawshank prison.

10.title: The best film of all time
10.content:
While my utmost respect is given to all the current box-office hits my loyalty truly lies before my time. In 1994 Frank Darabont brought to life Stephen Kings genius story line and gave us the best film created to date. Shawshank Repdeption tells us the story of Andy Dufrene (Tom Robbins) who is sentenced to life in prison for two murders that he did not commit. For 19 years Andy learns how to live in the harsh conditions of Shawshank prison and even attracts the attention of many fellow inmates, a soon to be dear friend, Red (Morgan Freeman), and the warden who eventually entrusts Andy to assist him in his legal work.

While the roll of Andy was originally turned by many big wigs including Tom Hanks and Brad Pitt because of other movie conflictions the universe eventually did Darabont a favor by landing Tom Robbins in the role. Robbins plays the seemly quiet, unforeseen mastermind of Andy Dufrene brilliantly. His lack of and delicately placed facial variations toys with the audience's emotions and somehow brings you to love the strange, shy convict. Perhaps the key element to Toms performance was not his own actions but reactions to the people around him. As a man of little words Robbins used his silence and expressions to rule his performance in a rare and powerful way.

No surprise is the also incredible performance of Morgan Freeman who plays Red, Andy's best friend in the prison, and also the films narrator. Red had been at Shawshank long before Andy arrived and tells his story to us, the audience, after his dear friend, Andy, is gone. Before Andy came into the picture Red had already taken on the role of a low-profile leadership role in the prison and its obvious he is comfortable behind the walls of Shawshank. However, Andy didn't come alone, he brought with a sense a hope that we see spread within the inmates in particularly, Red. Morgan perfectly embodies his new sense of hope so the audience can watch it unfold in him. Even in a prison uniform he still steals the hearts of the audience members and has us all routing for him in his journey of looking at his life in a new way. Freeman also nails his performance as films narrator. He specking with that sense of hope Andy clearly left him with, but also somehow makes us miss Andy, the way you can sense that he does. Using his calm yet inspiring voice Red highlights the overall message and leaves the audience feeling ready to take on the world.

The actor's incredible performances make this film what is it, but I would argue more than that, is the plot. Originally a Stephen King novel shawshank is undoubtabley the best written screenplay to date. Every intricate detail from prop placement to little character lines comes together in the end and forms a story like we have never seen before. The complexity is at the perfect balance where you aren't lost but you are always curious. Shawshank is a movie that you have to watch through and be constantly involved but naturally you are so intrigued that it is not hard to do.

Shawshank Redemption is packed full of brilliant characters and well thought out moments. However, in making the wise decision to watch this film you are getting so much more than the entertainment of a incredible film. Frank Darabont uses Morgan Freemans ending monologue to leave you pondering life in a new way and eager to live out the famous words of Andy Dufrese, "Get busy living, or get busy dying."

10.title: What a Movie
10.content:
Nice Movie forever. At its heart, "The Shawshank Redemption" is a story of perseverance and the indomitable power of the human spirit. Through Andy's meticulous planning and unwavering resolve, the film delivers a powerful message about the importance of holding onto hope even in the darkest of times.

With its masterful storytelling, poignant performances, and unforgettable climax, "The Shawshank Redemption" stands as a cinematic triumph that continues to resonate with audiences decades after its release. It's a testament to the enduring power of cinema to inspire, uplift, and remind us of the inherent goodness within us all.

10.title: MUY BUENA PELICULA, LA RECOMIENDO.....!!
10.content:
I'm trying to save you money; this is the last film title that you should consider borrowing. Renting Shawshank will cost you five bucks... just plunk down the and own the title. You'll wind up going back to this gem time and time again. This is one of few movies that are truly timeless. And it's entertaining and moving, no matter how many times you view it.

Forget about what others (including myself) might suggest you'll discover in "The Shawshank Redemption;" when you watch it, you'll identify something very personal in your own life with a scene, a character, or a moment in this uncomplicated movie. When you need hope, you'll look for Shawshank. When you want to believe in the will of overcoming even the greatest obstacles, Shawshank will uplift you in ways that you can't find in movies today.

Some liken the film to some kind of spiritual awakening. Of course, some can go to a church or mosque to find enlightenment and Faith in humanity, but most places of worship are open only certain days or times. But when you need affirmation of the lasting bond of friendships that prevail over the most dire circumstances, Shawshank will give it to you. It makes grown men (like me) cry, still. I wonder whether Shawshank was truly meant for viewing in the privacy of the home, because it is a personal experience that really makes you look inward. Nominated for seven, this is the best film that never one a single Oscar.

How ironic that an innocent man winds up being surrounded by the corruption of the legal system. Shawshank itself is similar to the character of Andy Dufresne. Prejudging this classic film, critics couldn't get past the title. The public followed suit, initially dismissing Shawshank, which failed in the box office just like "It's a Wonderful Life" and "Citizen Kane." It could have just whithered away on the store shelves, like Andy Dufresne could have in his own cell. But the characters prevailed, because Andy -- And Shawshank -- stayed true. Now, these movies are right up there as the most popular films of all time.

Anyone who has yet to watch Shawshank may be so jaded of movies, or the film's title, or how a 2-1/2- hour movie set inside the walls of a prison can manage to tap the soul of such a wide range of people. Shawshank has not one explosion. I wonder if it even has a single special effect or digitally- enhanced frame.

But every aspect of Shawshank fit together. The acting from the top to the bit part. The musical score. The editing. The photography. The story, from opening credits to final scene. All involved, including the town of Mansfield, Ohio (where Shawshank was actually filmed) played their roles perfectly. Shawshank is a must- see, must- own title.

10.title: Like the rest of Stephen King's
10.content: A drama about the life of Andy Dufresne (Tim Robbins) after he is sent to Shawshank prison for the murder of his wife and her lover. There he befriends fellow prisoner 'Red' (Morgan Freeman) who narrates the film with several voice-overs. An ordinary man in such a situation would be crushed by despair but Red relates that Andy was no ordinary prisoner. Although prison is a kind of hell, even in a completely unforgiving and corrupt system with an evil warden and dangerous fellow inmates, he doesn't lose his spirit. Andy makes the best of the situation and can even claim small victories while serving time. Most important (for a Hollywood film) Andy doesn't lose hope. Red initially sees Andy's efforts as futility and leading to inevitable disappointment, but over time Red develops great admiration for Andy. The Shawshank Redemption is almost the perfect Hollywood film and told well enough to touch even the most jaded viewer, with an ending that brings the ultimate cinematic catharsis.

10.title: message
10.content:
Can Hollywood, usually creating things for entertainment purposes only, create art? To create something of this nature, a director must approach it in a most meticulous manner, due to the delicacy of the process. Such a daunting task requires an extremely capable artist with an undeniable managerial capacity and an acutely developed awareness of each element of art in their films, the most prominent; music, visuals, script, and acting. These elements, each equally important, must succeed independently, yet still form a harmonious union, because this mixture determines the fate of the artist's opus. Though already well known amongst his colleagues for his notable skills at writing and directing, Frank Darabont emerges with his feature film directorial debut, The Shawshank Redemption. Proving himself already a master of the craft, Darabont managed to create one of the most recognizable independent releases in the history of Hollywood. The Shawshank Redemption defines a genre, defies the odds, compels the emotions, and brings an era of artistically influential films back to Hollywood.

The story begins with the trial of a young banker, Andy Dufrense, victimized by circumstantial evidence, resulting in a conviction for the murder of his wife and her lover. After a quick conviction, Andy finds himself serving a life sentence at Shawshank prison, with no hope of parole. He exists in this prison only in appearance, keeping his mind free from the drab walls around him. His ability to do this results in the gaining of respect from his fellow inmates, but most of all from Ellis Redding. Ellis, commonly referred to as Red, finds gainful use of his entrepreneurial spirit within the drab walls of Shawshank by dealing in contraband and commodities rare to the confines of prison. Andy's demeanor and undeniable sense of hope causes Red to take a deeper look at himself, and the world around him. Andy proves to Red and the other inmates that in the conventional walls of Shawshank prison convention will find no home in his lifestyle.

By creating the film's firm foundation, the meticulously chiseled screenplay paved the way for this film's success. Frank Darabont outdoes himself with the phenomenal adaptation of Stephen King's equally noteworthy novella, Rita Hayworth and Shawshank Redemption. In this novella, King demonstrates that he can break free from the genre he dominates and still create a marvelous piece of modern literature. Though the film mirrors the novella in many ways, Darabont illustrates a focused objective of improving upon the areas where the novella came up short, resulting in one of the best book to film transitions ever.

While maintaining some of the poetic and moving dialog of the novella, Darabont also proves that a film's score can generate a great deal of emotional response from its audience, as dialog does. He employs the cunning Thomas Newman, son of the legendary Hollywood composer, Alfred Newman. Darabont shows recognition for the film's needs by employing Newman, who makes the gentle piano chords whisper softly to the viewer, as if a part of the scripted dialog. Newman lends himself to individualism and tends to drive more towards the unique in the realm of score composition. His effort in Shawshank did not go unnoticed, as his score received an Oscar nomination in 1995. While unique and independent, Newman's score never once intrudes on your concentration or distracts from the film.

With work from vast array of talented scene designers, costume designers, composers, cinematographers, and various other Hollywood artists, the cast of The Shawshank Redemption had a strong foundation to work with. The marvelous cast of this film will dazzle you with some of the most convincing performances you will witness in a film. While both Tim Robbins and Morgan Freeman shine as Andy and Red, respectively, the true spectacle of acting lies within the plethora of amazing supporting actors who easily disappear into their roles. Most noticeable of these, the veteran film star James Whitmore, who portrays the elderly Brooks Hatlen. Brooks, a man incarcerated for an unmentioned crime for so long that he finds himself attached to the Shawshank and the daily life he has lead. Each of these actors show a true dedication to their art, and a focused purpose in their motivations, creating a convincing setting that never once caters to anything unbelievable.

With all of the aesthetic touches and attention to cinematic detail, the most beautiful part of the film lies within its thematic material, such as its focus on the human desires for the most abstract concepts, like hope and freedom. These themes, which concern things the human spirit undoubtedly yearns for, seem so intricately woven into the plot that it easily draws its audience in to its story. Though full of hardened criminals, your heart will go out to these men as they display the most basic of human emotions, and deliver some of the most quotable lines in a film to date. Like a great novel, this film manages to succeed at greater things than simply entertaining an audience. Darabont tells his story most masterfully, illustrating principles and inspiring his audience to think. He leaves us a poignant film with a powerful message of hope, and redemption, something we all seek.

Darabont shows us that artists still work in the Hollywood studios and production facilities. These artists show their capability to produce art; real art that inspires you to look at the deeper aspects of life and the world around you. The Shawshank Redemption delivers much- needed breath of fresh air for anyone who realizes the capability of film. It proves that masters of the craft still live on this earth, and still bless us with timeless masterpieces that we will never forget.

10.title: Possibly missing the point?
10.content: In reading many reviews of this film, it is evident that people will either absolutely love it, or absolutely loath it. I definitely am sided with the loving of the movie, however I believe some people are catching a different reason about why it is so enjoyable. Those who hate this movie definitely don't see the same message and definitely don't get the point. This movie is not made to be a "typical prison movie" because this one doesn't focus on those same ideas. Sure, there are similarities, but that's to be expected. As far as I know (for never having gone to prison) these depictions of prison are accurate, however, this film differs in the fact it is about HOPE. The movie isn't just about the main character trying to free himself from prison, it is about his journey through so many years of being beaten, raped, and abused, and never losing his hope. The other prisoners in this movie tell him that hope is a dangerous thing, that it can drive people crazy. He ignores the warnings and keeps his hope. The most beautiful scene in this film is when he plays the music of the opera over the loud speaker. "And just for that one moment, every last man in Shawshank felt free" are roughly the words Morgan Freeman says in his commentary. With the cinematography and the words, the feeling of hope is even implanted in the viewers themselves. I ask that those who dislike this film take it from that aspect the next time they see it, instead of an analytical viewpoint, focusing on directing style, costumes, "typical prison stuff" and other things and just let their souls take in the true meaning and feeling of hope, and what a beautiful emotion it is. I also ask that those who love it view the movie again and put yourself in a position where you felt there was no hope, that no one could help you but yourself, and let yourself become entangled in this wonderful web of hope and truly let this film be a redemption of your mind and soul.

10.title: Deserves all the credit it gets- absolutely AMAZING
10.content: Frank Darabont is a genius. In one of the most critically acclaimed, famous movies in Hollywood history, the director from France has created a work of art. Superb performances from Tim Robbins and Morgan Freeman carry the film throughout its fairly lengthy duration of 137 minutes smoothly. The film has a very slow pace, but somehow it is incredible absorbing, not boring in the slightest. The story follows Andy Dufresne, (Tim Robbins), a young banker who, despite protesting innocence, is jailed with back to back life sentences for killing his wife and her lover that she ran away with. Once at Shawshank Prison, he developes a friendship with Ellis Boyd Redding- "Red" (Morgan Freeman). Red is a man who "knows how to get things", i.e he smuggles things in from the outside world. What unfolds is not what you might expect- it's not the kind of prison film that has a gritty, explicit view of the bad things that happen in prison. Whilst this is shown to a certain extent, its not as bad as it could be and the bad sides generally come from the corrupt screws rather than the cons. This is a moral tale, as suggested by the tagline "Fear can hold you prisoner....hope can set you free". It's the kind of film that you can enjoy immensely, watch again and again, and really take a message about life away from. My favourite film, along with Pulp Fiction of the same year, I give it 10/10

10.title: A Timeless Tale of Hope and Friendship

Is an extraordinary film that remains a timeless masterpiece. Their bond explores themes of hope, resilience, and the human spirit.

Robbins' portrayal of Andy is nuanced and brilliant, while Freeman's performance as Red is compelling and memorable. The supporting cast, including Bob Gunton and Clancy Brown, adds depth and authenticity. The screenplay balances despair with triumph, enhanced by Roger Deakins' cinematography and Thomas Newman's score.

"The Shawshank Redemption" is more than a prison drama; it's a profound exploration of the human condition. Its timeless message of hope and the power of friendship continues to inspire audiences worldwide. This film is a must-watch, leaving a lasting impression and earning its place as a cherished classic.
