10.title: A Timeless Masterpiece
10.content:
"The Shawshank Redemption" is a timeless masterpiece that has rightfully earned its place among the greatest films of all time. This 1994 drama film, directed by Frank Darabont and based on a Stephen King novella, is a powerful and moving story of hope, friendship, and redemption in the most unlikely of places.

The film stars Tim Robbins as Andy Dufresne, a successful banker who is wrongfully convicted of murder and sentenced to life in Shawshank State Penitentiary. Inside the prison, he befriends Red, played brilliantly by Morgan Freeman, a longtime inmate who has learned to navigate the prison's politics and black market.

As the story unfolds, we witness the harsh realities of prison life, including violence, corruption, and institutional abuse. But at its core, "The Shawshank Redemption" is a story about the power of human connection and the resilience of the human spirit.

Robbins and Freeman deliver exceptional performances, perfectly capturing the complex emotions and motivations of their characters. The supporting cast is equally strong, with standout performances from Bob Gunton as the ruthless prison warden and William Sadler as the menacing Captain Hadley.

The film's direction is superb, with Darabont crafting a gripping narrative that seamlessly weaves together drama, suspense, and even moments of humor. The script is beautifully written, with poignant dialogue and insightful commentary on the criminal justice system and the human condition.

Overall, "The Shawshank Redemption" is a triumph of filmmaking that will resonate with viewers for generations to come. It's a story of hope and redemption that speaks to the resilience of the human spirit, and a testament to the power of cinema to inspire, entertain, and move us. Highly recommended for anyone who appreciates great cinema.

10.title: The Power of Hope: A Review of The Shawshank Redemption
10.content:
The Shawshank Redemption is a cinematic masterpiece that explores the themes of hope, friendship, and resilience against the bleak backdrop of a maximum-security prison. Directed by Frank Darabont and based on a novella by Stephen King, the film has garnered critical acclaim and remains a beloved classic.

At the heart of the story is Andy Dufresne, portrayed brilliantly by Tim Robbins. Andy's journey begins with his wrongful conviction for the murder of his wife and her lover. As he navigates the oppressive environment of Shawshank prison, the film deftly illustrates his unique way of coping with the harsh realities of his new life. Andy's character embodies intellect and perseverance, using his skills as a banker to bring hope and change to the lives of his fellow inmates.

Morgan Freeman delivers a stellar performance as Ellis "Red" Redding, the seasoned inmate who becomes Andy's closest friend. The chemistry between Robbins and Freeman is palpable, creating a bond that serves as the emotional core of the film. Red's narration adds depth and poignancy, guiding the audience through Andy's struggles and triumphs.

One of the film's greatest strengths lies in its exploration of hope amidst despair. The tagline, "Fear can hold you prisoner. Hope can set you free," encapsulates the essence of the narrative. Andy's unwavering spirit and determination to escape his circumstances resonate deeply, making his eventual triumph all the more impactful.

Visually, the film captures the oppressive atmosphere of Shawshank with its muted colors and somber settings, reflecting the characters' emotional states. The cinematography and score work in harmony to evoke a sense of longing and introspection.

The Shawshank Redemption is not just a story about imprisonment; it is a testament to the human spirit's ability to endure and thrive in the face of adversity. The film's poignant quotes, including Andy's famous line about choosing to "get busy living or get busy dying," linger long after the credits roll.

Despite its initial box office struggles, The Shawshank Redemption has risen to iconic status, frequently cited as one of the greatest films of all time. Its powerful message and unforgettable performances make it a must-see for anyone who appreciates storytelling that transcends the ordinary.

10.title: A Humble Review of the Awesome Film: A Shawshank Redemption
10.content:
Suphie W. 9/13/2012

The Shawshank Redemption Movie Review Though I haven't seen this film since the year of 2004, (it came out in 1994), I seriously remember being moved by it. I remember, quite vividly and with a pleasant vibe, how moved my friend and I genuinely felt when we first watched it together. These were in the days when Blockbuster was still around and when it was more monetarily feasible as well as logical to go out to your local movie store and rent a movie to watch with your friend; this was, with all due respect, before the current and giant economic melt-down that we are all experiencing. So, to set the scene and mood of the period in which we watched this film for the first time, the candles were lit, and my friend and I were seated eating gummy bears, and we stayed up and watched that sucker into the wee hours of the morning, cat-sitting. The economy was better, then, for sure, we all know, but, we were having a hell of a time (now my friend is away, teaching English abroad, in Korea, soon to retire there, though; she's had enough of it, as the lifestyle and the culture were just generally getting on her nerves, and she felt she had achieved what she wanted). Well, basically, the Shawshank Redemption is all about solitary confinement in a small, insulated, but high-security prison in middle-to-Southern Ohio, set in the '50s. Morgan Freeman and his white counterpart in the film (race was a factor back then), partner up to give each other moral support and courage during a very tough time for them both. The part that struck me most about this film, though, was that Tim Robbins, or, the character played by Tim Robbins, was put into solitary confinement, where food was shoved in his little cell in an unsanitary manner, and he was treated, as the proverb or saying goes, like a dog; and where he couldn't see nor hear from anyone for a long, long time; it was verifiable torture. In addition, Morgan Freeman, who plays someone who is, like Tim Robbins, on the death row, plays your average cool-cat gentleman who was convicted for the murdering of his wife or something, but who claims he didn't do it. There are many cafeteria scenes where the two bond joyously over their own jokes and jiving, and where they eventually become better friends. Basically, the two bond over their common suffering, and help each other through their sorrow. Indeed, Bob Gunton also plays in the film, a man who plays the jail-owner, or something. He appears, in real life, to be much older than either Robbins or Freeman, born in October of 1959, and 1937, respectively. Robbins notably graduated with honors from the drama program of UCLA in 1981, then went on to do other great things, such as forming the Actor's Gang Theatre Group, which expressed radical political views as seen through a European lens. In addition, Robbins has received many dramatic awards, and continues to do sporadic work in film. Freeman, of course, is the mighty train who continues to do well in whatever he does, and is well-liked by all, really. Bob Gunton has a tendency for playing strict, militaristic, authoritarian roles when it comes to his film-work, and he plays the role in the notable movie of The Shawshank Redemption. There are several intense scenes in the movie, The Shawshank Redemption, and many of them include the showing of the intense pain of both Freeman and Robbins, as they elude their grief. Robbins, in particular can't take the pain of being "locked-up" so to speak and often shouts, screams intensely out of frustration with having no one to talk to, and out of mental and emotional pain. Morgan Freeman notably cries, which is all the more pitiful as one sees his weary countenance.

10.title: The best story ever told on film.
10.content:
In its Oscar year, Shawshank Redemption (written and directed by Frank Darabont, after the novella Rita Hayworth and the Shawshank Redemption, by Stephen King) was nominated for seven Academy Awards, and walked away with zero. Best Picture went to Forrest Gump, while Shawshank and Pulp Fiction were "just happy to be nominated." Of course hindsight is 20/20, but while history looks back on Gump as a good film, Pulp and Redemption are remembered as some of the all-time best. Pulp, however, was a success from the word "go," making a huge splash at Cannes and making its writer-director an American master after only two films. For Andy Dufresne and Co., success didn't come easy. Fortunately, failure wasn't a life sentence.

After opening on 33 screens with take of $727,327, the $25M film fell fast from theatres and finished with a mere $28.3M. The reasons for failure are many. Firstly, the title is a clunker. While iconic to fans today, in 1994, people knew not and cared not what a 'Shawshank' was. On the DVD, Tim Robbins laughs recounting fans congratulating him on "that 'Rickshaw' movie." Marketing-wise, the film's a nightmare, as 'prison drama' is a tough sell to women, and the story of love between two best friends doesn't spell winner to men. Worst of all, the movie is slow as molasses. As Desson Thomson writes for the Washington Post, "it wanders down subplots at every opportunity and ignores an abundance of narrative exit points before settling on its finale." But it is these same weaknesses that make the film so strong.

Firstly, its setting. The opening aerial shots of the prison are a total eye-opener. This is an amazing piece of architecture, strong and Gothic in design. Immediately, the prison becomes a character. It casts its shadow over most of the film, its tall stone walls stretching above every shot. It towers over the men it contains, blotting out all memories of the outside world. Only Andy (Robbins) holds onto hope. It's in music, it's in the sandy beaches of Zihuatanejo; "In here's where you need it most," he says. "You need it so you don't forget. Forget that there are places in the world that aren't made out of stone. That there's a - there's a - there's something inside that's yours, that they can't touch." Red (Morgan Freeman) doesn't think much of Andy at first, picking "that tall glass o' milk with the silver spoon up his ass" as the first new fish to crack. Andy says not a word, and losing his bet, Red resents him for it. But over time, as the two get to know each other, they quickly become the best of friends. This again, is one of the film's major strengths. Many movies are about love, many flicks have a side-kick to the hero, but Shawshank is the only one I can think of that looks honestly at the love between two best friends. It seems odd that Hollywood would skip this relationship time and again, when it's a feeling that weighs so much into everyone's day to day lives. Perhaps it's too sentimental to seem conventional, but Shawshank's core friendship hits all the right notes, and the film is much better for it.

It's pacing is deliberate as well. As we spend the film watching the same actors, it is easy to forget that the movie's timeline spans well over 20 years. Such a huge measure of time would pass slowly in reality, and would only be amplified in prison. And it's not as if the film lacks interest in these moments. It still knows where it's going, it merely intends on taking its sweet time getting there. It pays off as well, as the tedium of prison life makes the climax that much more exhilarating. For anyone who sees it, it is a moment never to be forgotten.

With themes of faith and hope, there is a definite religious subtext to be found here. Quiet, selfless and carefree, Andy is an obvious Christ figure. Warden Norton (Bob Gunton) is obviously modeled on Richard Nixon, who, in his day, was as close to a personified Satan as they come. But if you aren't looking for subtexts, the movie speaks to anyone in search of hope. It is a compelling drama, and a very moving film, perfectly written, acted and shot. They just don't come much better than this.

OVERALL SCORE: 9.8/10 = A+ The Shawshank Redemption served as a message of hope to Hollywood as well. More than any film in memory, it proved there is life after box office. Besting Forrest and Fiction, it ran solely on strong word of mouth and became the hottest rented film of 1995. It currently sits at #2 in the IMDb's Top 250 Films, occasionally swapping spots with The Godfather as the top ranked film of all time -- redemption indeed. If you haven't seen it yet, what the hell are you waiting for? As Andy says, "It comes down a simple choice, really. Either get busy living, or get busy dying."

10.title: A Powerful Story of Hope and Redemption
10.content:
**The Shawshank Redemption** (1994), directed by Frank Darabont, is a deeply moving and inspirational drama adapted from Stephen King's novella *Rita Hayworth and Shawshank Redemption*. The film tells the story of Andy Dufresne (Tim Robbins), a banker wrongfully convicted of murdering his wife and her lover. Sentenced to life at Shawshank State Penitentiary, Andy befriends Ellis "Red" Redding (Morgan Freeman), a seasoned inmate, and together they endure the hardships of prison life while holding on to hope and friendship.

At its heart, *The Shawshank Redemption* is a story about resilience, the human spirit, and the belief that hope can persist even in the darkest of circumstances. Tim Robbins' portrayal of Andy is understated yet powerful, capturing a man who refuses to be broken by the brutal environment of Shawshank. Morgan Freeman's narration and performance as Red provide the film with a sense of warmth and wisdom, making their bond one of the most memorable aspects of the film.

The film's pacing is patient, allowing the relationships and emotional depth to develop naturally. Its themes of institutionalization, justice, and the power of hope resonate universally. Thomas Newman's evocative score, along with Darabont's careful direction, enhances the emotional impact of the story.

**Rating: 10/10** - *The Shawshank Redemption* is a masterful exploration of hope, friendship, and perseverance. Its timeless message, combined with outstanding performances and storytelling, makes it one of the most beloved films of all time.

"The Shawshank Redemption" is a movie about time, patience and loyalty -- not sexy qualities, perhaps, but they grow on you during the subterranean progress of this story, which is about how two men serving life sentences in prison become friends and find a way to fight off despair.

The story is narrated by "Red" Redding (Morgan Freeman), who has been inside the walls of Shawshank Prison for a very long time and is its leading entrepreneur. He can get you whatever you need: cigarettes, candy, even a little rock pick like an amateur geologist might use. One day he and his fellow inmates watch the latest busload of prisoners unload, and they make bets on who will cry during their first night in prison, and who will not. 10.title: My 12 year old daughter raved about this film

I just saw this movie for the first time. My daughter watched it first when she was 12 when it first came out. She went on and on about it saying how great it was then in about 1995. She also loved "Trading Places". I guess the moral of both of these stories is that the good guys win in the end. I now know what she was talking about. It is a great movie, and I can see why it appeals to women.

The movie is set in a prison, with the time old tradition of a close friendship over many years of an innocent young man as the hero and an "old lag" who knows all the ropes, in this case Tim Robbins and Morgan Freeman. This is the same formula earlier used in the films "The Count of Monte Cristo" and "An Innocent Man", both films which are highly recommended, if you liked this one.

The film, although made in 1994, goes back to a time when good wins out over evil. unfortunately the fashion for a long time in the nineties movies was for bad to win out, as in "the Terminator" and other movies. The bad guys are as usual the prison boss, The Warder and his Second in Command, the Uniformed Chief Officer. There is a highly unusual twist at the end of the movie, in which the good guys win out. This is a highly improbable situation, but fantasy is allowable in movies. One character of note is that of an old man, played by James Whitmore, who rescues a tiny bird, and nurtures it for years. Thank goodness it doesn't get killed by some other evil person, as usually happens. The old man has to cope with pressures in the outside after he is released.

The overarching theme of the movie is one of hope. No matter how bad things get, there is always hope that thing will get better. It also shows that it is possible to have a friendship between black and white people, as the older man, the main character's friend, is a black man. The thing that this movie gave me, is that I can see how wise my daughter already was at 12 years of age, and more importantly, it gives hope and a good philosophy for the rest of my life. I'm sure that it will do the same for those of you who see this movie too.

I am unsure as to whether it deserves to be rated the best movie of all time. However movies with hope and goodness as their main themes are generally up there, take "Gone With the Wind", "Schindler's List" and "Lord of the Rings" as examples of this.

But Andy does not crack: he has the hope of the truly innocent, which (together with his smarts) allow him to prevail behind bars. He uses his banking skills to win favor with the warden and the guards, doing the books for Norton's illegal business schemes and keeping an eye on the investments of most of the prison staff. In exchange, he is able to improve the prison library and bring some dignity and respect back to many of the inmates, including Red. Based on a story by Stephen King, The Shawshank Redemption was the directorial debut of screenwriter Frank Darabont.~ Mark Deming,

10.title: Title: The Shawshank Redemption (1994) - A Timeless Tale of Hope and Redemption
10.content:
"The Shawshank Redemption" stands tall as a cinematic gem, a powerful and emotionally gripping masterpiece that leaves an indelible mark on the hearts of its viewers. Directed by Frank Darabont, this adaptation of Stephen King's novella is a triumph of storytelling, featuring brilliant performances, a poignant narrative, and a profound exploration of the human spirit.

Set within the confines of Shawshank State Penitentiary, the film introduces us to Andy Dufresne, portrayed with remarkable depth by Tim Robbins. Wrongfully convicted of murder, Andy embarks on an arduous journey through the prison system, enduring its hardships while clinging to an unwavering sense of hope. Robbins effortlessly portrays Andy's quiet resilience, making him an unforgettable protagonist whose unwavering spirit captivates audiences from the very beginning.

Morgan Freeman delivers a career-defining performance as Red, a seasoned inmate and narrator of the story. Freeman's soothing voice and wise portrayal add a layer of richness to the film, serving as the perfect counterpoint to Andy's unwavering optimism. The bond that forms between Andy and Red is the heart and soul of the film, embodying the true essence of friendship and the strength it provides in the darkest of times.

At its core, "The Shawshank Redemption" is a story of hope and the indomitable human spirit. Through its vivid characters and thought-provoking dialogues, the film delves into themes of perseverance, friendship, and the quest for redemption. It reminds us that even in the most desolate circumstances, hope can be a powerful force that propels individuals toward transformation and renewal.

The film's cinematography paints a hauntingly beautiful portrait of life behind bars. The use of shadows and contrasts adds an atmospheric depth to the prison setting, mirroring the characters' emotional turmoil and yearning for freedom. Every shot is a visual delight, allowing viewers to immerse themselves fully in the world of Shawshank.

The screenplay, penned by Darabont himself, exhibits a perfect balance of humor and heartache, culminating in a story that leaves no emotional stone unturned. Each character, no matter how small their role, serves a purpose in the larger narrative, contributing to the film's emotional resonance and making it a truly unforgettable experience.

Accompanied by an evocative score composed by Thomas Newman, the film's music elevates every scene, evoking a range of emotions that stay with the audience long after the credits roll. The combination of captivating storytelling and a haunting musical score forms a harmonious blend that weaves its way into the hearts of its viewers.

"The Shawshank Redemption" is a timeless classic that transcends generations, reminding us of the power of hope, friendship, and the human capacity for redemption. It remains an enduring testament to the strength of the human spirit, leaving an eternal impression that will continue to inspire and touch lives for years to come. A cinematic triumph that should not be missed, this film stands as a shining example of the transformative power of cinema.

10.title: In the lead roles, both Robbins and Freeman are outstanding.
10.content:
On Sept. 23, 1994, after a premiere at the Toronto film fest, The Shawshank Redemption hit theaters nationwide. The Morgan Freeman film eventually nabbed seven Oscar nominations. The Hollywood Reporter's original review is below: Castle Rock has tapped into the wellspring of yet another Stephen King novella, from the same collection as Stand by Me. While it seems unlikely that this well-wrought film about hope and friendship in a maximum security prison will do Stand by Me-level business, The Shawshank Redemption should appeal to a mature audience. The marketing challenge will be to lure a mainstream audience to this dark drama starring Tim Robbins and Morgan Freeman with, to boot, an enigmatic title.

Covering a span of time from 1946 to 1967, Shawshank focuses on the plight of a Maine banker, Andy Dufresne (Robbins), sentenced to two life terms for the murder of his wife and lover. Laconic and a bit chilly, Andy is somewhat of an outcast among the uneducated, macho thugs who make up the main brunt of the prison population.

Admittedly, he's not an easy guy to get to know and only comes to enjoy a prison friendship when he makes a deal with the prison black-market supplier, Red (Freeman), to get him a tiny hammer for his rock collection. Red is also an enigma to most of the inmates. He keeps his nose clean and his hopes up even though the parole board routinely denies him pardon, obviously a racial antagonism.

While the story roils with some rousing prison-type action and is coarsened by an overpowering sense of frustration, The Shawshank Redemption is really about the unlikely friendship between Andy and Red: Each nurtures the other and serves as a touchstone for keeping their sanity intact.

Frank Darabont's writing and direction are generally crisp, but Shawshank is a tough watch and audiences could use some time cut from its 142 minutes.

In the lead roles, both Robbins and Freeman are outstanding, layering their performances with snippets of individuality: Their small, daily sustenance's and minor triumphs are wonderfully inspiring.

Technical contributions are well-crafted, particularly cinematographer Roger Deakins' forbidding lensing. Filmed in a garrison-like former prison in Mansfield, Ohio, Shawshank is often overwhelming in its depiction of the granite-cold, stony horror of prison life. Most splendid is Thomas Newman's somber score, which, at its best moments, alights with radiant textures and sprightly grace notes, nicely emblematic of the film's central theme.

10.title: The Shawshank Redemption: A Timeless Masterpiece of Hope and the Human Spirit
10.content:
The Shawshank Redemption is a film that transcends the boundaries of cinema and becomes an emotional experience about the enduring power of hope. It's not just a movie; it's a life lesson, delicately interwoven into a narrative of friendship, perseverance, and belief in something better.

From the moment we meet Andy Dufresne, played flawlessly by Tim Robbins, we are taken on a journey of a man wrongfully imprisoned, navigating the brutal realities of Shawshank State Penitentiary. Yet, through all the cruelty, injustice, and despair, Andy never surrenders his spirit. What makes The Shawshank Redemption truly unforgettable is its unwavering focus on hope-an almost spiritual belief that, even in the darkest of places, the light can find a way.

Morgan Freeman's portrayal of Red, a man who has long abandoned the idea of hope, acts as a counterbalance to Andy's quiet optimism. Their friendship is the beating heart of the film, and through Andy's relentless determination, Red begins to rediscover what hope can mean. As Red puts it, "Hope is a dangerous thing," yet by the end of the movie, we learn that hope is also the most powerful thing a person can hold onto.

Director Frank Darabont crafts a story that isn't just about breaking out of prison, but breaking free from the mental chains that hold people down. The pacing, the dialogue, the breathtaking score by Thomas Newman-everything builds towards a crescendo that reminds us that hope is not just something to cling to; it's something to fight for.

The final scenes are nothing short of cathartic, leaving you with a sense of awe and reflection on the strength of the human spirit. If ever there was a film that illustrates the power of hope to heal, to transform, and to liberate, The Shawshank Redemption is it.

Simply put, this film is a masterpiece-10/10. A story that reminds us to "get busy living or get busy dying," but above all, to never stop hoping.

10.title: Master Piece
10.content:
The Shawshank Redemption (1994), directed by Frank Darabont, is widely regarded as one of the finest films in cinematic history. Based on Stephen King's novella Rita Hayworth and Shawshank Redemption, the movie tells the powerful story of Andy Dufresne (Tim Robbins), a banker wrongfully imprisoned for the murder of his wife and her lover. Over the course of two decades in Shawshank Prison, Andy forms an unlikely friendship with Ellis "Red" Redding (Morgan Freeman), a fellow inmate and the film's narrator.

The film is not just a prison drama but a profound exploration of hope, freedom, and redemption. The performances are stellar, particularly Freeman's portrayal of Red, whose wisdom and world-weariness serve as a perfect counterbalance to Andy's quiet resilience. Robbins' subtle and deeply emotional performance as Andy makes his character's journey even more poignant.

Visually, the movie captures both the grim monotony of prison life and the fleeting moments of beauty that break through. The pacing is methodical, allowing the characters and their relationships to develop in a way that feels organic and real. The screenplay is emotionally rich, balancing moments of despair with undercurrents of hope that culminate in one of the most satisfying endings in cinema.

The Shawshank Redemption is a timeless film about the resilience of the human spirit, a meditation on the possibility of hope even in the bleakest circumstances. Its messages of friendship, perseverance, and finding meaning in life continue to resonate, making it a classic that stands the test of time.

Why do I want to write The Shawshank Redemption's 234th comment? I'm not certain because about everything that could have been said about it has been said. To Kill a Mockingbird is the only other movie I've ever seen that has such a profound impact on me. Having seen both films, I feel better for having done so.

I had no intention of seeing this movie because I typically avoid them and don't like them. Just two men conversing while wearing jail garb-no action, no special effects.

My two favorite films are To Kill a Mockingbird and The Shawshank Redemption. I'm not going to judge it on its technical merits since I don't really care. I've read that The Godfather, Citizen Kane, this movie, or that movie is the best motion picture ever made. They might employ the most advanced techniques or be the most significant films ever produced, but they are not the best. The best movies are the ones that move you emotionally. To touch the soul, a film like The Shawshank Redemption is necessary.

10.title: Flat out one of the most jaw-droppingly amazing movies ever made.
10.content:
Starring: Tim Robbins, Morgan Freeman There are some movies that when you watch them you can't help but feel you've done more than watch a movie. Sometimes it feels like you've been part of something bigger, like you witnessed a masterpiece. The Shawshank Redemption is like watching poetry. It is one of the most tragic, heartfelt, and deeply satisfying stories to have ever been put onto the big screen. There really is a reason that this movie is number two on the internet movie database's top movies of all time.

The premise of the movie is fairly simple. Andy Dufraine (Robbins) is wrongfully accused with the murder of his wife and her lover, and he is sentenced to two life sentences to be served back to back at Shawshank prison. The plot is simple, and yet at the same time deeply complex. This movie is a celebration of the human spirit, a celebration of hope and of freedom.

Life is difficult for Andy right from the beginning of his life sentence. It takes him at least a month before he goes and talks to anyone. The first person he does talk to is Red (Freeman), a man in the prison who is able to get things. Need to get a pack of cigarettes, a toothbrush, maybe some playing cards, then Red is your man on the inside. Andy asks Red to pick up a rock hammer so that he can carve stones.

This movie is anything but a fairy tale. It depicts prison life as being cruel, unfair, bitter, and downright horrible. Decent people die, people get gang raped, the guards beat the ever-loving daylights out of anyone who steps out of line. Shawshank prison is one hard place to serve your time.

After being in prison for a couple years, Andy gets transferred from laundry duty to library, mainly so the warden can send his men over to get financial advice from Andy. Andy starts doing income tax for the guards and the warden, setting up trust funds, and various other financial services, and after a few years, he becomes the man who launders the warden's dirty money. Sure, he got transferred to the library, but the only difference is he's washing money and not sheets and clothes.

Andy takes up all sorts of projects while he's in Shawshank. He makes chess pieces for a chess board, he makes it his personal task to obtain funds for and build a new prison library. He helps several of the inmates get their high school equivalence. He does whatever he can to pass the time and keep himself a little bit sane.

I'd hate to spoil the ending for anybody who hasn't seen this movie, so I will be very vague. All I will say is that it is one of the most satisfying and beautiful endings to any movie or story that has ever been captured. This movie is a masterpiece, and you would do yourself a favour to make sure you watch it. And if you've already seen it, watch it again, and introduce somebody else to the world of Shawshank prison.

Bottom Line: 4 out of 4 (own this movie)

10.title: Stories benefit from characterization
10.content: In Shawshank's world, black and white often have to be seen upside down. In addition to telling about the power of hope, the film also reflects the goodness and ugliness of human nature, just as we can't simply describe a person with good and bad, and many times, we can't judge whether a person is really the same. This film is not only Andy's self salvation, but also tells the world that all salvation comes from the choice of the heart, whether to yearn for the light or fall into the dark, lies in your heart. The absolute protagonist is a banker, family, career, wealth, fame and seemingly perfect life before he goes to prison. However, he was tragically interrupted and sentenced to life imprisonment because of being accused of murdering his wife and his lover. Since then, Andy's life has been gloomy. I always remember that scene: on the first night Andy and other new prisoners arrived at Shawshank, the old prisoners began to bet on who would cry and who would not. At first, I was a little surprised, because I thought it was common for a criminal to go to prison as a vicious criminal, and someone would cry? To cry, it can only happen to Andy, who had a promising future but was destroyed by misjudgment. However, it's not that Andy is the only one who doesn't cry. He was just silent in the dark. Red, Andy's good friend, said that all the new inmates would cry the first night, and Andy obviously refreshed all the old inmates' ideas. After all, Andy's wisdom, Andy's actions, Andy's bravery, and in order to leave Shawshank, he spent time and patience, are admirable and regrettable. Praise him for being able to regain his confidence quickly after falling from the cloud to hell; praise him for not hesitating to fight in the face of vicious same-sex prisoners who want to invade him; praise him for not forgetting to rely on his knowledge to help all the people who can help as much as possible when planning to escape, even if only to pass the long prison life, he has also achieved the goal that most people can reach Life. It's a pity that Andy's best years ended up in a joke of fate. His favorite disciple also died. When he climbed out of the filthy drainage channel as long as five football fields, when he took away the huge "compensation" he deserved, and when he finally recovered from freedom, how could the past 19 years' innocent disaster be liquidated? After all, no one can get rid of fate's teasing. Andy realized his plan by hope, but not everyone has such perseverance, such wisdom, and meet reliable friends, red. Andy's misfortune lies in God's injustice, Andy's luck lies in his never giving up hope, hope is a good thing.

10.title: Proof that box office takings aren't everything.
10.content: When I heard that this movie bombed at the box office during its theatrical run, I was very surprised as this is simply an all time classic. Rarely is narration in a movie been done as well as this, Morgan Freeman simply becomes Ellis Redding whose depiction of a hardened con who has accepted that he may never get out and goes through his parole hearings not caring about the outcome. Tim Robbins becomes Andy Dufresne and his portrayal of a man who is really out of his depth and his element, and finding adjusting to life on the inside difficult, almost impossible. The changing relationship between the two characters from initial hostility to deep almost brother like friendship is captivating. Clancy Brown's depiction of the tyrannical Captain Baron Hadley is amazing and likewise Bob Gunton as the hypocritical bible bashing, Warden Norton. The other characters like wise are also well done, especially Brooks and sadistic inmate Boggs. The depiction is what you'd expect from a prison movie and while depicting a life of boring monotony and routine show occasionally punctuated by brief moments of excitement is still fascinating thanks to the soundtrack and of course Morgan Freeman's narration, and I don't want to spoil the ending but it climaxes perfectly with not a dry eye in sight, thanks to the pacing, and the dialogue can't be faulted. Now in regard to the differences from the book, these are for the most part minor and if anything enhance the story rather than hinder it, a rarity. In summary this is a must watch for all movie lovers.

10.title: General information

"The Shawshank Redemption" is a critically acclaimed film released in 1994, directed by Frank Darabont and based on Stephen King's novella of the same name. It is widely regarded as one of the greatest films of all time and has garnered a large and dedicated fanbase over the years.

The movie tells the story of Andy Dufresne, a banker who is wrongfully convicted of murdering his wife and her lover. He is sentenced to life imprisonment at Shawshank State Penitentiary, where he faces the harsh realities of prison life. The film primarily focuses on Andy's experiences and his unlikely friendship with another inmate, Ellis "Red" Redding.

What sets "The Shawshank Redemption" apart from other prison dramas is its emphasis on hope, friendship, and the indomitable spirit of the human soul. The movie explores themes of perseverance, the power of the human spirit, and the quest for redemption. It beautifully captures the complexities of the prison system and the personal struggles faced by the inmates.

The performances in the film are outstanding. Tim Robbins delivers a nuanced and compelling portrayal of Andy Dufresne, capturing his quiet strength and determination. Morgan Freeman's portrayal of Red is equally impressive, bringing depth and warmth to the character. The chemistry between Robbins and Freeman is a highlight of the film, and their friendship forms the emotional core of the story.

The screenplay, written by Frank Darabont, is superbly crafted. It skillfully balances moments of heart-wrenching drama with moments of humor, creating a captivating narrative that keeps viewers engaged throughout. The film's pacing is excellent, allowing the story to unfold at a steady and satisfying pace.

Visually, the film is well executed, with atmospheric cinematography that captures the bleakness of prison life and the beauty of freedom. The production design and costumes effectively recreate the period setting, immersing the audience in the world of Shawshank.

"The Shawshank Redemption" is a thought-provoking and emotionally resonant film that leaves a lasting impact on its viewers. It explores universal themes of hope, friendship, and the capacity for redemption, making it a timeless classic. The movie's enduring popularity is a testament to its quality and the profound effect it has on audiences. Whether you're a fan of dramas, prison stories, or simply great storytelling, "The Shawshank Redemption" is a film that should not be missed.

10.title: The Shawshank Redemption: A Poignant Tale of Hope and Friendship
10.content:
The Shawshank Redemption is a timeless classic that has captured the hearts of audiences for over two decades. Directed by Frank Darabont and based on a short story by Stephen King, the film is a poignant tale of hope and friendship that has stood the test of time.

The film follows the story of Andy Dufresne, a banker who is wrongly convicted of murdering his wife and her lover. He is sent to Shawshank State Penitentiary, where he befriends Red, a long-time inmate played by Morgan Freeman. Over the course of their time in prison, the two men form a deep bond, and Andy's unwavering spirit and determination to maintain his dignity and humanity in the face of degradation and injustice serve as a beacon of hope for Red and the other inmates.

One of the most striking aspects of the film is its exploration of the theme of hope. Despite the bleak and oppressive environment of the prison, Andy never loses sight of his belief in the possibility of redemption and a better life. His unwavering hope serves as a source of inspiration for the other inmates, who are also struggling to cope with the harsh realities of prison life.

Another compelling theme of the film is the power of friendship. The friendship between Andy and Red is the heart of the film, and it is a testament to the human spirit's ability to find connection and meaning in even the most unlikely of circumstances. Through their friendship, the two men find a sense of purpose and belonging, and they learn to rely on each other for support and companionship.

The film's visual style is also noteworthy. The stark and oppressive atmosphere of the prison is captured in vivid detail, creating a sense of claustrophobia and hopelessness that is both palpable and suffocating. The contrast between the bleakness of the prison and the beauty of the natural world, which is glimpsed through Andy's letters from Mexico, serves as a poignant reminder of the power of hope and the human spirit's ability to endure even the most difficult of circumstances.

The film's exceptional cast is also a highlight. Tim Robbins delivers a powerful and nuanced performance as Andy, conveying the character's intelligence, resilience, and determination with subtlety and grace. Morgan Freeman's portrayal of Red is equally impressive, as he brings depth and complexity to a character who could have easily been reduced to a stereotype.

The film's message of the power of hope and the resilience of the human spirit is a timeless reminder that even in the face of seemingly insurmountable obstacles, we can find the strength to persevere and triumph. The film's themes of friendship, redemption, and the human spirit's ability to endure are as relevant today as they were when the film was first released.

In conclusion, The Shawshank Redemption is a powerful and poignant film that explores themes of hope, friendship, and redemption. The exceptional performances, stunning visual style, and timeless message make it a must-see for anyone who appreciates a good story. The film's unforgettable characters and unforgettable story have left a lasting impact on audiences, and it remains a timeless classic that will continue to inspire and move viewers for generations to come.

They'll just have to satisfy themselves with the equally prestigious recognition of being voted the best film of all time by LADbible readers.

As for the other films in the running, they were chosen because of their high-rating on film encyclopedia website IMDb.

Currently, Christopher Nolan's second Batman film holds a rating of 9.0 on the website, as does The Godfather Part II.

The Godfather starring Marlon Brando, Al Pacino, and James Caan - among others - has a rating of 9.1, whereas The Shawshank Redemption rates at 9.2.

10.title: An innocent banker is sentenced to life in a state prison for the murder of his wife and her lover; he is abused by other inmates until he is befriended by a cynical lifer.
10.content: A "life-affirming" tale about life imprisonment, THE SHAWSHANK REDEMPTION is the kind of old-fashioned entertainment that is easily overvalued in an era of diminishing expectations. This reverent adaptation of an unremarkable 1982 Stephen King novella was received tepidly at the box office--due in part to advertising that offered no clue as to what the movie was about--but gained a remarkably enthusiastic following and surprised many by netting seven Oscar nominations. In mid-1940s Maine, banker Andy Dufresne (Tim Robbins) is tried and convicted for the murder of his wife and her lover. He is sentenced to life at Shawshank prison, where he meets affable lifer Ellis Boyd "Red" Redding (Morgan Freeman), whose applications for parole are turned down on an annual basis. Known as one who can get things--for a price--Red secures for Andy a pinup of Rita Hayworth and a rock hammer to pursue his geological hobbies. Both items turn out to be crucial parts of a scheme that the mild-mannered banker nurses through years of painstaking preparation. Whereas some Stephen King adapters have seemed intent on transcending or trashing their source material, writer-director Frank Darabont succeeds through fidelity to the text; the few deviations make this subdued male love story even more audience-friendly. The film benefits greatly from elegant cinematography by Roger Deakins and a poignant score by Thomas Newman. Freeman creates an endearing portrait of a decent man with a dark deed in his past, and Tim Robbins gives what may be his most accomplished portrayal. The excellent supporting cast includes James Whitmore, cute as the dickens as old-timer Brooks Hatlen, and William Sadler as a con who starts out scary and ends up lovable. Which brings us to the film's greatest limitation: prison hasn't looked this inviting since 1940s Hollywood. Nothing seems to build character like a long stint at Shawshank, which on the whole seems not much worse than a downmarket summer camp. This makes for a crowd-pleasing story that has little to do with the messy complexities of reality.

Deciding on the best movie of all time requires a balance between objectivity and subjective preference, which can be different for industry professionals and general audiences. 10.title: Cinematic Excellence in Story and Craft
10.content:
"The Shawshank Redemption" is a cinematic triumph that masterfully blends exceptional filmmaking techniques with a profound narrative. Directed by Frank Darabont, the film employs meticulous cinematography to enhance the emotional depth of the story. The use of lighting and shadows creates a stark contrast between hope and despair, mirroring the internal struggles of the characters. Close-up shots capture the nuanced performances of the actors, particularly Tim Robbins and Morgan Freeman, allowing audiences to connect deeply with their journeys. Wide-angle shots of the prison compound emphasize the isolation and confinement experienced by the inmates.

An intriguing aspect of the film is the near absence of female characters. Only one woman appears in the story, and her presence is solely through her voice. This occurs during the iconic scene where Andy Dufresne plays a recording of "The Marriage of Figaro" over the prison's loudspeakers. The ethereal voice captivates all the male inmates, momentarily transporting them beyond the prison walls. This singular female voice symbolizes hope, freedom, and the beauty of the outside world, serving as a poignant contrast to the harsh realities of prison life.

The screenplay is another standout element, showcasing brilliant writing that weaves themes of friendship, redemption, and resilience. The dialogue is sharp and meaningful, driving the narrative forward while providing deep insights into the characters' psyche. Adapted from Stephen King's novella, the script successfully translates the source material's emotional weight to the screen. The pacing is deliberate, allowing the story to unfold naturally and giving viewers time to form a strong emotional connection with the characters.

In conclusion, "The Shawshank Redemption" excels on multiple fronts-its innovative cinematography, the subtle yet powerful inclusion of a single female voice, and its outstanding screenplay. These elements come together to create a film that is both emotionally resonant and visually compelling. It remains a timeless classic that continues to inspire and move audiences, reminding us of the enduring power of hope and human spirit.

10.title: Shawshank's Genius Makes Harsh Critics Look Stupid
10.content: Even though the number of fantastic reviews overpowers the bad reviews I would like to challenge the bad. These "critics" call this movie boring, stereotypical, and not believable. Their ratings, 1 out of 10, are based on an overreaction in order to draw attention to themselves. These ratings don't have merit and quite frankly are immature. For starters, this movie is based around a theme that's both controversial and important. The premise of falsely convicting someone to life in prison or capital punishment is as real and as touchy of a subject that you can get. It has been a major problem in society since the beginning of law and occurs more frequently then anyone would like to admit or even think about. So already we have a movie that is thought-provoking, relevant, and powerful. Then you get Tim Robbins and Morgan Freeman, in their prime, give career and industry altering performances. Then the movie goes above and beyond ALL others when the universal themes of fear, friendship, and hope are exquisitely baked into the plot. Unlike most movies, the final outcome isn't always apparent and is definitely not given up easily. The movie is purposely stretched out in order to create an emotional connection. Shawshank understands that whenever something is quickly and easily given up it won't be very thought provoking. Additionally, Shawshank understands it is a fictional story and that key embellishments are vital to any influential story. Therefore, this movie allows the viewer to get emotionally committed so that you walk away feeling affected.

10.title: . The Shawshank Redemption
10.content:
The Shawshank Redemption is1994 American prison drama film . Adapted and directed by Frank Darabont , the film is based on Stephen King 's 1982 novel Rita Hayworth and Shawshank Redemption . The film tells the story of Andy Dufresne, a banker who is sentenced to life in prison at Shawshank State Prison for allegedly murdering his wife and her lover, even though he maintains his innocence. During his more than two decades in prison, he develops a friendship with another inmate, "Red" Redding , and becomes involved in a money laundering scheme run by the prison warden , Samuel Norton . The film also features William Sadler , Clancy Brown , Gil Bellows , and James Whitmore in supporting roles.

Frank Darabont acquired the rights to adapt King's story in 1987. However, he only began development five years later, completing the script in eight weeks. Just two weeks after submitting the script to Castle Rock Entertainment , Darabont secured $25 million in production funding. Pre-production on the film began in January 1993. Although the story is set in Maine , most of the shooting took place in Mansfield, Ohio , from June to August 1993, using the Ohio State Reformatory as the main prison location. Several well-known actors, including Tom Hanks , Tom Cruise , and Kevin Costner , were attracted to the role of Andy. The film's music was composed by Thomas Newman .

10.title: I hope you enjoy your time at Shawshank.
10.content:
I'm not going to tell you anything you probably don't already know. Shawshank Redemption is one of the most critically acclaimed movies of all time - for a reason. It all comes together.

First off, the story is a tried and true classic, an innocent man accused and wrongly convicted, sentenced to spend the rest of his life in a place he doesn't belong, amongst men who make it all the worse for him because they do belong there. Without hope of release, he overcomes the depression and hopelessness he finds himself in, and decides to seek and find new meaning. Then, in the pursuit of this new revelation, he sees hope again.

The details in the writing are outstanding. Stephen King and Frank Darabont have brought the characters to life in their attention to the particular attributes of each of them. Some of the writing reminds me of the way a talented mystery writer formulates a story, allowing for the details to be picked up on by the reader (watcher in this case) if one is looking for them or paying close enough attention.

The acting is at the level that should be used for teaching. If you're trying to get into acting, these are actors you can learn something from. Morgan Freeman is well known as an amazing actor, and both before and after this role, he has done impressive work. Tim Robbins is fantastic in this role, and I personally feel he's underutilized in film today. Some of the other roles he's had haven't really made use of his acting chops the way Shawshank did. There are several other actors in the film who do absolutely outstanding work; Bob Gunton, William Sadler, and Clancy Brown rise to the top of my list.

The cinematography is great. They do a remarkable job of making you feel the prison environment, enclosed and cramped all the time, except when it fits to do something else.

The score really comes in as another character. Each piece is perfectly fit to each scene. I'm imagining seeing the movie without the music and it would still be worthwhile, but it would feel like there's something missing.

I've done my best to leave out spoilers because I've been trying to write this for someone who has never seen it. If you haven't, I highly recommend it. It tells an amazing story of the human spirit and the struggle to survive against overwhelming odds, including the reality of what can happen on both sides of the struggle.

10.title: Freeman
10.content: The Shawshank Redemption is about a Wrongly convicted, Andy Dufresne (Tim Robbins) who is sentenced to two consecutive life terms in in Maine's Shawshank prison for the murders of his wife and her lover. Set in the 1940's, the film shows how Andy learns to get by in the brutal confines of prison, even earning the respect of his fellow inmates, most notably the long time convict "Red" Redding (Morgan Freeman). While being an R rated film I didn't feel like it was an R rated film. I mean there were some scenes, other than that it could've been rated a PG-13, but it's not up to me. The Drama/Crime film was surprising on first view but in the best world, I literally watched it straight after I watched for the first time, although it does have a running time of 142 minutes. It was well worth it. I now know some of the most iconic scenes ever in film history, I knew them before but I never understood until I watched it for the first time. I think one of the most touching and in terms of the film itself, one of the biggest scenes was the death of Brookes. I wasn't able to handle it, you know that feeling you get when you're watching a film and you can kind of guess what's about to happen but you don't want it to happen, so you're sat there like no, no, no, no, no, you know? In the film it becomes clear that the prison is corrupt with inside deals and businesses going on, it is also revealed to the audience that the prison does not follow the prison standards of the state and that it does what it wants. Such as, when on the first night Andy is in his cell and all of the other prisoners tell him and are talking about who there is always one who cracks first, it turns out to be a guy only a few cells away from Andy, we then see how the guards deal with the situation in a sarcastic manner and how they blatantly don't care at all, as they proceed to actually club the guy to death. It is deeper than most films; about continuity in a lifetime, based on friendship and hope. Interesting that although the hero of the film is the convicted former banker Andy Dufresne (Tim Robbins), the action is never seen from his point of view. The film's opening scene shows him being given two life sentences for the murder of his wife and her lover, and then we move, permanently, to a point of view representing the prison population and particularly the lifer Ellis 'Red' Redding (Morgan Freeman). It is his voice remembering the first time he saw Andy ("looked like a stiff breeze would blow him over"), and predicting, wrongly, that he wouldn't make it in prison. . We've been shown by Andy's example that you have to keep true to yourself, not lose hope, bide your time, set a quiet example and look for your chance. "I guess it comes down to a simple choice, really," he tells Red. "Get busy livin' or get busy dyin'." The key to the film's structure, I think, is that it's not about its hero, but about our relationship with him - our curiosity, our pity, our admiration. If Andy had been the heroic center, bravely enduring, the film would have been conventional, and less mysterious. But we wonder about this guy. Did he really kill those two people? Why does he keep so much to himself? Why can he amble through the prison yard like a free man on a stroll, when everyone else plods or sidles? The movie avoids lingering on Andy's suffering; after beatings, he's seen in medium and long shot, tactfully. The camera doesn't focus on Andy's wounds or bruises, but, like his fellow prisoners, gives him his space. There's an underlying problem. Behind bars, Red is king. He's the prison fixer, able to get you a pack of cigarettes, a little rock pick or a Rita Hayworth poster. On the outside, he has no status or identity. We've already seen what happened to the old librarian (James Whitmore), lonely and adrift in freedom. The last act, in which Andy helps Red accept his freedom, is deeply moving - all the more so because Andy again operates at a distance, with letters and postcards, and is seen through Red's mind. Roger Deakins' cinematography is tactful, not showy. Two opening shots, one from a helicopter, one of prison walls looming overhead, establish the prison. Shots follow the dialogue instead of anticipating it. If you have not seen this film, WHAT ARE YOU DOING?!?!?!?!!? Follow me on Instagram @gabewatling and Twitter @gmwatling

10.title: "The Shawshank Redemption: A Timeless Tale of Hope and Resilience"
10.content:
"The Shawshank Redemption," directed by Frank Darabont and released in 1994, is widely regarded as one of the greatest films of all time. Adapted from Stephen King's novella "Rita Hayworth and Shawshank Redemption," the movie tells the story of Andy Dufresne (played by Tim Robbins), a banker who is sentenced to life in Shawshank State Penitentiary for the murder of his wife and her lover, despite his claims of innocence.

The film explores themes of hope, friendship, and resilience. Andy befriends Ellis "Red" Redding (played by Morgan Freeman), a fellow inmate and the film's narrator. Through their deepening friendship, the film delves into the harsh realities of prison life, while also highlighting the enduring human spirit. Andy's intelligence, determination, and unwavering hope eventually lead to his daring and meticulously planned escape, which stands as one of cinema's most iconic moments.

The movie's success lies in its powerful storytelling, strong performances, and evocative score by Thomas Newman. Tim Robbins delivers a subtle yet profound performance as Andy, while Morgan Freeman's portrayal of Red, with his rich, soothing voice, adds a layer of warmth and wisdom to the narrative.

Although it was not a major box office hit upon its initial release, "The Shawshank Redemption" has gained immense popularity over the years, becoming a beloved classic. It has received numerous accolades, including seven Academy Award nominations, and consistently ranks high on various lists of top films, such as IMDb's Top 250.

Overall, "The Shawshank Redemption" is a deeply moving and inspirational film that resonates with audiences through its message of hope and the enduring power of the human spirit.

10.title: In the pantheon of cinema, "The Shawshank Redemption" stands as a beacon of storytelling excellence.
10.content:
The Shawshank Redemption" stands as an extraordinary cinematic achievement that transcends the boundaries of time and genre. Released in 1994 and directed by Frank Darabont, this film is a testament to the transformative power of storytelling and the indomitable human spirit.

At its core, "The Shawshank Redemption" is a tale of hope, resilience, and the enduring pursuit of freedom. Tim Robbins delivers a stellar performance as Andy Dufresne, a banker unjustly sentenced to life imprisonment at Shawshank State Penitentiary. The narrative, adapted from a Stephen King novella, unfolds through the eyes of fellow inmate Red, portrayed with exceptional depth by Morgan Freeman. Their on-screen chemistry is nothing short of magical, creating a poignant and lasting impact on the audience.

What sets this film apart is its ability to seamlessly blend elements of drama, friendship, and redemption. The script is a masterpiece, skillfully weaving a narrative that is both heart-wrenching and uplifting. The deliberate pacing allows for the organic development of characters, making their stories all the more compelling and emotionally resonant.

The cinematography, led by the talented Roger Deakins, captures the stark contrasts of prison life and the fleeting moments of beauty within its confines. Each frame is a visual feast, contributing to the overall atmosphere of the film. Thomas Newman's hauntingly beautiful score further enhances the emotional depth, eliciting a range of feelings from the audience.

"The Shawshank Redemption" is a rare gem that explores the complexities of the human condition. It delves into the depths of despair and emerges with a message of enduring hope. The film's iconic scenes, such as Andy's escape through the sewage pipe or the triumphant moment in the rain, have become ingrained in the collective consciousness of film enthusiasts.

Beyond its technical brilliance, the film resonates because of its universal themes. It speaks to the resilience of the human spirit in the face of adversity and the transformative power of friendship. The characters are not merely inmates but symbols of the enduring capacity for change and redemption.

In the pantheon of cinema, "The Shawshank Redemption" stands as a beacon of storytelling excellence. Its impact is timeless, and its brilliance is undiminished by the passage of years. For those who have experienced its magic, it remains not just a film but an emotional journey that lingers in the heart and mind-a true testament to the enduring power of exceptional storytelling in the world of cinema.

I believe that this film is the best story ever told on film, and I'm about to tell you why.

Tim Robbins plays Andy Dufresne, a city banker, wrongfully convicted of murdering his wife and her lover. He is sent to Shawshank Prison in 1947 and receives a double life sentence for the crime. Andy forms an unlikely friendship with "Red" (Morgan Freeman), the man who knows how to get things. Andy faces many trials in prison, but forms an alliance with the wardens because he is able to use his banking experience to help the corrupt officials amass personal fortunes. The story unfolds....

I was so impressed with how every single subplot was given a great deal of respect and attention from the director. The acting was world- class. I have never seen Tim Robbins act as well since, Morgan Freeman maybe (e.g. Seven). The twists were unexpected, an although this film had a familiar feel, it wasn't even slightly pretentious or clichéd, it was original. The cinematography was grand and expressive. It gave a real impression of the sheer magnitude of this daunting prison.

But the one thing which makes THE SHAWSHANK REDEMPTION stand above all other films, is the attention given to the story. The film depends on the story and the way in which it unravels. It's a powerful, poignant, thought-provoking, challenging film like no other. If Andy were to comment on this film, I think he might say: "Get busy watching, or get busy dying." Take his advice.

Thoroughly recommended.

10.title: A Film that will touch your soul
10.content: I read this novella in Stephen Kings "Four Seasons" while i was doing my GCSE exams. i remember then what a profound effect the story had on me. A story of hope through extreme adversity and the power of friendship that i thought could not be found between two men. The sheer anticipation of this film being released was almost heart stopping, but coupled with the fear it would not live up to my expectations. i also remember thinking that i did not want to see it for fear of it shattering my own perceptions of the two main characters, ANDY and RED. i need not have feared a thing.....the screenplay and adaptation was done with nothing short of pure brilliance. the camera work and choice of location could not have been more suitable. perhaps it is a symbol of how well Mr King writes that, it seems, everyones picture of everything is the same!!! Thus is was quite easy to choose sets, locations and of course actors. In the book, RED is a white, Irish man......against all odds, i cannot imagine ANYONE else delivering such a captivating, believable and utterly brilliant performance as Morgan Freeman. This man deserves 20 Oscars his acting together with the small stabs of narration are mind blowing who else could have done this?!! NO-ONE!! Tim Robbins IS ANDY!....his whole movement and attitude were exactly what King had written, this was encompassed in Robbins' portrayal perfectly. together the chemistry they had was beautiful, you could see that these characters were good friends, as well as the actors that played them. The visionary pieces of the film that will always linger? well the whole film lingers, such was the effect it had on me, but the two specific points in the film? Firstly, Andy described to RED where he could find a box, near a tree in a field, under some rocks to be exact. Now this bit is in the book (obviously!!) but i remember when i read it, the picture of that tree, in that field, next to that wall. In the film it was as if they had asked ME to choose the location, a chill went down my spine and it nearly brought me to tears!!! and i am NOT KIDDING!!!!. The second bit, well its right at the end, its the smile on RED's face when he sees ANDY again. This is not a feeble lip turning grin.....NO this is a full , both sets of teeth, cheek aching smile!!!! it IS the biggest and most emotional smile i have ever seen in any film. i could go on for pages about this film, i have been a film fan ever since i can remember, sitting with my father on a Sunday afternoon (before the times of VCR's or satellite, when you watched what was on that day or tough!!!) we watched films like "The African Queen", "Bridge on the River Kwai", "Citizen Kane", "The Rear Window", etc and from then i always liked a good film with a good story, The Shawshank Redemption was already a good story, it took genius to make it a GREAT film. to date i have seen it over 100 times. this has taken me through 3 copies on Video before the DVD came out, i am now on my 2nd DVD. if i have to buy another 100 DVD's it will always always alway be my number one favourite film of all time. It is a film you can watch at any time, when you are in any mood and it is still as compelling as the first time i saw it, or indeed the first time i read the story. 20 out of 10........

10.title: An Amazing Experience

It's been 15 years since I watched this movie for the first time. Back then, in my youth, several aspects of this movie made me think a lot: the value of true friendship, the injustices in life, the importance of not giving up on your dreams and, the most powerful of all, always have hope and make your thoughts and actions rely on that hope. I also remember thinking that, while some characters got what they deserved, others were wronged in a way that annoyed me too much. That was the reason that I liked but not loved this movie in the first time.

After that first time, I watched this movie at least another five times. Today, 15 years later, I can say that the injustices in the movie are not only bearable but also completely necessary. This is the real magic about this movie: you can find good in murderers, evil in wardens, friendship in a deceitful place, justice in injustices and hope in despair. Those ingredients are responsible for making this story so believable. This movie is capable of captivating the viewer through the natural bond created with the protagonist, in such way that, in the end, when everything went to despair, the viewer learns that hope is the only thing that anyone should not abandon. Yes, this movie is a true masterpiece.

The narrative is beautifully paced, the cinematography is stunning, and the score by Thomas Newman perfectly complements the film's emotional beats.

Every time I watch this movie, I discover something new-whether it's a subtle detail in the performances, a line of dialogue that resonates differently, or a deeper appreciation for the story's themes. It's a movie that invites you to reflect on life, friendship, and the human spirit.

The Shawshank Redemption is not just a movie; it's an experience. It's one of those films that stays with you, and no matter how many times you revisit it, it never loses its magic. For me, it's a perfect example of why cinema is such a powerful art form.

**"The Shawshank Redemption": A Tale of Hope and Friendship**

"The Shawshank Redemption" is a film that transcends its prison setting to explore themes of time, patience, and loyalty. Directed by Frank Darabont and based on a Stephen King story, the movie follows the lives of two men serving life sentences in Shawshank Prison.

The story is narrated by Ellis "Red" Redding (played by Morgan Freeman), a long-time inmate who becomes friends with Andy Dufresne (played by Tim Robbins). Andy, a former banker convicted of murder, possesses an unwavering determination and strength that captivates everyone around him.

10.title: about the movie

really its a great movie.......... It is a strange comment to make about a film set inside a prison, but "The Shawshank Redemption" creates a warm hold on our feelings because it makes us a member of a family. Many movies offer us vicarious experiences and quick, superficial emotions. "Shawshank" slows down and looks. It uses the narrator's calm, observant voice to include us in the story of men who have formed a community behind bars. It is deeper than most films; about continuity in a lifetime, based on friendship and hope.

Interesting that although the hero of the film is the convicted former banker Andy Dufresne (Tim Robbins), the action is never seen from his point of view. The film's opening scene shows him being given two life sentences for the murder of his wife and her lover, and then we move, permanently, to a point of view representing the prison population and particularly the lifer Ellis 'Red' Redding (Morgan Freeman). 10.title: A Groundbreaking Masterpiece
10.content:
Many of the most powerful stories are the soulful ones that teach us not to despair, not to be swamped by sorrow. They remind us that hope is a precious and buoyant emotion which can give our lives substance and meaning.

The Shawshank Redemption is based on a novella by Stephen King. Tim Robbins plays Andy, a banker who is sent to prison for the murder of his wife and her lover. The judge who sentences him finds him "a particularly remorseless and icy man." Andy's cool reserve and aloofness is not accepted well by the other inmates at Shawshank maximum-security prison in Maine. He is raped by some angry men and given several long stretches in solitary confinement for his bad attitude.

Luckily, Andy is befriended by Red, played by Morgan Freeman, the prison fixer. He is awed by this young man's quiet reserve and inward resolve to make the best of his bad situation. Andy's accounting skills come in handy, and he begins doing the taxes for the guards and laundering money for the corrupt warden. This lands him the cushy job of librarian. Eventually, Andy wrangles money out of state officials to build the best prison library anywhere.

Writer and director Frank Darabont draws out strong and intense performances from Morgan Freeman and Tim Robbins as soulmates who support each other while doing hard time. Red sees hope as a dangerous thing that can drive a man insane, but Andy believes it is fuel that keeps one going against all odds. The Shawshank Redemption is a jubilant tribute to hope as an essential quality of soul.

10.title: One Of The Greatest Films Ever Made. An Excellent,Powerful,Unforgettable Masterpiece.
10.content:
The Shawshank Redemption is one of the greatest films ever made,an excellent,powerful and unforgettable masterpiece that combines terrific direction,brilliant performances from an outstanding cast,a wonderful script and a powerful and memorable score. All of those elements make The Shawshank Redemption not only one of the best Stephen King adaptations but a movie that is cinema at it's best.

Based on the Novella Rita Hayworth and The Shawshank Redemption by Stephen King,The Shawshank Redemption tells the story of Andy Dufresne(Tim Robbins),a banker who is serving two life prison sentences for killing his wife and lover(although he claims he's innocent)at Shawshank prison. While at the prison Andy meets fellow inmate Red(Morgan Freeman)a man who can get things inside and the two form a long friendship while dealing with life in Shawshank prison.

Released in 1994,The Shawshank Redemption is a truly brilliant and outstanding film that was the directorial debut of Frank Darabont and his first feature film adaptation of a Stephen King tale. Despite receiving rave reviews from critics and earning 7 Academy Award nominations The Shawshank Redemption wasn't a huge hit at the Box Office and was overshadowed by other classic movies released the same year such as Pulp Fiction and Forrest Gump. But thanks to television showings and success on Home Video The Shawshank Redemption became a classic and one of the most memorable movies of all-time. The Shawshank Redemption is a film that is an instant classic the first time you watch it and is a movie that is powerful and dramatic,meaningful and gripping,uplifting and sad as well as humorous and light. All of those elements give Shawshank Redemption an emotional weight that reminds viewers why film is such a beautiful art form because it's a film where just everything works from the direction,acting and writing where everything is flawless. The Shawshank Redemption is a prison movie that has some of the grit and brutality of other prison movies but the storyline is much different and unpredictable than other prison films with messages and themes that are repeated throughout such as hope,life and optimism despite being in prison and dealing with the hardships. It's rare to see or hear such themes talked about in a prison movie but that is one of the things that makes Shawshank stand out from the other movies in the prison genre. Shawshank also shows viewers what a talented and versatile writer Stephen King truly is showing us that King can not do Horror and Science Fiction but can also do Drama. Shawshank along with other great Stephen King adaptations such as The Green Mile and Stand By Me are prime examples that King can do Drama. Shawshank also deals with not only prison life but also the passage of time going from the 1940s to the 1960s with posters of beautiful and sexy actresses such as Rita Hayworth,Marliyn Monroe and Raquel Welch showing that while time stands still in prison the world can move pretty fast. The pace of this movie is just terrific going by fast making you feel like you're watching a 90 minute film than a 2 and half hour one. The screenplay by Frank Darabont is amazing and memorable with dialog that is fresh and powerful as well as memorable and thoughtful. Shawshank's two main characters Andy and Red are classic characters who are the anchors of the film showing viewers the kind of friendship that lasts a long time. Andy and Redd look at prison life in different ways,Andy despite serving a life sentence believes that there is still hope beyond the prison walls and no one not the warden or the guards can't touch inside of him. Whereas Red is opposite and more cynical believe there is just prison life and that's all there is. However,despite their opposite ways of thinking Andy and Red's friendship and bond is strong and grows as the film goes on and when you see these two throughout the movie you will feel that there is redemption and hope for Andy and Red. Andy and Red is one of the best depictions of friendship in movie history and you will never forget these characters after the film is over. The final 20-30 minutes of The Shawshank Redemption is one of greatest endings ever seen on film because there is surprises and happiness that will make you smile and cry with joy. A masterful conclusion.

The cast is outstanding. Tim Robbins is excellent and at his best as Andy Dufresne,with Robbins bringing a power and emotional depth to the performance. Morgan Freeman is brilliant and his best as well as Red,Andy's best friend and prison mate. Robbins and Freeman are magical together and have great scenes. Bob Gunton is fantastic and memorable as Wardon Norton,a corrupt prison Wardon. William Sadler is terrific and funny as Heywood,Andy and Red's friend and fellow prisoner. Clancy Brown is amazing and menacing as Captain Hadley,a Shawshank's brutal guard. Gil Bellows is sensational as Tommy,a young convict. James Whitmore is outstanding as Brooks,an old timer and prisoner. Mark Rolston(Bogs),Larry Brandenburg(Skeet),Brian Libby(Floyd),Neil Giuntoli(Jigger),David Proval(Snooze),Joseph Ragno(Ernie)and Jeffrey McDunn(1946 D.A)give good performances as well.

The direction by Frank Darabont is fantastic and stunning,with Darabont moving the camera with tracking shots,low angles with beautiful and harsh lighting. Great direction,Darabont.

The score by Thomas Newman is terrific,beautiful and epic and is fits with the movie's tone. Incredible score,Newman.

In final word,if you love Tim Robbins,Morgan Freeman,Frank Darabont,Stephen King,Prison Films or movies in general,I highly suggest you see The Shawshank Redemption,an excellent and unforgettable masterpiece that you can watch again and again and is cinema at it's best. Highly Recommended. 10/10.

There are no special effects in this, no action, just men in a prison who talk. But it's what they talk about that matters. All these beautiful themes of friendship, hardship, hope and freedom are in all these prisoners who we all come to love (well, most). Thomas Newman provides us with a gentle and utterly beautiful score. It is truly hard to believe this didn't sweep the Oscars (not that it matters). Tim Robbins gives his greatest performance in this film, it's truly moving and he just embraces his character. Morgan Freeman also gives a performance to remember and his narration couldn't have been done better by anyone else, it's a beautiful thing that helps carry the movie.

5/5. I urge people who haven't seen it to see it immediately, you will not regret it.
