10.title: "Fear can hold you prisoner, Hope can set you free"
10.content:
"The Shawshank Redemption" takes a look at life behind bars from a whole, new perspective. Rather than your basic break for freedom plot, this film focuses on the cost of adapting to prison life and how some convicts, once they conform, lose the ability to survive beyond the iron bars and barbed wire. The story takes place between the years of 1947 through to 1966 and follows the struggle of one-time successful and promising banker Andy Dufresne. Dufresne was convicted of the murder of his wife and lover when he is sent to Shawshank State Prison and sentenced to life behind bars. It is in Shawshank where he forms a friendship with Ellis Boyd "Red" Redding, the "Sears and Roebuck" of Shawshank and uses his "hope" to get through life behind bars. It is he ("Red") who narrates the film which, rather than interfere upon the story, sustains and facilitates the film to make for an incredibly powerful and moving account of life inside prison. Director, Frank Darabont directs a magnitude of remarkable performances. Most notably from Tim Robbins who gives an exceptional performance as Andy Dufresne and Morgan Freeman who's performance as 'Red' makes for a fascinating and intriguing film. Fine supporting performances also come from Bob Gunton (Warden Samuel Norton), William Sadler (Heywood), and Clancy Brown (Captain Byron T. Hadley) but remarkably, one of the first-class performances comes from James Whitmore as Brooks Hatlen. The scenes with him attempting to cope with life outside of Shawshank make for one of the film's most moving, effective and powerful sequences. "The Shawshank Redepmtion" is a truly remarkable film and is utterly unique not just in the prison drama genre but in the history of film its self.

My Rating : An Outstanding 10/10

A slow paced burn with a cathartic ending, this film demonstrates the true power of cinema.

10.title: Splendid

Masterpiece."The Shawshank Redemption," directed by Frank Darabont and based on Stephen King's novella, is a timeless masterpiece that delves into themes of hope, friendship, and the resilience of the human spirit. The film follows Andy Dufresne, played by Tim Robbins, a banker wrongfully imprisoned for his wife's murder, and his transformative friendship with fellow inmate Ellis "Red" Redding, portrayed by Morgan Freeman.

The cinematography beautifully captures the oppressive atmosphere of Shawshank Prison, while the screenplay is filled with poignant dialogue and memorable moments. Robbins delivers a powerful performance, showcasing Andy's quiet determination and intellect, while Freeman's narration adds depth and warmth to the narrative.

What truly sets this film apart is its exploration of hope-Andy's unwavering belief in a better future resonates profoundly. The emotional payoff is satisfying and uplifting, making it a film that stays with you long after the credits roll. A true classic that masterfully intertwines despair with an enduring message of redemption and freedom.

10.title: My First Review!
10.content:
The Shawshank Redemption is a movie which will always stay with you. It has been good 15 years since I first saw this masterpiece and yet its taste lingers with me. It is not that I had not read Stephen King's short story, 'Rita Hayworth and Shawshank Redemption' already, nor was it the first time that I was watching a movie adaptation of a classic book or a short story (which, I confess, as a cherishing reader of the original works, had often been disappointing). But despite having watched this adaptation over and over again, each time I suggest this work of art to a friend, I have just one thing to say, 'If a movie could ever intoxicate its viewers, this would be the one'.

The life of the Shawshank prison is manifested in the story of Andy Dufresne, a banker, who was convicted for the murder of his cheating wife and was forced to accustom to the miserable life of the prison. Compellingly narrated by his best prison buddy 'Red', the movie, since the word go, engages the viewer in a tug of war as one tries to decide if the prison was changing Andy or, if Andy, through his submission, was changing the life within the prison. He was resilient, bold,yet non-rebellious, he was persistent, yet never imposing, and he was blending in yet standing out. Thus, if Andy was in a predicament within Shawshank, he was himself a predicament for the prison and it is left upon the viewer till the very end to decide on the question of who prevails in the end.

But the movie is not engulfed by Andy alone. It weaves within his life an account of multiple characters who give altering dimensions to the viewer's imagination of a prison life, as each character attempts to force an outcome for itself within the constraints of Shawshank. Yet the charm of Andy's character makes him stand out for me. It did not take long for 'handy' Andy to come to terms with this new life,and it seems to the viewer that he has accepted his fate. In his long journey, he makes warm relationships with his inmates and on rare, but stunning occasions, makes them see themselves as free men, albeit in prison uniform. And then one realizes that despite having accepted his fate,this was probably what Andy always felt;he was a free man within a prison uniform. How else could he have relentlessly pursued his freedom and executed his escape with such beauty? The viewer, the prison, saw him caged in his circumstances, surrendered and accustomed, freed only in the end after his escape from Shawshank. But the story was throughout different for Andy was always free, even inside Shawshank.

This classic has seen me through tough times and is no less than a lesson in optimism and tenacity. Amidst all other things, it is a story about one's pursuit after the impossible. When the going gets tough, the tough usually find ways to force a change as it tells you to begin with the slightest of openings and keep 'chipping away'.

10.title: Greatest movie ever made?
10.content: //////SPOILERS INCLUDED////////// Before I begin this review I would like to state my age and the date. I am 16 years old and today's date is July 16th 2016. I know thousands of reviews have been written regarding this movie but I doubt many have been wrote through the eyes and mind of a teenager. This film was originally recommended to me by my uncle when I was the age of 14, at the time I shunned the offer. 2 years later I have sat down to watch this film and I can comfortably say it was one of the best decisions I've made. The movie begins with an innocent banker Andy Dufrene (Tom Robbins) being sentenced to Shawshank prison for the murder of his wife. He soon is introduced to the trusty Red (Morgan Freeman), their friendship blossoms and this adds to the raw cinematography. I can honestly say from the eyes of naive teenager this is one of, if not the best films I have seen. It stems along side another Stephen King classic, Stand by me. The Shawshank Redemption is often critiqued along side The Godfarther to determine which is the greatest. But personally I believe The Godfarther should put it's success down to the director Francis Coppola and main actor Marlon Brando, without them the movie would not be the same. Shawshank is genuine and delivers morals with a great perspective on life, that being friendship and loyalty is more important than greed and success. It's very rare to find a film that really hits you and makes you actually contemplate what should be a priority and that is why I believe The Shawshank Redemtion is greatest film ever made. Frank Darabont - job well done!

10.title: Superb!!!
10.content: First, the Shawshank Redemption has been my favorite movie ever since I saw it for the first time a few years after its initial release. I know I have seen it more than 50 times and it never gets old. The film is a heart-wrenching tale of a falsely accused man forced to do a life term in prison due to an ironic twist of fate. Along the way, Andy makes friends amongst his fellow prison mates; as well as some friends in higher places. These friendships greatly influence the plot and outcome of the story. The film has a dark side, too as the brutalities of everyday prison life come to the forefront. Also, the film possesses a lighter side with its portrayal of hope and faith and how those traits can rise out of desperation. This film is a must see, and anyone who watches it will undoubtedly laugh, cry, and wonder as they follow the trials and tribulations of Andy Defresne and his close circle of friends as they experience life behind bars inside the deep, dark, and dank Shawshank Prison.

10.title: a film to treasure
10.content:
The Shawshank Redemption is one of those films which will stick with you for the rest of your life. You'll always remember it, think of it fondly, and smile when you think of the best parts of the film. Many films come and go in your memory (will you honestly look back at a film like Armageddon and think of it in the same light? I hope not), but this is one which has become great, and will become greater with time.

Everyone knows the story, so I will save time relating that to you, but I will say that the story has many levels to it, which are not as obvious to some viewers. The multitude of characters which the story gives us all have meaning and consequences to the two central characters, Andy and Red. (Think about the references to/theme of birds). All the characters are a pleasure to watch, and come to life by the actors. However, the actors inhabit their roles so well, its hard to see them in different roles now.

Tim Robbins was unfortunate not to be nominated for any other award than the screen actors guild award, because he brought such weight and balance to the film, where Morgan Freeman had the slightly more showy role, bringing dignity and honesty to it. I think any nomination or award for either of the actors should have been shared.

Frank Darabont is a talented director who has a good eye for what looks good on screen, has a way with his actors to produce the best out of them, understands how to tell a good story, and is likely to produce fine pieces of work in the future.

I have always loved this film, and the story is just one which warms the heart and blood just thinking about it.

As the uptight banker, Robbins does some of his subtlest acting to date. As his hardened but resilient friend, Freeman is simply miraculous, giving the role so much depth, dignity, and good humor that you feel that you've known this man forever. If the film is perhaps a little slow in its middle passages, maybe that is part of the idea, too, to give us a sense of the leaden passage of time, before the glory of the final redemption. Some of "The Shawshank Redemption'' comes across as outrageously improbable. Yet the film keeps pulling you back with its sense of striving humanity slowly turning the tables against evil.

Because it did have Morgan Freeman in it, I made a mental note and said to myself, "If its available I may give it a go". All my manager would tell me was it was "long, drawn out and tedious" but that I should hang with it cause it would be "well worth the wait". Now he's a decent manager but our lifestyles are so different outside of work, I was like "yeah right. He would recommend something that I would like." But it was available and I rented it. I held on to it for seven days, about to just take it back since it was due without watching it but hey--I hated to feel like I wasted money.

I watched it and I did not waste my money.

This has become to me one of the best films I have ever seen(so far) in my life. It was long but I got into it slowly, methodically and so captivatingly, the time drifted slowly. Sucking me in, I could hardly know what to expect. And what I expected didn't happen and I just was transfixed. Tim Robbins to me was brilliant. He painstakingly went through those years, aging and moving forward through all the disappointments, growth and experiences as if he were in a long chess game. I became so caught up I could not even begin to think about how this would turn out all the stories and events.

And when the end came, I was just blown away by it. I truly loved all performances and so many "character actors" now are faces and names I know and they all performed well and are remembered in my head when I see them--for this movie.

I find myself recommending it now to people and I too ask them to "hang with it. its well worth the wait".

10.title: This is a movie that you can watch it again right after you just finished watching it.

The movie, The Shawshank Redemption, which came out in 1994 is about two main characters Andy Dufresne (Tim Robbins) and Ellis Boyd 'Red' Redding (Morgan Freeman) and their journey through prison in the 1940's. Andy was falsely accused and sentenced to life imprisonment for the murder of his wife and her lover. This movie represents integrity as Andy never gives up and he knows that in the end he will be free as he was falsely accused. He knew that one day the prison guards and warden would pay their dues for how they ran their prison. This movie shows it all and is absolutely a 10 out of 10.

My favorite scene was when Andy was when Andy gets access to the room where the microphone is set up to talk over the intercom. Andy plays a record of two ladies singing and all of the prisoners sit in awe not knowing what to think or how to feel. Red makes the statement that he doesn't know what the two ladies were singing let alone saying but how it brought peace over his mind and the others as the music was calming, soothing, and a sight of the real world.

This is a movie that you can watch it again right after you just finished watching it. There is so much anticipation and as a viewer you get wrapped up in the scene and the emotions that are the prisoners are feeling.

Another scene that really made me nervous was when Red is about to leave to meet Andy in Buxton County and he signs his name on the board where a previous prison member hung himself and had signed his name before he committed suicide. In this scene, the viewers watches Red sign his name and assume that he is going to hang himself but the scene flashes forward to Red digging up a box that Andy had given him directions to. In that box, there is cash and a post car of where Andy is at.

This film is absolutely amazing and I recommend it to anyone. I could go on forever about this movie but it is a must see, it's a movie that will have you thinking about it after you watch it. The friendship that Andy and Red made was unbreakable; they had hope in one another. Each character showed determination and courage, this is a movie that you wont regret watching.

On the other hand, a children's movie that shows integrity would be the movie Antz. As adults watch Shawshank they can relate on multiple levels as they have gone through life experiences where they have been falsely accused or have been in a situation where they know if they stay true to themselves then the right thing will happen. Same goes for children in the movie Antz as Flick never gives up on himself or the fact that he is trying to help his colony even when they are all against him.

10.title: The Shawshank Redemption Review
10.content:
The Shawshank Redemption follows a group of prison inmates as they serve out their sentences.

This film is nothing short of phenomenal and I can see why it is considered among many as the greatest film ever created. My favourite two kinds of films consist of crowd pleasers and deep dive dramas that focus on certain lifestyles. This film fills both those slots. We get to see how exactly prison affects people and everything that is involved with being a prisoner. We also get some great moments towards the end that put a smile on your face every time you watch it.

Across the board incredible acting, Tim Robbins and Morgan Freeman both give probably their greatest performance, along side the rest of this perfect cast.

Tim Robbins character Andy Dufresne gives us the angle of an innocent man entering prison, but not just an innocent man an intelligent innocent and I'll get to why his intelligence is so important later. We get to see Andy go through different stages of prison as we see what happens to people that are alone in prison, how they get targeted out by rapists and how they are treated with zero respect. Then we get to see what happens when you have something to offer the guards and the warden, in Andy's case it's is knowledge of banking. We see Andy begin by helping guards set up savings accounts and help them with their taxes all of which help him get in good with guards. But eventually we get to see how certain guards or in this case the warden may be worse then the people imprisoned. Warden Norton played by Bob Gunton recruits Andy to help him launder money, but once Andy has a chance at getting out the Warden makes sure he can't leave by killing the person that could lead Andy to freedom. This again gives us a great angle into what goes on in these prisons and how guards and wardens take advantage of their authority since they know inmates can do nothing to stop them.

We don't find out until the end of the film but throughout his time in prison Andy has been digging a hole to escape, which really adds another layer onto why he does the things he does. Andy has been attempting to make the lives of these inmates better so when he eventually escapes he doesn't feel guilty for leaving his friends in a unsafe environment. We see him build up a large library as well as teach certain inmates so they can receive their high school diploma. Then at the end Andy is responsible for the arrest and 'almost arrest' of the warden and captain hadley.

Another side of prison we get to see are the prisoners who have essentially spent their lives in prison. Red played by Morgan Freeman has become somewhat of a tycoon in prison, as he is one of the people that smuggle into the prison. By the time Red is released he had spent 40 years in prison and isn't accustomed to life outside, so when he is released and begins working he realizes that he is not meant to be outside of prison.

Another character in this film had the same revelation. Brooks Hatlen played by James Whitmore was released from prison earlier in the film but when he had that revelation he committed suicide. Red on the other hand was lucky enough to have a friend like Andy. Before Andy escaped we get to see him give instructions to Red on where to find a rock, and under that rock is where Andy had hidden something. Under that rock was a letter to Red explaining where Andy was and that he would love to have his help with a new project of his. That is when we get to see the two reunite in a very satisfying conclusion.

10/10.

10.title: The Shawshank Redemption Movie

The film, directed by Frank Darabont and adapted from a Stephen King novella, captivates with its strong performances, particularly by Tim Robbins and Morgan Freeman. It effectively portrays the human spirit's capacity to overcome adversity, set against the backdrop of prison life. The storytelling is meticulous, blending a sense of realism with an uplifting narrative. Its powerful themes and well-developed characters contribute to its status as a beloved classic, resonating with audiences through its message of enduring hope and personal strength.

10.title: Thanks for everyone's high rating. I adapted the short story for the screen
10.content: Wow, been a few years. I'm editing my old post. I'd like to humbly thank everyone here for rating my flick so highly. #1, huh? Providing the story for Shawshank Redemption was an imagination of myself under the short story's circumstances. It is similar to K-PAX that way and of the same vintage. Having been a business major at Georgia Tech, it would be natural for me to help with estate planning, taxes, and accounting had I been taken prisoner. The inside out program of public works and attendant graft, corruption, intimidation and murder was my way of encouraging scrutiny of similar programs nation-wide. I had been Postmaster of the Georgia State Senate at 21, so that is why the State Senate was written instead of the more common oracles, say the Maine Governor's office or other organs of government and foundations. The Mozart duet wasn't of my choosing, but it's generally acknowledged as among the most beautiful pieces of music ever written, so that choice was a no-brainer. I would have preferred the flute solo from Orpheus, but that's just me. I purposefully decided against another loathsome portrayal of racial casts that were very common at that time, so as not to 'date' the picture and to influence viewers toward tolerance even in intolerable circumstances. Against opposition, I gave the important Red character to an African-American actor. (In the short story Red had been an Irishman.) At the time, that dimmed prospects for box office success, but given that the flick is now well- received, emulation has led to further improvement. When we did this one in 1988ish, in Syracuse, New York, I was attending graduate school of medicine at SUNY-upstate and working in Max Mozell's lab. At about the same time, I did dozens of films and won many Oscars for the various ghost writers. (Gladiator, Good Will Hunting, Cast Away, Mystic River, Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind, Enemy at the Gates, Green Mile, Shawshank Redemption, Vanilla Sky, A Beautiful Mind, Forrest Gump, The Matrix films, The Bourne films, National Treasure films, Pirates of the Caribbean films, Avatar, Titanic, Lost in Translation, UP, ). The name of the Mexican town on the seashore was conveyed to me by my old friend, Frank Arnold, who was Zawataneo (sp?) on vacation while in medical school. He spelled it for me over the phone while the 'creative team' and I worked out the flick's details. Since then, the town has boomed, an unexpected gift to Mexico. I set this one in Maine, to de-stigmatize inflexible regional prejudices then current. It seems to have worked. Michael Meyers figured me out, this flick is part of the series designed to change the world, save the planet, and bring the human race closer to God Almighty.

Forget about what others (including myself) might suggest you'll discover in "The Shawshank Redemption;" when you watch it, you'll identify something very personal in your own life with a scene, a character, or a moment in this uncomplicated movie. When you need hope, you'll look for Shawshank. When you want to believe in the will of overcoming even the greatest obstacles, Shawshank will uplift you in ways that you can't find in movies today.

Some liken the film to some kind of spiritual awakening. Of course, some can go to a church or mosque to find enlightenment and Faith in humanity, but most places of worship are open only certain days or times. But when you need affirmation of the lasting bond of friendships that prevail over the most dire circumstances, Shawshank will give it to you. It makes grown men (like me) cry, still. I wonder whether Shawshank was truly meant for viewing in the privacy of the home, because it is a personal experience that really makes you look inward. Nominated for seven, this is the best film that never one a single Oscar.

10.title: Brilliant and Moving:
10.content:
This is a love story, as old as the hills and yet with freshness that can only be given to us by great Celluloid actors such as Morgan Freeman and Tim Robbins. There are many examples of this throughout literature and the adaptation of this from word to film is breathtaking.

Andy and Red quite obviously have a deep and abiding love and respect for each other that transcends any feeling we might otherwise have about the nature of their love, which incidentally is not a homosexual love.

But let us not forget the other performances. How wonderful to see James Whitmore as Brooks Hatlen and of course the brilliant William Saddler. It would have been too easy to slip into a prison melodrama but I think it was played perfectly by having Red narrate throughout, the two most wonderful pieces of narrative are where Andy plays Mozart over the prison loudspeakers and where Red sits in his cell, fearful and alone in the dark on the night of Andy's escape.

'Some things are just too beautiful.' 'Time draws out like a blade.'

I guess that encapsulates the whole thing for me, because it's how time draws out while watching this beautiful picture. The blade cuts you to the heart because you long for Red and Andy to fulfil their hope.

If I could, I would give this more than 10 out of 10 but I cannot. Instead I'll just say that this movie will give pleasure to people when played as an oldie in 50 years, because the story is timeless. No special effects, no fancy graphics, just a simple story, beautifully told and acted superbly.

10.title: "Prison is no fairy tale world."
10.content: I never fail to be captivated by this film when I watch it.This,indeed, is no run of the mill prison flick.It is really not a prison movie at all.True,it takes place in a prison,but it is really a story about what lies beyond the prison walls;freedom itself.Some within the prison walls crave it,desire it.Others fear it,simply because prison has become their home,and freedom would remove them from their comfort zone.This is a sad reality made all too clear,here.This is also a story of hope and tenacity.You find yourself looking at the film's main character, Andy Dufresne (played brilliantly by Tim Robbins),and you find yourself wanting to have as much smarts,and tenacity as he does.You also find yourself looking at Andy's close friend,Ellis "Red" Redding (played with flawless perfection,as always,by Morgan Freeman),and wanting to go back and correct all the stupid things you did when you were young. You look at Brooks (James Whitmore) and you are saddened to realize that having been imprisoned so long,that he is doomed,never to fit in,in this ever rapidly changing world.Being released,in fact,becomes a worse hell than being incarcerated in the first place.There are many individual characters to look at from different angles,and this is what makes Shawshank a great film.Don't miss it.

10.title: Timeless classic
10.content:
One of the most gripping movies of all time. Its a fantastic journey which has three characteristics:

1. It would take a really long time to complete. He has a feel for how long it would take - but he doesn't know that exactly. And that feel changes every day as well.

2. He can get caught at any point - in the beginning, in the middle, or at the end - literally on any given day until he is done - and if he is caught, all his efforts up to that point add up to nothing. The net effect of getting caught would be negative, in the form of additional punishment, added with absolutely no scope of receiving a parole thereafter

3. The end result is binary: If he gets caught, twenty years' effort adds up to nothing. On the other hand, if he succeeds, he can be a free man and live the rest of his life happily.

If you think about it, the exact same characteristics are shared by anyone working on a Startup (in addition to the fact that only fools would embark on a journey with these characteristics):

1. It would take a really long time to complete. You have a feel for how long it would take - but you don't know that exactly. Besides, this feel changes everyday. 2. You can fail at any point- in the beginning, in the middle, or at the end - literally on any given day until you are done - and if you fail, all your efforts up to that point add up to nothing. The net effect of a failure would be negative, in the form of lost investment, opportunity costs, and a bunch of significant 'could have beens' 3. The end result is binary: If you fail, you will feel that your efforts added up to nothing. If you succeed, well.....

It might be a strange observation to make from a movie about people serving life-terms in prison - but if you observe closely, the simple and most powerful message from 'The Shawshank Redemption' is this: 'Enjoy The Journey'.

10.title: Uplifting and Inspirational
10.content:
Back in 1994, 'The Shawshank Redemption' opened to lukewarm reviews and mild economic success, securing less than $30 million at the domestic box office. Though nominated for a very respectable seven Academy Awards, it failed to win any of these, up against the likes of 'Forrest Gump' and 'Pulp Fiction.' Since then, the film has steadily grown in popularity and now stands as one of the most highly-regarded films of the 1990's.

Convicted for the brutal murder of his wife and her lover, a crime of which he claims to be innocent, Andy Dufresne (Tim Robbins, 'Mystic River,' 2003) is ordered to serve two back-to-back life sentences at Shawshank Prison. Life is hard. The prison guards are brutal and unforgiving, many prisoners are ruthlessly antagonistic towards Andy, and the warden is greedy and corrupt. Nevertheless, Andy forms lifelong friendships with many of his fellow prisoners, most particularly Red (Morgan Freeman, 'Se7en,' 1995), the "man who can get things." Clinging stubbornly to the knowledge of his own innocence, Andy never loses his hope that justice will inevitably prevail.

Despite being a story filled with suffering and adversity, 'The Shawshank Redemption' remains one of the most uplifting and inspirational films of all time.

10.title: Best movie ever
10.content:
The Shawshank Redemption is a timeless masterpiece that transcends the typical prison drama, offering a profound meditation on hope, friendship, and resilience. Directed by Frank Darabont and based on a novella by Stephen King, the film centers around Andy Dufresne (played brilliantly by Tim Robbins), a man wrongfully imprisoned for the murder of his wife. Over the course of two decades, we witness Andy's quiet strength and determination, as he befriends Ellis "Red" Redding (portrayed by Morgan Freeman), a long-time inmate with a deep sense of wisdom.

What sets The Shawshank Redemption apart is its focus on the emotional and psychological aspects of imprisonment rather than sensationalizing violence. The narrative is enriched by Freeman's impeccable voice-over, offering reflective insights that elevate the film to a philosophical level.

The film's pacing is slow but purposeful, allowing viewers to truly invest in the characters. The bond between Andy and Red is the heart of the story, showcasing the power of human connection even in the bleakest circumstances. The final act delivers a satisfying and emotionally charged conclusion that reaffirms the central theme: hope is a powerful force that can sustain the human spirit, no matter the odds. An unforgettable, uplifting cinematic experience.

10.title: A masterpiece

The Shawshank Redemption" is a masterpiece that transcends its genre. As an amateur watcher, I was captivated by the film's gripping narrative, compelling characters, and poignant themes. Set within the confines of Shawshank State Penitentiary, the story follows Andy Dufresne, a banker wrongly convicted of murder, and his unlikely friendship with fellow inmate Red.

What struck me most about the film was its portrayal of hope and resilience in the face of adversity. Despite the harsh realities of prison life, Andy maintains his dignity and optimism, inspiring those around him to believe in the possibility of redemption. The bond between Andy and Red, beautifully portrayed by Tim Robbins and Morgan Freeman, is the heart of the film, offering moments of warmth and camaraderie amidst the bleakness of their surroundings.

Director Frank Darabont's direction is masterful, creating a sense of claustrophobia within the prison walls while also capturing the vastness of the human spirit. The cinematography is stunning, with hauntingly beautiful shots of the prison juxtaposed with scenes of freedom and liberation.

"The Shawshank Redemption" is a film that stays with you long after the credits roll, reminding us of the power of hope, friendship, and the resilience of the human spirit. As an amateur watcher, I can confidently say that this is a film that deserves its place among the greatest of all time.

10.title: Emotions, thrills, drama and triumph
10.content:
Based on a Stephen King novel, it's better than even THE GREEN MILE and shows that you don't need supernatural elements in a prison story - the setting is enough to make the movie what it is. SHOWSHAKN is frequently featured as the "best movie of all time" on various movie lists, including here, and while I don't necessarily agree with it, it's actually a very good movie, almost flawless in fact.

Every technical element of the film is impeccable, from direction to music, editing and acting; Morgan Freeman delivers his best performance ever, while Tim Robbins shows us what a great character actor he is. It's even better for a fan of the genre like me to see beloved actors like Clancy Brown, William Sadler, Brian Libby and James Whitmore appear in the film together and play more than just good or bad guys. Every single actor here is great, and the script (which is completely true to King's writing) is near-perfect. Emotions, thrills, drama and triumph.

10.title: The Shawshank Redemption - A Timeless Masterpiece
10.content:
"The Shawshank Redemption," directed by Frank Darabont, is a cinematic masterpiece that continues to captivate audiences with its powerful storytelling, exceptional performances, and profound themes. Adapted from Stephen King's novella, the film takes viewers on an emotional journey through the lives of two inmates at Shawshank State Penitentiary.

The film revolves around the character of Andy Dufresne, played brilliantly by Tim Robbins, a banker who is wrongfully convicted of murder and sentenced to life in prison. Inside Shawshank, Andy forms an unlikely friendship with Red, portrayed by Morgan Freeman, a long-term inmate who becomes his confidant and mentor.

What sets "The Shawshank Redemption" apart is its ability to delve deep into the human spirit and explore themes of hope, friendship, resilience, and the power of personal redemption. It presents a thought-provoking commentary on the nature of freedom and the indomitable strength of the human will, even in the most oppressive circumstances.

The performances in the film are exceptional, with Tim Robbins delivering a nuanced portrayal of Andy Dufresne. Robbins captures the character's quiet determination and subtle vulnerability, allowing the audience to connect with his journey of survival and transformation. Morgan Freeman's portrayal of Red is equally remarkable, showcasing his trademark gravitas and wisdom that perfectly complements Andy's character.

10.title: Possibly the Best of All Time
10.content:
I swear this movie was narrated by God, and by God I mean Morgan Freeman. When I found out Shawshank Redemption was a movie based off a Stephen King book, I expected a creepy horror movie, sort of like The Shinning. Needless to say, I was pleasantly surprised. Tim Robbins, Morgan Freeman, and the rest of the cast deliver in one of the greatest films ever made in history, at least according to IMDb, it was ranked number one. So how does one review possibly the best movie ever made?

The first time I watched Shawshank Redemption I wasn't really impressed, but when I saw it ranked atop the leader board on IMDb, I watched it again, and I agreed with its place. This movie was absolutely fantastic. The story flows and connects really well. The characters are lovable and important to the overall story and by the end it made me just go, "wow that was awesome."

This is a story of a man named Andy Dufresne who was convicted for the murder of his wife and the man who she had an affair with. When Dufresne arrives in Shawshank he keeps a low profile but struggles with what one would call normal prison problems. He then uses his intelligence of the business world to get on the good side of the guards and the warden. He makes the warden really wealthy and prison life becomes simpler. Then the story develops from there and it is rather complex, but I won't give too much away.

I have to start with a few flaws I saw in this movie. The story was a bit slow with a lot of scenes or stories within the major story taking place. In the beginning Andy had problems with the perverts of the prison, or Andy playing the music over the speakers of the prison etc. A few of these stories were pointless and just made me think, "Why?" Some were definitely amusing but it is only a small gripe. Maybe if I watch it again I will appreciate them more, but for now it just dragged the story if you ask me. A second problem, and this really bugged me, was the fact that Andy Dufresne entered the prison in 1947 and left in 1966. That is a 19 year period. For a story to last 19 years is not a problem at all, but the fact that the characters do not age annoyed me a lot. Morgan Freeman was supposed to be in his 40s at the start. Now it doesn't matter what decade it is in real life, Morgan Freeman always looks old and wise. And by the end, Freeman didn't really age at all. Sure maybe a gray hair or two, but that was it. Dufresne looked the exact same and so did the Warden. Now some might ask why 19 year storyline but it makes sense if you actually see the movie. The director could have easily added some wrinkles, white hair, something, but there was nothing and it didn't make the time span believable. When Freeman narrates it's 1966 I didn't really believe it. Little details like that are things I can overlook because it is such a fantastic movie but small things like that make an awesome movie a classic movie.

The major strength of the movie, in my opinion, is the characters. Dufresne, Red, the warden are the main characters so obviously they will have complexity and lovability, but even smaller characters like Brooks are still important. Brooks showed the prisoner who spends his life in prison and knows nothing else. He is a minor character but he made me think of prison life and prisoners themselves. When he got out of prison he didn't know what to do, he even wanted to stay. He had a minor role with a big impact. Even when he is gone he is remembered and mentioned many times.

I really don't remember his name but the character who was the stereotypical 60s man and resembled Elvis was possibly the most important character of all (I'm just going to call him Elvis.). To save spoilers I will only hit the tip of the iceberg. The main story connects with the minor stories told throughout the movie really well but the all seemed pointless until Elvis shows up in Shawshank. He gives Dufresne what he needs and makes the warden put on his evil pants. Basically, he is the turning point of the story and makes it relevant. If you saw the movie you will know exactly what I mean, and if you haven't then go see it so you aren't completely lost.

Now the ending was absolutely phenomenal. Throughout the entire move I was thinking what the point was and where it was going, but by the end it is so surprising and personally I thought it was unexpected. It makes you appreciate the idea of storytelling and keeping an audience interested and when I watched it a second time it was one of those times when you think, "Why didn't I see this coming?" I love it when movie do that because it makes me think and if a movie makes me think it means I am interested and it does its job of being a good movie.

Overall The Shawshank Redemption is a classic, possibly one of the best of all time. Do I think it deserves number one on IMDb's list? No, absolutely not but it should be in the top 10. A bit of a slow start to an amazing story that connects really well, a cast of characters portrayed in depth and detail, and an ending that will possibly blow your mind all form together to form on of, but not the best, movie of all time and without a shadow of a doubt gets the WillyT seal of approval. See this movie ASAP.

10.title: Truly a modern masterpiece.
10.content:
The Shawshank Redemption is about Andy Dufresne who was sent to Shawshank Prison for the double homicide of his cheating wife and her secret lover. But instead of feeling sorry for himself he lived the best he could and bettered the lives of fellow inmates through shear determination. In the process, he made many friends (Ellis 'Red' Redding being most notable of all) and even gained the respect of prison guards. Despite of serving back to back life sentences, Andy never gave up his ultimate dream of one day living by the ocean. That dream was further jeopardized because of what he knew, and there was someone who will go to great lengths to keep him locked up forever. Will Andy finally crack and lose hope, or will his perseverance prevail?

The Shawshank Redemption is the best movie that I've ever seen. I even like it better than any of the Godfather movies (which have a completely different theme up to the last episode). Perhaps I like this movie so much because it suits my taste. But I think most viewers of all kinds will appreciate Shawshank for the superb acting of the main characters, the insightful dialogs throughout, the powerful message it conveys, and the realness of the lives of convicts both inside the prison and outside once they're paroled.

It's a shame that Shawshank didn't win many awards since '94 was a tremendous year with the release of other great films like Pulp Fiction and Forrest Gump. But the acting and directing of this film was still outstanding. I can't ever imagine serving a life sentence, and prison life was much different in the mid 1900's from today. Still I was able to relate to what the main characters were feeling, and I was moved by their words and actions numerous times (especially those of Brooks).

The underlying theme of Shawshank was simple; it celebrated hope and perseverance just like Lord of the Rings. Hope and perseverance are indeed powerful elements in arts, and both films have done a marvelous job portraying these two aspects. However, Shawshank seemed more real because frankly it was set in our world and not a fantasy one. This is no knock against LOTR, but I find myself more involved in this film because I could relate to it more and it made a deeper impact on me.

******POSSIBLE SPOILERS BELOW******

Of course no film is perfect. There are minor details here and there than didn't make sense to me. For example, how could the wall fall apart so easily? How could Andy cut/break such a big hole through that steel pipe with a rock? How can Shawshank Prison ignore the smuggling of things (they definitely knew since there were posters on the prison walls and men were smoking smuggled cigarettes)? But these are minor things, and don't jeopardize the integrity of Shawshank.

I don't want to over-analyze Shawshank and give it away, but I would highly recommend it to anyone who's in the mood for a serious film. My final rating: 10/10.

10.content: The Shawshank redemption is about a man who is wrongly accused of murdering his wife and her lover and sentenced to life in prison. In prison the man makes friends with the inmates while improving the prison's library. He also gives financial advice to the prison security guards and personnel. The theme of this film, The Shawshank Redemption, is about finding friendship and having hope while being at a hard time in your life. Andy Dufresne is play by Tim Robbins and is the main character who is accused of murdering his wife and her lover in a jealous rage. Morgan Freeman also plays a huge part in this film as Ellis "Red" Boyd. Ellis or Red as he preferred to be called in the film is Andy's best friend in prison. There are five main plot points in my opinion within this film. These points include when the inmates are betting on the new arrivals, when some of the inmates are re-tarring the roof on one of the buildings, when new library books finally arrive after all of Andy's attempts, and when the warden of Shawshank discovers that Andy has escaped. This films theme is similar to the retelling of the mythical story of "Perseus" by author Edith Hamilton. There are several techniques that were used throughout this film but a few really caught my attention. The first technique is a motif, this is the repeated showing of the crow that Brooks rescued and raised. The birds represent a hopefulness of freedom but it also represented the loss of hope after prison. When Brooks is released, he also sets "Jake" the crow free and continues to look for him in a park nearby hoping that he will return to him. However, when Jake does not return it represents the loss of hope in Brooks for life after prison. Another technique that attributed to the emotions of the film was the lighting aspects. In the scene after Andy escapes where he is standing in water while it is raining with his arms spread wide, the light is directed down on him with his back in the shadows. This lighting technique in this scene adds to the feeling of triumph, of hope and of freedom. This film absolutely reflects the feeling of hope onto the viewers.

10.content:
The Shawshank Redemption" is a cinematic masterpiece that transcends time, offering a profound exploration of hope, friendship, and the human spirit's resilience. Directed by Frank Darabont and adapted from Stephen King's novella, the film takes us on an unforgettable journey through the lives of Andy Dufresne (Tim Robbins) and Ellis "Red" Redding (Morgan Freeman) within the cold, oppressive walls of Shawshank Prison.

The story begins with Andy, a quiet and intelligent banker, being convicted for the murder of his wife and her lover-a crime he insists he didn't commit. Thrown into the harsh realities of prison life, Andy seems out of place, but his determination to hold on to hope sets him apart. Over time, he forms an unlikely bond with Red, a long-serving inmate known for his ability to "get things." Their friendship becomes the heart of the story, offering moments of warmth and humanity amid the grim backdrop of Shawshank.

What makes The Shawshank Redemption so extraordinary is its ability to weave a narrative that is both poignant and uplifting. The screenplay is a masterclass in storytelling, blending subtle symbolism with powerful dialogue. Andy's actions-whether it's carving chess pieces, introducing a library system, or playing Mozart over the prison PA system-represent his quiet rebellion against despair. His unwavering belief that "hope is a good thing, maybe the best of things" becomes the film's central message.

Morgan Freeman's narration is iconic, lending the film a soul-stirring depth. His voice carries the weight of years spent in confinement, balancing moments of quiet reflection with dry wit. Tim Robbins, on the other hand, delivers a restrained yet compelling performance as Andy, portraying a man whose intelligence and quiet strength become his tools for survival.

Visually, the film captures both the claustrophobia of prison life and the expansiveness of hope. Roger Deakins' cinematography uses stark contrasts to reflect the emotional tone, while Thomas Newman's hauntingly beautiful score elevates every scene.

At its core, The Shawshank Redemption is about the triumph of the human spirit. It reminds us that even in the darkest places, hope can light the way to freedom-whether that freedom is physical, emotional, or spiritual. The final act, with its twist and deeply satisfying resolution, is as cathartic as it is inspiring.

Released in 1994, the film initially underperformed at the box office but has since gained legendary status, often regarded as one of the greatest films of all time. Its enduring appeal lies in its universal themes and ability to connect with audiences on a deeply personal level.

In short, The Shawshank Redemption is not just a film you watch-it's a film you experience, and it leaves you with the unshakable belief that "some birds aren't meant to be caged." A true classic, it's a testament to the power of storytelling and the enduring strength of hope.

"Get busy living or get busy dying"

An amazing movie. Easily one of the best movies made during the 90s and definitely one of the top "prison" movies of all-time. Pretty much everything about this movie works and works extremely well! The film touches upon many subjects, including the ideas of hope, redemption, love, loneliness, justice, life/death, friendship, endurance, fear, patience, inspiration and so much more.

Watching this movie always makes me feel a million times better, and if that's not the greatest reason to watch a film, I don't know what is. Give it up to both Freeman and Robbins for completely engulfing their characters with heart, soul and the spirit of humanity. I appreciated the message in this film, I absolutely loved the way it ended, I surrendered to its pace, I enjoyed all of its characters, I thought it was wonderfully photographed, I loved the score and I could seriously watch this movie 10 times a year and not bat an eyelash the whole way through.

And what kind of banner year was 1994?? PULP FICTION, FORREST GUMP, THE SHAWSHANK REDEMPTION and FOUR WEDDINGS AND A FUNERAL (one of my favorite romantic comedies of all-time) were all nominated for Best Picture. It's really too bad that most everyone got swept by that chocolate-lover, but no matter what the Academy deemed "better" that year, it goes without saying that SHAWSHANK has developed an even greater audience and following since that time, and is probably one of the most appreciated movies from the past twenty years (I usually NEVER hyperbolize any of my reviews (this is the BEST EVER...this is the WORST EVER...), but in this case, this film takes that cake and damn well, eats it too!).

Love it, watch it, get your own motivation from it and surrender to its spirit which gives anyone in the world hope to do whatever they dream to do in life. It's like I quoted back at the top of this review, you better "get busy living, or get busy dying". It don't get more black and white than that. Your choice.

CONTAINS SPOILERS Review by Joe: `Rita Hayworth and the Shawshank Redemption' the original short novel by legendary author Stephen King, sparked the start of a superb movie and ongoing legend. Andrew Dufresne, a fairly young man committed murder and was sentenced to life in Shawshank prison. There are some elements of this film that differ from elements of this novel. And yet many things are the same.

In the novel, Andy was a short, partially bald man, who was quiet and shy, and in the movie he was a tall intimidating stocky figure. I think this difference is important in one particular scene: the prisoners are tarring the roof, and Andy overhears Hadley, a man who is angry at the world, talking about his inheritance from his deceased brother. Andy speaks up about the taxes of the inheritance and Hadley gets furious. I think that if in the movie he was the man described in the book, it would have made this seem weak, and Hadley probably wouldn't have thought him worthy to even speak to him. I think this movie was put together well, but to be honest, I like Stephen King's short novel better.

Review by Steve: The movie was very good. Andy's life in prison was real. Andy really got cheated out of 20 years of his life. Andy's in jail for something he didn't do. I especially like the scene when the warden was talking to the media. When the warden was in front of the building talking it looked like the warden had a crown on. Showing that he was a king he had all the power. I didn't like the ending of the movie. It was good for them because it was what they both wanted. They both wanted freedom and that's what that scene showed. But they should have had some sort of action, like gone sailing, fishing, showed them both out to sea doing something. Being free. Not just on the beach hugging each other.

Review by Derek: I think that the directors should have filmed the movie in Charleston, Maine because I've spent a lot of time there. I wish I would have had a chance to see the whole movie but from what I saw it was a great movie. I liked the movie cause it seemed so real. But what I didn't like was how the guards and the warden thought that any one who got in the way or their business they could kill them or put them in solitary confinement. Plus I didn't like how guards treated inmates like slaves. They couldn't just face reality and treat them like equals. But it happens in prisons all over the world so that's why I liked Shawshank Redemption.

Review by Brad: I liked the movie compared to the book. I think that the movie was way better. The movie seemed to be way more interesting. It was complimentary to Stephen King's ways of writing an intricate portrayal of an actual event that took place in Maine. One of the things I liked about the movie is the way camera angles portray power.

Review by Dan: A Review of Shawshank Redemption from an Inmate's View I found the movie not nearly as enjoyable as Stephen King's `Rita Hayworth and the Shawshank Redemption'. The points I found I did not agree with are they have Red's character as a black man in the movie when in the short story he was a white Irish man but it kinda adds a little laughter to a serious theme. Second they have Andy Dufresne as a tall skinny man when in `Rita Hayworth.' he's a small and a heavy man with not much of an aura. Thirdly they have one warden Mr. Norton when there is three in the short story because it seems to the viewer that 19 years did not go by, but in a way its good so the viewer can focus his hate towards one figure. That's what I didn't like but there are more pros than cons. The film makers did an excellent job with the lighting, the angle of the camera and the music. With these three combined it gives the feelings of dread and despair as black as death. Freedom as high as a bird and sadness as deep as an ocean. With all these in mind it makes a great movie on a scale from 1 to 10 I'd give it 8 ½.

10.title: Masterpiece
10.content:
Why do I want to write the 999th comment on The Shawshank Redemption? I am not sure - almost everything that could be possibly said about it has been said. But like so many other people who wrote comments, I was and am profoundly moved by this simple and eloquent depiction of hope and friendship and redemption.

The only other movie I have ever seen that effects me as strongly is To Kill a Mockingbird. Both movies leave me feeling cleaner for having watched them.

I didn't intend to see this movie at all: I do not like prison movies and I don't normally watch them. I work at a branch library and one day as I was checking The Shawshank Redemption out to one of our older patrons, she said to me, "Whenever I feel down or depressed, I check out this movie and watch it and it always makes me feel better." At the time, I thought that was very strange. One day there was nothing on TV except things I absolutely would not watch under any circumstance or things that I had seen too many times already. I remembered what she said, so I watched it. I have watched it many many times since then and it gets better with every showing.

No action, no special effects - just men in prison uniforms talking to each other.

The Shawshank Redemption and To Kill a Mockingbird are the best movies I have ever seen. I do not judge it by it's technical merits - I don't really care about that. I have read that Citizen Kane or The Godfather or this or that movie is the best movie ever made. They may have the best technique or be the most influential motion pictures ever made, but not the best. The best movies are ones that touch the soul. It takes a movie like The Shawshank Redemption to touch the soul.

10.title: Unorginal Prison Fairytale my hairy foot!
10.content:
***SPOILERS*** ***SPOILERS*** Imagine me as an old man with a beard sitting on the stoep (porch) waving my cane at people passing by.

"How dare you call the Shawshank Redemption an unorginal prison fairytale! It is not supposed to be a run of the mill prison movie. Its not supposed to be The Birdman of Alcatraz! It's not supposed to be MIDNIGHT EXPRESS! It's not even supposed to be Stir Crazy, you wippersnappers! The prison is only the backdrop! It's about overcoming the odds when you are at your rope's end. This is a movie about hope and finding it in the darkest and dreariest of places.

"This movie could easily have been set in Nazi Germany in opressed Germany, in a concentration camp, in a 19th century work house! It's about breaking free from things that oppress us needlessly! (Spoiler starts here) Andy is the only person in prison that doesn't belong there! If he had done something bad he would have accepted it, but he didn't, so he tunnels through a wall to freedom. (Spoiler ends here).

"Sentimentalism can be bad in a movie if handled incorrectly, but Darabont uses it better than other Capra impersonators out there (even beating the Coens with their Hudsucker Proxy). And there is nothing wrong with sentimentality in The Shawshank Redemption. And I can't see what cliches you are talking about. Just because good things happen doesn't mean they cliches.

"This is a meditative movie. It's also has a lot of little things to enjoy for repeat viewing. So get off your high-horse and enjoy this movie.

"This is all I have to say."

Get back onto his chair and blows bubbles out of his pipe.

10.title: impressive
10.content: "The Shawshank Redemption" is a movie about time, patience and loyalty... Tim Robbins and Morgan Freeman are crucial to the story unfolds. This is not a "prison drama" in any conventional sense of the word. It is not about violence, riots or melodrama. The word "redemption" is in the title for a reason. The movie is based on a story, Rita Hayworth and the Shawshank Redemption, by Stephen King, which is quite unlike most of King's work. The horror here is not the supernatural kind, but the sort that flows from the realization of 10, 20, 30 years of a man's life unreeled in the same unchanging daily prison routine.

10.title: "The Shawshank Redemption" left an indelible mark on me.
10.content:
It's a powerful tapestry woven with friendship, hardship, hope, and dreams. But what truly elevates it is its ability to inspire. Despite the prison walls separating the characters from our world, their struggles resonate deeply.

The film's brilliance lies in its simplicity. Director Frank Darabont crafts a timeless message without resorting to flashy effects. The power lies in the raw performances and Morgan Freeman's captivating narration. While it may not have swept the Oscars, its place on IMDb's top 250 speaks volumes. Don't let awards sway you - trust the countless recommendations and its iconic status.

Invest a little over two hours tonight. Rent this movie, and you'll finally grasp why everyone raves about it. You might just discover your new favorite film.

10.title: Shawshank Redemption Dynamics
10.content:
The film The Shawshank Redemption is about Andy Dufresne, a prestigious banker ordered to serve time in prison for crimes he was found guilty of, however he claims that he has not committed. The film mainly follows Andy and his "friends' that he has made in prison around their day to day lives. From working in the prison or what is like to be in your cell by yourself at night, it also follows Andy through his plans and is most definitely brilliant and unbelievable escape.

Frank Darabont's The Shawshank Redemption is a film about hope and persistence and the rewards for being hopeful and persistent. Throughout this film the main character Andy Dufresne (Tim Robbins) shows that by being persistent and hopeful you can achieve whatever you want. Red (Morgan Freeman) is a character who plays the devil's advocate throughout the film; while he supports Andy and everything he does, he also manages to make it seem like his actions are pointless and a waste of time, however Andy did what he wanted and did not care what others thought, thus reinforcing the theme of persistence. The film uses Brooks (James Whitmore) actions to exemplify the decisions that are made when someone loses hope and does not have the persistence to move forward. The sound effects of this film are key to the added sense of realism and dimensionality of the film. Such as the background noises like small water droplets to the right up front noises like the slamming and locking of the prison cell doors. Other things such as background music are used to set the theme of the movie and the scene currently being viewed, while the background and foreground noises add depth and dimension to the film immersing the viewer and giving the sense of physically being there. Sounds like those of the prison cells, water droplets and the absolute silence of solitary confinement exemplify the theme because to survive all of that you have to have the determination, persistence and hope in order to move forward and survive. The director, Frank Darabont, used the cutting and duration of scenes in order to reinforce the theme and convey the emotions of the film. Such as when there is a dramatic/sad scene the panning is very slow and the scene last for an extended period of time with soft music playing in the background, thus providing the feeling of hopelessness, loss and sadness. On the other hand he also uses this technique to convey happy scenes in the film, such as when Andy's schemes went to plan, the scenes were very bright, usually with upbeat background music and were brightly lit. All in all this movie was done very well and tells the story while trying to immerse the viewer into the film. 10.title: My All Time Fav movie
10.content:
The Shawshank Redemption is a masterpiece of storytelling and cinematography. The film follows the life of Andy Dufresne, a banker who is wrongly convicted of murdering his wife and her lover, and sentenced to life imprisonment at Shawshank State Penitentiary. There, he meets Red, a seasoned inmate who becomes his friend and mentor. Together, they endure the harsh realities of prison life, while never losing hope of freedom.

The film is based on a novella by Stephen King, but transcends the genre of a typical prison drama. It explores themes such as friendship, justice, corruption, redemption, and the human spirit. The film is full of memorable scenes and dialogues, such as the iconic "Get busy living or get busy dying" quote, or the scene where Andy plays Mozart's music over the prison loudspeaker, giving a moment of beauty and joy to the inmates.

The performances by the cast are superb, especially by Tim Robbins and Morgan Freeman, who deliver nuanced and emotional portrayals of their characters. The film also features a brilliant score by Thomas Newman, and a stunning cinematography by Roger Deakins, who creates a contrast between the dark and oppressive prison and the bright and liberating outside world.

The Shawshank Redemption is a film that will stay with you long after you watch it. It is a film that celebrates the power of hope and the resilience of the human spirit. It is a film that deserves its place among the greatest films of all time.

10.title: Greatest Movie

Who can't identify with the conception of hope, truly the foundation of this picture. There is so much raw emotion, and the movie bears upon many. With such brilliant performances by the cast, and the amazing job done by Frank Darabont and co., the viewer becomes immersed in the film, and feels each of those emotions. It becomes a very personal experience that way.

I've not discussed this movie with anyone, at any length, that didn't love it. It is worthy of every bit of acclaim it continues to receive. I can't say that The Shawshank Redemption has changed my life as it has for some, but every time I watch it I'm drawn in again. And every time I run the emotional gamut it takes us through. It is the one film of which I will never tire.

-Jason Stanley

10.title: Why take anything away from the film, when it's that great
10.content:
For a long, long time I wondered what was really going on. 9.3 out of 10 possible points on the world's largest film database IMDb, even before classics like The Godfather Part 1 and 2 and leader of some best lists. Yet it's just about a convicted banker who befriends Morgan Freeman and gets used to his life as a prisoner in Shawshank men's prison. But there's a lot more to this film than the blue-eyed setting up of modern movie clichés.

For the crux of The Shawshank Redemption already lies in its ensemble. Tim Robbins and Morgan Freeman as the leading men in their absolute prime as actors. Secondary characters that integrate ideally into the scenarios of the protagonists and all have essential functions as their companions. Villains that seem generic from today's point of view, but for those times were unparalleled in cruelty. All of these ingeniously written roles have a hand in the plot, none of them feeling superfluous at any point. Of course, the film's trump card is the chemistry between Robbin's character Andy and Freeman's Red. After an initial distance, the two grow closer and closer as the film progresses, and within the nearly 30 years over which the plot takes place, they become almost inseparable. A down-to-earth and simple male friendship, where both of them share a terrible fate. How the two manage to carry each other through the cold harshness of prison life is gripping to follow. The individual scenes mainly belong to Robbin's Andy. This one is characterized by Red's over-voice and while this movie tool works in very few cases, it's a bull's eye here. It's not for nothing that Freeman's voice is considered iconic to this day. You have from the start that a man is telling his friend's story. Freeman's screen time suffers a bit as a result, but it doesn't take anything away from what is arguably the best performance of his career. Robbins delivers the much quieter and subtler performance, while Freeman excels in empathetic and even comedic monologues and dialogue at times. The rest of the cast adds to an all-around perfect ensemble performance. Foremost among them is Bob Gunton as the corrupt Warden Norton, under whose hypocritical posturing as a sensible Christian lurks a malicious layer that lends the film some (necessary) devastation.

Whether The Shawshank Redemption is really the best film of all time is debatable. However, one thing can't be denied: From an objective point of view, it is without major weaknesses. If anything, the slightly pathetic and conventional ending actually fits seamlessly with the previous plot. In this respect, this is perhaps a point of criticism, but merely one without much significance. Otherwise, it's a film that still did a lot to me at 22 years old, even 27 years later. The sensations of pain, shock and happiness regularly catch up with you. Despite its epic running length and slow build, the film is always entertaining and engaging, and it's also beautifully directed and photographed. Hard to find any flaws here.

10.title: Forget the IMDB Top 250 ranking- this is still a great movie.
10.content:
Is The Shawshank Redemption the second best movie of all time? No, it isn't. However, I contributed to its ranking by giving it a 10/10 vote. Yes, IMDB's Top 250 list is flawed in the sense that some of the greatest films ever made inspire some of the most violently negative reactions in a sizable contingent of the collective movie-viewing public (thereby rendering them ineligible for the highest overall voting average). The Shawshank Redemption, however, clearly did not evoke many negative reactions- should the film be faulted for that?

Absolutely not, I say. This is a grand movie that strikes one fundamentally real and basic existential chord, namely the abstraction of faith and hope within the context of the tremendous pain and frustration humanity inflicts upon itself. Faith does not have to be of a religious nature, and The Shawshank Redemption doesn't go there (this is why I love it, but abhor The Green Mile). Rather, the faith of Shawshank is a stubborn, earthly, human faith, that despite the arbitrary injustice of existence, the individual can persevere and affirm within himself or herself that yes, life is worth living. For my money, that is solid return on two hours of my time.

I am a cynic and a misanthrope, supremely so on both counts. That said, I acknowledge that I have no choice but to accept the context of my existence for what it is, and I can either "get busy living or get busy dying." Apparently, most people agree on some level.

10.title: The Shawshank Redemption: A Timeless Masterpiece
10.content:
"The Shawshank Redemption" is a cinematic triumph that transcends the boundaries of genre and era. Adapted from Stephen King's novella, this film weaves a spellbinding narrative of hope, resilience, and the enduring power of the human spirit.

Set within the confines of Shawshank State Penitentiary, the film follows the journey of Andy Dufresne, a banker wrongfully convicted of murder, and his unlikely friendship with fellow inmate Red. As the story unfolds, we are drawn into a world of injustice and oppression, where hope flickers like a distant beacon in the darkest of nights.

What sets "The Shawshank Redemption" apart is its unwavering commitment to authenticity and emotional depth. Every frame is imbued with a sense of raw honesty, capturing the pain and longing of its characters with unflinching precision.

At the heart of the film lies the transformative power of friendship and the indomitable human spirit. Andy and Red's bond transcends the confines of their prison walls, offering solace and redemption in the most unlikely of places.

Director Frank Darabont's masterful storytelling is complemented by stellar performances from Tim Robbins and Morgan Freeman, who breathe life into their respective roles with a rare blend of nuance and gravitas. Their on-screen chemistry is nothing short of mesmerizing, elevating "The Shawshank Redemption" to a level of cinematic greatness rarely achieved.

As the story reaches its poignant conclusion, we are reminded that hope is a force more powerful than any prison bars or shackles of injustice. "The Shawshank Redemption" is a timeless masterpiece that continues to inspire and uplift audiences around the world, proving that even in the darkest of times, there is always light at the end of the tunnel.

I've seen this movie about a half-dozen times now, and it's slowly occurred to me that this is one of my two or three very favorite films. Each time I've seen it, I can appreciate different things about it, and the depth of the dialogue, and the meaning behind the events and characters takes on different symbolism and significance.

Having just read the story this was based on, I find it a rare example of where the film is better than the book. Not that the book isn't good, but there are some significant changes in the film that helped to make it such an endearing piece of work, and a more powerful experience than the original short story was. The development of the characters of the warden, and Brooks, for example, really fleshes out the story well.

The acting and direction is perfectly subtle and restrained, and though the feel may be a bit slow at times for some people, it gives a good sense of the feeling of time slowly dripping by in these people's lives.

What a shame that this was nominated for so many Academy Awards, including Best Picture, Actor (Morgan Freeman), and adapted screenplay, cinematography, music, etc., but didn't win anything. Granted, "Forrest Gump" is a great film, too, but it would have been nice if "Shawshank" had at least won something. Oh, well, that's not really important in the big picture, I suppose. The fact that this film is ranked #2 of all time here is very telling, and I'm sure it will be appreciated for a very long time to come... I know that every time it comes on TNT, I have to watch it again!

10.title: The Best Movie In A Long, Long Time.
10.content:
If you're sitting there, like I was a few hours ago; thinking that this film doesn't deserve to be called the Greatest Film of All Time, as IMDb has it placed, then do yourself a favor and watch it first.

I thought this was a popular vote that had no basis in reality, like how people call a new- age pop band the "best band ever". I was wrong. Very, very wrong.

I'm not here to tell you that this is the best movie ever made, I can't do that. Movies are about the meaning they have to your life and one's personal experience defines what you relate to, thus that title will always be different for each individual, but what I can do is tell you about the effect it had on me.

First and foremost this is a story about hope. It's not a story about crime & prison, if you adhere to this interpretation then you're not looking deep enough into the themes of the film. Yes, Mr. King uses the story of Andy to communicate his messages, but the narration itself is entirely superficial, this could have just as easily been a story about war, but the conduit he uses is fairly well suited to his goal.

The acting is superb, I couldn't think of a better suited cast. Tim Robbins is fantastic as Andy (The main character), and Morgan Freeman is just as good as his friend. The last time I saw acting this good was in The Godfather. You feel for the characters, not only because of the superb acting but also because the character development is so subtle and concise that by the end of the film you feel as if you've known them all your life.

I'll elaborate on the allegory portrayed. The film explores such areas as corruption, religion, hope, love & integrity. King suggests that hope is the most important thing in life, and those who have lost it ultimately decay into a sea of mediocrity (as shown through contrast between Brooks & Red). This was the theme I found most interesting and applicable to my life, but the rest are equally as touching. Notice the difference in behavior between those who are religious and those who are not, King hints at a perceived justification for evil in the contrast between Andy & the Warden.

Integrity is also portrayed as something delicate and somewhat essential to happiness, like hope. King shows this mainly through the actions of Andy, as embodied in the quote "The funny thing is - on the outside, I was an honest man, straight as an arrow. I had to come to prison to be a crook." (That was not a spoiler, it's fairly obvious that he goes to prison, just by looking at the synopsis)

I don't wish to get into the story too much, just keep these themes in mind when you watch the movie and you'll find it infinitely more rewarding.

In conclusion, The Shawshank Redemption is the best film of the past 20 years, and while it perhaps doesn't deserve that top spot (I'm still deciding, but I doubt I can convince myself to concede it does), it is still an essential movie in my collection and I wouldn't give it up for anything. It's right up there with The Godfather and The Good, The Bad & The Ugly.

Themes: 100% - Perhaps the best film ever made in this regard.

Acting: 96% - Fabulous performances all round, characters don't age much though.

Story: 98% - A classic, the best King adaption by far.

Lasting appeal: 99% - The only film you can watch 100 times and discover something new each sit through.

Influence: 92% - Watch it and you'll realize how ripped off it's been.

Overall: 98% - It doesn't get much better than that.

10.title: A heart-felt movie on friendship!
10.content:
Absolutely amazing movie. A must watch! This movie is based on a novella by Stephen King, but don't let that put you off. It's not a horror film, rather a thumpingly good ode to friendship, hope, wit, wiles and wisdom, brimming with crackling characters and topped with the most twisteroo of twists since The Crying Game. Found guilty of killing his unfaithful wife and her lover in a fit of passion, sullen accountant Andy Dufresne (Robbins, casting off his goofball image to display more layers than the proverbial onion) is shipped to the gothic wind-swept corridors of the Shawshank State Prison for life. It is here the movie gracefully unfolds. With a beautifully rounded script, writer/director Darabont conjures up a spellbinding personal odyssey stretching through the years from 1946 to 1967.

Dufresne, all the while protesting his innocence, slowly overcomes the hellfire tortures of the prison system - an unblinking range of beatings, rapings and abject humiliations - while managing to inspire his fellow inmates to lift their degraded horizons. Among them is Red (Freeman, in a matchless supporting role), the lifer who can, given time, provide virtually anything. And for reasons best known to himself, Dufresne requires 40s starlet Rita Hayworth, provisioned in poster form.

The mood swings rigorously through every emotion as the cranky, wiseguy and downright crazed array of criminals bare the brunt of the turbulent life within the doomy Shawshank catacomb. Then it gets really mean, gearing up for its injury-time shockers. Dufresne, a whiz with figures, is bullied into running the warden's (Gunton) petty accounting scams, giving him the chance to execute his and the film's final, greatest miracle.
