9.title: Hope will endure
9.content:
When the odds are against you, there's only moving forward or turning back. When Andy Dufresne (Tim Robbins) is sent to one of the toughest prisons for two consecutive life sentences for murders he did not commit, the mere thought is enough to make anyone insane. Prison life is tough, but Shawshank prison gets the cake for displaying just how harsh it can be. Corrupt guards, brash punishments and bare minimum accommodations are only half the picture. Just as soon as he's about to break, he makes a discovery that requires incredibly true determination and hope. The Shawshank Redemption is a screenplay adaptation of Stephen King's novella; Rita Hayworth and Shawshank Redemption. Writer and Director Frank Darabont was able to capture a realistic representation of what prison life might have looked like in the first half of the 20th century. Although the budget was very modest for this film, it really looks like they didn't need anymore. A cast that consists of veteran actors helps to meld the film's respect with their performances. One very noteworthy performance was from Morgan Freeman's character: Ellis Boyd (Red). He was also the one who narrated most of the film and that's always a treat for the audience.

Thomas Newman who was responsible for the soundtrack did a great job enhancing the scenes whether it is eerie or joyous. Although at times I felt that there needed to be a more powerful theme to reflect the scene which fortunately was only in a few scenes. Nevertheless, the captivating themes are something to remember in this film. Memorable characters, a great soundtrack and an excellent plot all make this a highly recommended movie to watch. There really isn't much to nit-pick about this film which is what really brings it to the top. Like all highly rated/regarded films, there tends to be some form of overrating which is understandable, since all great things attract jealousy.

9.title: A fantastic piece of film making that stands the test of time.
9.content: What is there to say about The Shawshank Redemption? Clearly there is a reason for it's widespread popularity, and thankfully that praise is warranted. While far from the best film I've ever seen (it currently holds the #1 spot on IMDb), I can't argue against it being a great film. In particular, the performances by Tim Robbins and Morgan Freeman are inspiring enough to power the film through it's slower passages. The cinematography has been praised for good reason as well, a lot of thought was obviously put into every shot to convey a certain feeling or message. Although I found the story arc to be somewhat predictable, the art of storytelling is the real star here, guiding us through themes that are masterfully simple on the surface, but have a lot going on underneath for you to think about later on. Really the only thing that held this film back for me is it's reliance on some rather cliché (at least at this point in time) plot developments amidst it's middle act. Being objective though, it's hard to tell whether that is the fault of the way it was crafted, or just the result of the film being so broad in it's scope. Either way, it stands the test of time as a film very much worth viewing. Maybe we have been looking at Shawshank all wrong. Maybe it's not so amazing because of how many people think it's great, maybe it's because of how few people there are that don't. It certainly has a message that everyone can appreciate.

Review from Roger Ebert: There are key moments in the film, as when Andy uses his clout to get some cold beers for his friends who are working on a roofing job. Or when he befriends the old prison librarian (James Whitmore). Or when he oversteps his boundaries and is thrown into solitary confinement. What quietly amazes everyone in the prison -- and us, too -- is the way he accepts the good and the bad as all part of some larger pattern than only he can fully see.

The partnership between the characters played by Tim Robbins and Morgan Freeman is crucial to the way the story unfolds. This is not a "prison drama" in any conventional sense of the word. It is not about violence, riots or melodrama. The word "redemption" is in the title for a reason. 9.title: super
9.content: The short novel by Stephen King has been adapted by Owen O'Neill and Dave Johns and is likely to prove popular with fans of the film as well as those who are too young to remember the original format. Based on the 1982 novella Rita Hayworth and The Shawshank Redemption, the play examines desperation, injustice, friendship and hope behind the bars of a maximum security facility. The 1994 feature film, regularly voted Britain's favourite ever movie, starred Tim Robbins and Morgan Freeman and was nominated for seven Academy Awards. Two of TV's best loved leading men, Ian Kelsey (Doctors, Casualty and Emmerdale) and Patrick Robinson (Casualty, Midsomer Murders), star in this new production of The Shawshank Redemption, which is running at Milton Keynes Theatre until Saturday. Despite protests of his innocence, Andy Dufresne is handed a double life sentence for the brutal murder of his wife and her lover. Incarcerated at the notorious Shawshank facility, he quickly learns that no one can survive alone. Andy strikes up an unlikely friendship with the prison fixer Red, and things take a slight turn for the better. However, when Warden Stammas decides to bully Andy into subservience and exploit his talents for accountancy, a desperate plan is quietly hatched. A minimalist set is the perfect backdrop as the story unfolds in the confines of the prison walls. Dim lighting with the sound of doors slamming and keys turning makes you feel as though you were inside the 'Shank' with the inmates. The onstage partnership of Kelsey and Robinson has a genuine warmth to it, and this is complimented by their co-stars who bring both light and shade to the performance. No one can miss the distinctive laugh of Rooster, wonderfully but hauntingly captured by Leigh Jones, and Ian Barritt as Brooksie and George Evans as Tommy Williams shine in their 'darkest' moments. Owen O'Neill is perfect for the role of Warden Stammas, chillingly bringing a sense of fear to the stage every time he features. With the film's cult status, some die-hard fans may not like the fast-pace of the stage adaptation, which takes you through the years inside at a much quicker pace than the original film. But there is no harm in breathing new life into a classic and if you loved the film, why not indulge yourself in re-living it in a new format. The show contains strong language and adult content and is recommended for people aged 15 and over.

9.title: nice film tbh

I'm trying to save you money; this is the last film title that you should consider borrowing. Renting Shawshank will cost you five bucks... just plunk down the $25 and own the title. You'll wind up going back to this gem time and time again. This is one of few movies that are truly timeless. And it's entertaining and moving, no matter how many times you view it.

Forget about what others (including myself) might suggest you'll discover in "The Shawshank Redemption;" when you watch it, you'll identify something very personal in your own life with a scene, a character, or a moment in this uncomplicated movie. When you need hope, you'll look for Shawshank. When you want to believe in the will of overcoming even the greatest obstacles, Shawshank will uplift you in ways that you can't find in movies today.

Some liken the film to some kind of spiritual awakening. Of course, some can go to a church or mosque to find enlightenment and Faith in humanity, but most places of worship are open only certain days or times. But when you need affirmation of the lasting bond of friendships that prevail over the most dire circumstances, Shawshank will give it to you. It makes grown men (like me) cry, still. I wonder whether Shawshank was truly meant for viewing in the privacy of the home, because it is a personal experience that really makes you look inward. Nominated for seven, this is the best film that never one a single Oscar.

How ironic that an innocent man winds up being surrounded by the corruption of the legal system. Shawshank itself is similar to the character of Andy Dufresne. Prejudging this classic film, critics couldn't get past the title. The public followed suit, initially dismissing Shawshank, which failed in the box office just like "It's a Wonderful Life" and "Citizen Kane." It could have just whithered away on the store shelves, like Andy Dufresne could have in his own cell. But the characters prevailed, because Andy -- And Shawshank -- stayed true. Now, these movies are right up there as the most popular films of all time.

Anyone who has yet to watch Shawshank may be so jaded of movies, or the film's title, or how a 2-1/2- hour movie set inside the walls of a prison can manage to tap the soul of such a wide range of people. Shawshank has not one explosion. I wonder if it even has a single special effect or digitally- enhanced frame.

But every aspect of Shawshank fit together. The acting from the top to the bit part. The musical score. The editing. The photography. The story, from opening credits to final scene. All involved, including the town of Mansfield, Ohio (where Shawshank was actually filmed) played their roles perfectly. Shawshank is a must- see, must- own title.

9.title: A Timeless Tale of Hope and Redemption
9.content:
The Shawshank Redemption is a cinematic masterpiece that has captivated audiences for decades. This poignant drama, directed by Frank Darabont, delves into the depths of human resilience, the power of hope, and the enduring bonds of friendship. Set within the confines of Shawshank State Penitentiary, the film follows the story of Andy Dufresne (Tim Robbins), a banker wrongfully convicted of murder, and his unlikely friendship with Red (Morgan Freeman), a seasoned inmate.

One of the film's greatest strengths lies in its ability to create a richly detailed world within the prison walls. Darabont masterfully captures the harsh realities of prison life, from the oppressive regime of the guards to the camaraderie among inmates. The bleakness of the setting is juxtaposed with moments of quiet beauty and unexpected humor, adding depth and nuance to the narrative.

Tim Robbins delivers a powerful performance as Andy Dufresne, a man who never loses his spirit, even in the face of adversity. His portrayal of a man wrongfully imprisoned is both heartbreaking and inspiring. Morgan Freeman, as the wise and worldly Red, provides a steady anchor to the film, his narration guiding the audience through the story with a sense of both weariness and hope.

The film's exploration of themes such as hope, redemption, and the human spirit is both profound and timeless. Andy's unwavering belief in his own innocence and his determination to find a way out of Shawshank serve as a beacon of hope for both himself and those around him. Red's gradual transformation from a cynical inmate to a man capable of love and compassion is equally moving.

The film's pacing is deliberate, allowing the story to unfold at a measured pace. This deliberate approach allows the audience to fully immerse themselves in the world of Shawshank and connect with the characters on a deeper level. The film's climax, a thrilling and suspenseful escape, is a testament to the power of human ingenuity and the enduring nature of hope.

The Shawshank Redemption is a film that resonates with audiences on a profound level. Its exploration of universal themes, combined with its stellar performances and masterful direction, has solidified its place as one of the greatest films of all time. It is a film that will continue to inspire and move audiences for generations to come.

Key Themes and Analysis

Hope and Perseverance: Andy's unwavering belief in his innocence and his determination to find a way out of Shawshank serve as a powerful testament to the human spirit. His ability to maintain hope in the face of adversity inspires others to never give up.

Friendship and Redemption: The bond between Andy and Red is one of the most heartwarming aspects of the film. Their friendship transcends the harsh realities of prison life and provides a source of solace and support for both men.

The Power of Knowledge: Andy's pursuit of knowledge and his ability to use it to his advantage highlights the transformative power of education. His self-education not only helps him to survive but also empowers him to take control of his own destiny.

The Nature of Time: The film's exploration of the passage of time and the impact it has on individuals is a poignant reminder of the fleeting nature of life. The cyclical nature of the seasons mirrors the cyclical nature of human existence, emphasizing the importance of living in the present moment.

The Importance of Human Connection: The film underscores the importance of human connection and the power of empathy. The relationships between the inmates, as well as between the inmates and the guards, highlight the complexities of human nature and the potential for both good and evil.

Cinematography and Sound Design

The film's cinematography is stunning, capturing the bleak beauty of the prison setting and the lushness of the natural world outside. The use of color and light is particularly effective, highlighting the stark contrast between the confined world of Shawshank and the freedom of the outside world.

The sound design is equally impressive, creating a sense of both isolation and community. The haunting score, composed by Thomas Newman, perfectly complements the film's mood and adds to its emotional impact.

Conclusion

The Shawshank Redemption is a timeless masterpiece that continues to resonate with audiences of all ages. Its exploration of universal themes, combined with its powerful performances and stunning cinematography, makes it a truly unforgettable cinematic experience. It is a film that will stay with you long after the credits roll, reminding you of the power of hope, the importance of friendship, and the enduring nature of the human spirit.

9.title: Flawless Story-Telling
9.content:
Hope. It is the single most powerful human emotion. It can keep you alive, and it can destroy your life. Hope can be the one thing left in a world where everything else is taken from you- and The Shawshank Redemption is the perfect artistic visualization of the tremendous power that hope can have over someone who has lost everything else.

The opening scene introduces us to a young and successful banker named Andy Dufresne, and the things that have transpired to destroy his life. We can't help but feel sympathy toward a man who finds out that his wife is having an affair, and then gets convicted for the double homicide of his wife and her lover- when he is innocent of the crime. Taken to Shawshank prison for two life sentences, Andy has had his entire life taken from him in a spiral of terrible events. It only gets worse at the prison, as the brutality of the prison guards is unbridled, and a few inmates make his life hell. However, Andy continually surprises the audience with his resilience and his character finds ways to amaze the inmates, the guards, the warden, and the audience. The story itself is not wholly original or groundbreaking, and there is no 'surprise-ending' or major twists that come out of nowhere to shock the audience. However, it is in the delivery of the story that this film excels beyond all others.

Every aspect of this movie compliments the incredible script written by Frank Darabont that was based on Stephen King's novella. The music is a composition of slow-moving and peaceful ballads that bring out just how long-winded a life sentence in prison can be, and how undaunted Andy is by the terrible environment he is in. The cameras move slowly and steadily, repeatedly scanning the prison and also emphasizing the endless span that life in prison truly is. On the artistic side, the movie is something to behold. But ultimately, what brings the entire movie together is the beautifully written and exceptionally delivered narration of Morgan Freeman, playing a fellow inmate named Ellis 'Red' Redding. Not only are we given a view into Andy's character through this man's observations, but we also see how Red himself changes his life as a result of Andy Dufresne.

The amazing thing about this film is how every detail in the entire movie somehow contributes to the story on the whole. It takes a few times of viewing before you can really appreciate just how intricate the plot is- how every single moment helps increase the power of the incredible ending sequence. It is not too complex, with many tangents that end up confusing the viewer. Instead, it runs with a simple theme and adds to it with everything that is depicted. The only negative thing I have to say about this movie is that the ending seems a bit drawn out, but by this time you are so enthralled and satisfied as a viewer that it should not pose a problem.

A great story, told flawlessly, with a powerful message. There is not a lot more that you could ask for in a movie. Entertaining and inspiring. Deep, yet not complicated. A message delivered with undeniable power, and an excellent movie experience overall. If you have ever felt like everything has been taken from you, then learn from Andy Dufresne. 'There's something inside that they can't get to, that they can't touch. It's yours.' Hope. It can set you free.

9.title: A Compelling Film
9.content:
My Rating: ***1/2 out of ****.

Spoilers

In many ways, I am more than a little shocked at the overwhelming popularity of The Shawshank Redemption. I am not in anyway saying that it is a bad film, in fact its a great film. However, I never thought Shawshank would appeal to so many people. It just seems odd that it has received over 112,000 votes (More than the Godfather) and it is #2 on the Imdb top 250 list. I do not think it deserves this high position but it is nice to see the film get alot of notice.

Shawshank deserves high marks in these categories: Directing, Acting, Cinematography, and Writing. This was the debut feature for Frank Darabont and he chooses to let Shawshank unravel at a slow pace. This is the perfect choice for the film. It moves slow but it is nevertheless compelling. There is only one time when the slow pace actually interferes with the film.

Darabont also gets some highly impressive from his cast. Tim Robbins gives a strong, subdued performance. Morgan Freeman, who was nominated for a Best Actor Oscar, does an equally strong job here. The chemistry between them is effective too.

As strong as the two leads are, they do not outshine the supporting cast. All of them are excellent but two of them deserve to be singled out. James Whitmore gives a brilliantly moving performance. Bob Gunton also deserves mention as the warden in charge of Shawshank.

Cinematographer Roger Deakins should be given a lot of credit. He finds the perfect mood for the film. Shawshank is not a colorful place at all. He creates a dreary atmosphere that fits the film perfectly. There alot of uses of the color, gray that is used to create this atmosphere.

9.title: The Best Film from a Stephen King Novel
9.content:
'I wish that I could tell you that Andy fought the good fightand the Sisters let him be. I wish I could tell you thatbut prison is no fairy-tale world.' This quote nicely sums up The Shawshank Redemption, a film that earnestly shows the violent life in prison, but chooses not to focus on the violence, rather using it to portray emotion.

Andy Dufresne (Tim Robbins), a successful banker, is convicted for the murder of his wife and her lover. The judge describes Andy as cold and sends him to the Shawshank prison to serve two life sentences. Andy, however, maintains his innocence, despite the fact that he was seen at the murder scene carrying a weapon.

In prison, Andy eventually gains the respect of his inmates, including the influential prisoner 'Red' (Morgan Freeman) who 'gets things' for the prisoners. Later, Andy's knowledge of finance gains him popularity with the cruel prison guards and the Warden (Bob Gunton).

The development of the friendship between Red and Andy is one of the focal points of the film as each man learns from the other. Several subplots are nicely intertwined into the film, none better than the story of old Brooks Hatlen (James Whitmore) and his release from prison. Having spent so much time at Shawshank, Brooks has become 'institutionalised' i.e. so attached to prison that he cannot cope in the outside world. The sense of helplessness and solitude Brooks feels when released is one of the films most genuinely emotional moments.

The plot of the movie is solid, and while it encompasses some 20 years, it transitions well and never really feels slow. Credit for this must go to screenwriter Frank Darabont who nicely adapts Stephen King's novel to the big screen.

The entire cast of the movie gives standout performances, led by Robbins. Robbins portrays Andy beautifully throughout the film, especially with his facial expressions. His eyes are incredibly focused and haunting throughout and he often wears a smile on his face that belies his situation. Freeman does well as Red, playing him with confidence and a sense of despair at the same time.

Visually the film opts for a very grey tone that fits in with the dreary feel of the prison and the prisoners. It also succeeds in helping Andy to stick out, as his hope and demeanour contradict the tone.

The Shawshank Redemption is a truly beautiful film, easily one of the best of the 90's, filled with a great story, acting, emotion and a series of memorable quotes.

9.title: Watch it at least once
9.content:
The Shawshank Redemption was a hard watch at times. We know prison is far from glamorous, so I couldn't imagine the conditions in the 1940s.

An institution supposedly designed to rehabilitate, but is a total ruse. The parallels between the cruel warden and prison guards versus the charming and endearing prisoners, makes you wonder who really belongs in jail.

Not entirely far from the truth. Prisons are usually privately owned, and it just goes to show how warped the whole system is.

Psychopaths being put in charge of troubled people. It really doesn't make much sense. But the movie shows the hypocrisy of it all.

I enjoyed the heartwarming moments between the inmates that reminded us that they are people too. And that people are flawed. This doesn't condone crimes, but we don't know the full story behind some of these characters. And I doubt they were as thorough with background checks then. So many of these people could have been in the wrong place at the wrong time.

Who knows what led them to their decisions. Red made a great points when faced against the panel for the last time. And the movie really shows the psychological damage that being locked away in such an environment would do. "These walls are funny".

Brooks' story bothered me more than I was expecting. They lock these people away, expect them to live in these conditions for years and become puzzled when they find it hard to cope with the real world. It's sad.

They are considered free, but what even is freedom at that point? When everything you've known, your social circle and daily routine that you've adapted to is taken away?

I think what also made this movie great was that it ended up answering all my questions. The ending couldn't have been more satisfying. There is hope, because anything can change at any time. You never know.

My biggest take away from this movie is to judge less. You don't know someone's full story.

If you don't have all the details, don't judge.

9.title: The Shawshank Redemption
9.content:
"The Shawshank Redemption" stands as a timeless classic in the realm of cinema, a film that resonates deeply with audiences across generations. Directed by Frank Darabont and based on Stephen King's novella, it is a masterclass in storytelling, filled with poignant themes, unforgettable characters, and stellar performances.

Set within the walls of Shawshank State Penitentiary, the film follows the journey of Andy Dufresne, a banker wrongly convicted of murder and sentenced to life behind bars. As Andy navigates the harsh realities of prison life, he forms an unlikely friendship with Red, a seasoned inmate and narrator of the story, played with remarkable depth by Morgan Freeman. Through their bond, "The Shawshank Redemption" explores themes of hope, resilience, and the enduring power of the human spirit.

At its core, the film is a testament to the indomitable nature of hope. Despite the grim circumstances of his imprisonment, Andy refuses to succumb to despair, finding solace in acts of defiance, small triumphs, and the pursuit of knowledge. Tim Robbins delivers a tour de force performance as Andy, capturing the character's quiet determination and inner strength with remarkable nuance. Robbins infuses Andy with a sense of dignity and grace that is both inspiring and deeply moving, making him a character that lingers in the minds of audiences long after the credits roll.

Opposite Robbins, Morgan Freeman delivers a performance of equal brilliance as Red, the film's narrator and Andy's closest confidant. Freeman's gravelly voice and world-weary demeanor imbue Red with a sense of wisdom and perspective that anchors the film's narrative. As Andy's steadfast ally, Red serves as a symbol of resilience and redemption, embodying the belief that no prison bars can contain the human spirit.

Director Frank Darabont demonstrates a keen eye for detail and a deft hand at storytelling, crafting a film that is both visually stunning and emotionally resonant. From the bleak confines of Shawshank's walls to the sweeping vistas of freedom, Darabont's cinematography captures the essence of Andy's journey with haunting beauty. Each frame is imbued with a sense of atmosphere and emotion, drawing the audience deeper into the world of the film.

"The Shawshank Redemption" is also notable for its stellar supporting cast, including the likes of Bob Gunton as the corrupt warden Norton, William Sadler as the tragic Brooks, and Clancy Brown as the sadistic Captain Hadley. Each actor brings depth and complexity to their roles, elevating the film beyond the confines of its genre.

But perhaps the most enduring legacy of "The Shawshank Redemption" lies in its universal appeal and timeless themes. At its heart, the film is a celebration of the human spirit's capacity to endure and overcome even the greatest of adversities. It speaks to the power of friendship, the importance of hope, and the transformative nature of redemption.

In conclusion, "The Shawshank Redemption" is a cinematic masterpiece that continues to captivate audiences decades after its release. With its powerful performances, poignant themes, and masterful direction, it is a film that transcends the boundaries of its genre to become something truly extraordinary. For these reasons and more, it deserves every bit of its status as one of the greatest films ever made.

"The Shawshank Redemption" is a timeless classic that follows the journey of Andy Dufresne, a banker wrongly convicted of murder and sentenced to life in Shawshank State Penitentiary. Through his friendship with Red, Andy finds hope and resilience amidst the harsh realities of prison life. Directed by Frank Darabont and featuring stellar performances by Tim Robbins and Morgan Freeman, the film is a poignant exploration of the human spirit's capacity to endure and overcome even the greatest of adversities. With its universal themes of hope, friendship, and redemption, "The Shawshank Redemption" remains a cinematic masterpiece that continues to resonate with audiences worldwide.

9.title: Masterpiece, isn't it?
9.content:
"The Shawshank Redemption" is a film that undoubtedly leaves an impression and deserves the viewer's attention. However, despite its popularity and a rating of 9 out of 10, there are a few aspects that could have been improved.

Firstly, the predictability of the plot is noteworthy. Although the story of a prisoner finding hope and freedom through sheer willpower is compelling, it gives off a sense of set-piece scenarios and anticipated plot twists. The viewer may sense a certain degree of cliché in the unfolding events.

Additionally, the characters, while well-played, sometimes appear too stereotypical. The relationships between them, though emotional, could have been deeper and more unexpected, adding an extra layer of complexity to the film.

Moreover, the time and place stylization, while atmospheric, can at times feel overused and lose its freshness due to numerous similar works.

Despite these observations, "The Shawshank Redemption" remains a vivid representative of the film industry, impressing with its storytelling strength and human themes. While deserving of a high rating, the film lacks some innovation to become a truly unexpected masterpiece.

Every technical element of the film is spot-on, from direction to music, editing, and acting; Morgan Freeman delivers his best ever performance whilst Tim Robbins shows us what a great character actor he is. Even better, for a genre fan like me, is seeing acting favourites like Clancy Brown, William Sadler, Brian Libby, and James Whitmore all appearing in the film together and playing more than just stock good or bad guy roles. Every actor is great here, and the script (which sticks closely to King's writing) is nigh-on perfect. Emotion, thrills, drama, and the triumph of the human spirit are all present in this movie, which is one of the greatest prison flicks ever.

9.title: You'd be Obtuse not to Appreciate This Fable
9.content:
This film, a modern fable, is an amazing success story - not in monetary terms, but in terms of reputation. It began as just another of many dramas, in this case based on a Stephen King story, and has emerged as possibly the best film of the decade, the '90s (#2 of the IMDb top 250 as of this writing, right up there with The Godfather!). The story begins as another prison drama but gradually metamorphoses into a poetic commentary on friendship and the scope of life. The main character (Robbins) is sent to prison in the late forties for supposedly murdering his wife. It really is a men's picture; there are literally no female characters (the wife appears for a few seconds early on in flashback and that's about it, besides a complaining shopper later; oh, and, of course, Rita Hayworth pops in as herself). The film holds many surprises in store for the viewer as the story progresses, not the least of which is the subtle revelation, towards the end, that the main character may just be Freeman's (how appropriate is that name!). If one had to pick one reason for this film's success (and there are probably several), it's that it's probably the best depiction of friendship between men on celluloid - no cutesy buddy-buddy stuff, no homo-erotic connotations - just a solid, adult basis for two men to bond over and remain friends.

But there are many other, I dare say, cool aspects to the film. Most everyone who has seen this has at least two or three favorite scenes which they remember forever and which they watch over and over. My personal favorite is the one on the roof, where Andy (Robbins) makes his bid for a slightly better existence, taking a big risk with the captain of the guards (Clancy Brown, always intimidating). It's a turning point in the picture and shows two important matters recurring through it: taking a risk and using your intelligence. Andy turns out to be very smart; he's always using his head. And the ultimate switchback of the picture, the comeuppance of the evil warden (Bob Gunton, excellent as scum dressed in pricey suits), shows you that a film doesn't need a standard shootout to depict the ultimate justice or retribution. No, if you use your brains, you can really get back at those oppressive forces seeking to dehumanize you, abuse you, and lord over you. Boy, can you get them back. I mean really - has there ever been a bigger turnaround in the history of cinema? OK, maybe this is why this film is rated so high - you just can't get a better release from frustration than this, not on film. Here, payback isn't just a bitch - she's the daughter of Satan sent to take you to hell.

Another thing to mention is that this film covers about 20 years of time. That's a long stretch. The film itself is over 2 hours running time. Most films, even the best ones, with so much to cover, can't help but sag in places, especially historical pieces. But that's not the case here. Writer-director Darabont, who also worked on the even longer "The Green Mile" later, shows us how to create films which are always interesting to watch, whether at the one hour or 2-hour mark. Or am I being obtuse?

9.title: "Get busy living, or get busy dying." - Andy Dufresne
9.content:
This work from 1994 directed and written by a Hungarian-American Frank Darabont that was based on Stephen King's novella Rita Hayworth and Shawshank Redemption was nominated for several highly appreciated awards, including The Academy Awards and The Golden Globe Awards. In spite of being nominated for so many prestigious prizes, it did not win any. However, this fact cannot put a shadow over the fantastic job that was done while making the movie. Critics from all over the world were absolutely amazed by the drama with outstanding and unbelievably realistic scenery. It is simply a must to pay a great respect to the main protagonists – experienced Morgan Freeman as Red, a man who will provide you with everything you need, and irreplaceable Tim Robbins as Andy Dufresne, a banker who was unjustly convicted of murdering his wife and her lover.

The story starts in the late 1940's when a banker Andy Dufresne is sentenced to two consecutive life sentences at the Shawshank State Penitentiary for murdering his wife and her lover. He instantly becomes a friend with a contraband smuggler and the film's narrator Ellis "Red" Redding who procures a rock hammer for Andy so he can create small stone chess pieces. Soon, Andy unleashes his financial skills when he overhears the merciless guard chief Hadley complaining about taxes. Thanks to his former occupation, Andy is given a position in the library so he can manage financial matters for Shawshank. As the years pass, Norton, the head of the prison, uses the library and public works worked by prison labor to undercut skilled labor costs so he can receive huge kickbacks. Andy is used for laundering the money using the alias "Randall Stephens". In the mid-1960's young Tommy Williams, an irredeemable burglar, is imprisoned. He gets close with Andy and Red and when hearing the details of Andy's case begins to talk about his former inmate. He explains that the inmate told him how he had killed two people and got away with it which seems to be a proof of Andy's innocence. Unfortunately, as soon as Norton hears a word about it, he has young Tommy shot by Hadley. This appears to be enough for Andy. He tells Red about his secret dream of living in a Mexican coastal village and instructs him how to get there when he is free. The next day, Andy's cell is found empty. Norton and the guards find out that Andy escaped through a tunnel which he had dug with his rock hammer over the previous two decades. While they are searching for him, Andy, as Randall Stephens, visits a large number of banks to withdraw the laundered money. Besides that, he sends a package with evidence of what has happened at the prison to a regional newspaper. Will the police and the newspaper trust Andy? Will he and Red ever meet again? Go and watch the bravura ending.

It is hard to find a more proper word for the film than a masterpiece. The Shawshank Redemption is an opportunity to witness how fate is the best judge in the end, how a frightened cat can turn into a brave lion and how a friendship can be developed even in the darkest moments of ones' lives. Next, I was really impressed by the perfect narrating skills of Mr. Freeman. The actor's storytelling keeps you deeply settled in your seat and you are able to literally breathe the story. I haven't seen such a well-thought-out plot like this in a long time. The diligent work of the producers, cameramen, costume designers, make-up and hair stylists and all of the crew will be remembered. I can't write this without mentioning the set. I have already talked about it, but I need to praise it a little bit more. It was so easy to get into the plot thanks to the set – you do not get a chance to doubt the realism of the scenery. Another aspect to be spotlighted is the soundtrack. Magnificent Thomas Newman and his team produced a piece of quality material which does not stay unnoticed and bonds you even more with the whole drama. Last but not least, I must applaud the directing and screen writing of Mr. Darabont who created a completely unique and new experience for TV viewers and cinema audiences. We can only guess what happens in the end until we finally get to see the finish line of Shawshank. I guarantee you will end up with a wide smile on your face.

To sum up, we can only thank the entire crew for the spectacular project with an inspiring story of not giving up. The conclusion of my review is as brief as it can be – go and book your place in front of the big screen! You will not regret it. The massive number of emotions you can experience while watching The Shawshank Redemption will make you laugh or cry whenever you want.

9.title: A classic piece of unforgettable
9.content:
In its Oscar year, Shawshank Redemption (written and directed by Frank Darabont, after the novella Rita Hayworth and the Shawshank Redemption, by Stephen King) was nominated for seven Academy Awards, and walked away with zero. Best Picture went to Forrest Gump, while Shawshank and Pulp Fiction were "just happy to be nominated." Of course hindsight is 20/20, but while history looks back on Gump as a good film, Pulp and Redemption are remembered as some of the all-time best. Pulp, however, was a success from the word "go," making a huge splash at Cannes and making its writer-director an American master after only two films. For Andy Dufresne and Co., success didn't come easy. Fortunately, failure wasn't a life sentence.

After opening on 33 screens with take of $727,327, the $25M film fell fast from theatres and finished with a mere $28.3M. The reasons for failure are many. Firstly, the title is a clunker. While iconic to fans today, in 1994, people knew not and cared not what a 'Shawshank' was. On the DVD, Tim Robbins laughs recounting fans congratulating him on "that 'Rickshaw' movie." Marketing-wise, the film's a nightmare, as 'prison drama' is a tough sell to women, and the story of love between two best friends doesn't spell winner to men. Worst of all, the movie is slow as molasses. As Desson Thomson writes for the Washington Post, "it wanders down subplots at every opportunity and ignores an abundance of narrative exit points before settling on its finale." But it is these same weaknesses that make the film so strong.

Firstly, its setting. The opening aerial shots of the prison are a total eye-opener. This is an amazing piece of architecture, strong and Gothic in design. Immediately, the prison becomes a character. It casts its shadow over most of the film, its tall stone walls stretching above every shot. It towers over the men it contains, blotting out all memories of the outside world. Only Andy (Robbins) holds onto hope. It's in music, it's in the sandy beaches of Zihuatanejo; "In here's where you need it most," he says. "You need it so you don't forget. Forget that there are places in the world that aren't made out of stone. That there's a - there's a - there's something inside that's yours, that they can't touch." Red (Morgan Freeman) doesn't think much of Andy at first, picking "that tall glass o' milk with the silver spoon up his ass" as the first new fish to crack. Andy says not a word, and losing his bet, Red resents him for it. But over time, as the two get to know each other, they quickly become the best of friends. This again, is one of the film's major strengths. Many movies are about love, many flicks have a side-kick to the hero, but Shawshank is the only one I can think of that looks honestly at the love between two best friends. It seems odd that Hollywood would skip this relationship time and again, when it's a feeling that weighs so much into everyone's day to day lives. Perhaps it's too sentimental to seem conventional, but Shawshank's core friendship hits all the right notes, and the film is much better for it.

9.title: There are places in the world that are not made out of stone
9.content: Before I review this fascinating tale of abuse, intrigue and resourcefulness taking place in a penitentiary, let me state the following... "Bad things happen to good people." The movie starts with a court trial for the murder of a banker's wife. Our defendant is Andy Dufresne (Tim Robbins) accused of this crime and all the evidence or lack of points in his direction. Found guilty Andy and other recruits (little fishes ) are bused over to Shawshank Prison. During the ride, a portly (FAT ASS)Frank Medrano starts to whine about the fact that he's not suppose to be here.The rookie cons are greeted by the Warden Norton (Bob Gunton) who chillingly affirms at the end of his speech, "Welcome to Shawshank." Fat Ass continues to moan about being in jail but Captain Hadley (Clansy Brown) wanted to hear no part of his whining.Meanwhile the prison inmates where placing bets on which rookie con will crack under the strain of a first night in prison. As the neophytes walked down the main corridor to a loud bunch of inmate hecklers as they yelled endlessly,"Here fishy fishy." Veteran Con Ellis Redding AKA Red our narrator played by Morgan Freeman bet two packs of smokes on Andy Dufresne. Meanwhile the majority bet on Fat Ass to crack under the taunting and teasing of the hardened inmates. The mocking was too much for poor, hysterical Fat Ass as he screamed for his Mommy as Captain Hadley beat him endlessly with his night stick as he laid lifeless on the cement floor. Prison life was presented in all it's harsh realities right from the start. The next morning Red was amazed that Andy made it through the first night without making a sound. As the movie progressed Andy needs a rock hammer to make Chess pieces. Red being the prison hustler/scrounger can get mostly anything from the outside, magazines, liquor and posters. Red and Andy develop a friendship/bond. One day the Warden offered volunteer work for the inmates to tar the roof of the guard house. The names where picked at random and Andy and Red were among the chosen for the task. The first day as the men were dipping there mops into tar buckets under the hot sun, Andy overhears Captain Hadley complaining of an cash inheritance. The other guard congratulates him on his new found cash but Hadley says the government will tax him on every penny of it. Andy takes a u-turn toward Hadley and Says, "Do you trust your Wife?" Hadley enraged, grabs Andy and is ready to throw him off the roof. Andy in breathless desperation replies, There's a way to gift your spouse tax free and I'll can show you how to file the papers and it's perfectly legal for a small price of three beers for each man working on the roof. A few days later it came to pass as his fellow inmate looked on at Andy as they were swigging suds on a hot roof. The Cons at least for a little while felt like men thanks to Andy and his legal advise. Andy had won the respect of his peers. Despite doing curry-favor for the guards, with W2 forms and retirement advise Andy wasn't protected either. Being constantly harassed and beaten by Boggs and his pose (The Sisters). Boggs wanted Andy for sexual favors and I'd like to tell you Andy put up a good fight but the truth is Andy ended up in the hospital infirmary while Boggs laid in the hole of solitary confinement for a month. Word got out about Andy's nemesis to Hadley and the guards and they didn't want their personal Banker harmed any more. Boggs was beaten to a pulp and the Sisters never laid a hand on Andy again.The movie continues and shows the hopelessness of an innocent educated man adjusting to an institution. Making friends and gaining respect with his knowledge in a world of maladjusted criminals. Building a library and fudging the books under the direction of the Warden. This shows how a person entering the criminal system become institutionalized on a positive side and a negative side. Veteran actor James Whitmore give an impressive performance as Brooks the original weathered Librarian. Also notable was the performance by Tommy (Gil Bellows) who takes this story in a different direction. The appeal of this movie is how everything ties together in a hopeless situation and comes out clean on the other side. The original book (Stephen King), was at best, ho-humm by critics standards but the magic of the screenplay brought this story to new heights. Kudos to the screen writing of Frank Darabont. Never get tired of this movie.

9.title: The Shawshank Redemption
9.content: This touching and heart warming film is the most perfect celebration of the human spirit I have seen. Andy Dufresne, wrongly convicted of murdering his wife and her lover, finds the strength not only to change himself, but to bring hope to those around him in Shawshank Prison. This inspiring story is interwoven with a soundtrack which invokes every emotion, from haunting and chilling, to stirring and beautiful. When you go to see a movie and it touches you with its poetry, music, and its atmosphere, and leaves you with a sense of victorious satisfaction, it is a triumph. Field of Dreams was the first movie which invoked these emotions in me. Shawshank Redemption is even more powerful for its simplicity. It doesn't pretend to be clean, nor could it be called a family movie. It is brutal and violent at times, horrifying and sickening at others. However the title says it all. Redemption is what this story is all about. And it is not necessarily redemption for the actual crimes you might have committed, but it is redemption for the way you have lived your life. What emerges can only be called a maginificent piece of art. This is what movies were meant to be.

9.title: Gripping, Moving, and occasionally Mindbending!
9.content:
The Shawshank Redemption is a film that is continuously moving forward; a stream of characters and narrative arcs are put into the foreground for around 20 minutes each, in each of these, a different aspect of prison life is conveyed, and occasionally, the tone is entirely different from the previous one; despite this, the film avoids feeling anthology-like with a consistent setting.

Shawshank Prison feels living and breathing from the moment it first appears on the screen; via the forever-moving background characters, and the varied environments inside and outside of the prison! Shawshank itself is one of the most interesting things about this film, and quite possibly why it appeals to so many people; prison is an inherently interesting location to set a film; much like a school or workplace setting; there is a sense of order: people's routines are controlled by people above them - Shawshank combines the relatability of this with the crime and drama of a courtroom or heist film.

Please have a nice day, and enjoy the film!

9.title: The ONLLY Perfect Movie
9.content:
The film tells the story of Andy Dufresne (Tim Robbins), an educated banker sentenced to life for the murder of his wife and her lover. In prison, Andy inspires his fellow inmates with his courage and humanity and has a profound effect on Red (Morgan Freeman), an older prisoner, who has given up hope.

Unlike many films of the 90's, "The Shawshank Redemption" has "high concept" plot premise and is somewhat episodic compared with the tight, linear narratives of closer structured pictures. This sense of freedom in the storytelling allows the film to consistently throw up genuine surprises, as the viewer isn't constantly on guard for clues and plot points. In hindsight, we tend to forget how successfully director Frank Darabont leads us to expect a very different resolution.

"The Shawshank Redemption" does things well that you might not expect. It has lengthy voice-overs (that actually work well) and it has a sappy predictable ending, but yet these elements work because they are not placed in the over-used, meaningless context that movies today place them in. The voice overs are also consistently used in such a way that distinct worlds are created. There's a real world inside the prison and the surreal outside world.

These two distinct worlds are created help to place the viewer inside the halls of the prison, they are no longer watching a movie, but they are also feeling it.

This is a movie that will remain a favorite of the people for many decades to come. 10/10

9.title: The Shawshank Redemption: A Timeless Masterpiece of Hope and Resilience
9.content:
"The Shawshank Redemption," directed by Frank Darabont and based on Stephen King's novella, is a cinematic gem that has captivated audiences since its release in 1994. This film is more than just a story about prison life; it's a profound exploration of hope, friendship, and the indomitable human spirit.

Set in the grim confines of Shawshank State Penitentiary, the film follows the journey of Andy Dufresne (Tim Robbins), a banker unjustly convicted of murdering his wife and her lover. Despite the harsh realities of prison life, Andy remains steadfast and unbroken, befriending Ellis "Red" Redding (Morgan Freeman), a seasoned inmate who becomes his closest ally.

The narrative is expertly woven with themes of hope and redemption, making it a deeply emotional experience. Darabont's direction and the screenplay's pacing ensure that the story unfolds with perfect timing, allowing the audience to become fully immersed in the characters' lives and struggles.

Tim Robbins delivers a masterful performance as Andy, portraying his quiet strength and resilience with subtlety and grace. Morgan Freeman's portrayal of Red is equally compelling, his deep, resonant voice providing a poignant narration that adds depth to the film's introspective tone. The chemistry between Robbins and Freeman is palpable, their friendship forming the heart and soul of the story.

The cinematography by Roger Deakins captures the oppressive atmosphere of the prison while also highlighting moments of beauty and hope. Thomas Newman's hauntingly beautiful score enhances the emotional impact, perfectly complementing the film's mood and themes.

One of the film's most powerful aspects is its ability to inspire. Andy's unwavering hope and ingenuity in the face of seemingly insurmountable odds serve as a testament to the human spirit's resilience. His iconic line, "Hope is a good thing, maybe the best of things, and no good thing ever dies," resonates long after the credits roll, reminding viewers of the power of hope and perseverance.

"The Shawshank Redemption" is not just a film; it's an experience. It speaks to the core of human emotion and leaves a lasting impression on all who watch it. Its timeless message, outstanding performances, and masterful storytelling have cemented its place as one of the greatest films of all time. Whether you're watching it for the first time or the fiftieth, "The Shawshank Redemption" never fails to move and inspire, making it a must-see classic.

It is a strange comment to make about a film set inside a prison, but "The Shawshank Redemption" creates a warm hold on our feelings because it makes us a member of a family. Many movies offer us vicarious experiences and quick, superficial emotions. "Shawshank" slows down and looks. It uses the narrator's calm, observant voice to include us in the story of men who have formed a community behind bars. It is deeper than most films; about continuity in a lifetime, based on friendship and hope.

Darabont constructs the film to observe the story, not to punch it up or upstage it. Upstaging, in fact, is unknown in this film; the actors are content to stay within their roles, the story moves in an orderly way, and the film itself reflects the slow passage of the decades. "When they put you in that cell," Red says, "when those bars slam home, that's when you know it's for real. Old life blown away in the blink of an eye. Nothing left but all the time in the world to think about it." Watching the film again, I admired it even more than the first time I saw it. Affection for good films often grows with familiarity, as it does with music. Some have said life is a prison, we are Red, Andy is our redeemer. All good art is about something deeper than it admits.

9.title: A true underdog story
9.content: Shawshank Redemption is a film about the unlikely friendship between two men from different walks of life. Their paths would not have even crossed had Andy, portrayed by Tim Robbins, not been falsely imprisoned for the murder of his wife and her lover. Andy becomes friends with Red, played by Morgan Freeman; a prison bootlegger who was guilty of his crime of murder. This unlikely friendship becomes their saving grace. Their friendship makes their prison days more bearable until Andy's escape changes things. Red must serve his remaining sentence with memories of their time together. Andy left clues for Red to find him so they could be reunited. When Andy first arrives at the prison, Red and fellow inmates make bets on which new guy will break down first. Red chooses Andy on first sight. What a culture shock Andy and the new prisoners receive before they ever enter the cell block. We see them get verbally abused, stripped of their rights, showered with hoses, deloused, and made to march naked to their new homes. This stark transition makes the audience feel sympathy and humiliation for these men. When the first man breaks down that night, we see him get badly beaten by the guards. We find out in the morning that he didn't receive medical attention and died from the beating. Shawshank Redemption is one of those movies where you can help but root for the underdog. While we are unsure if Andy committed the crime he was sentenced for or not, you can't help but root for the guy. When it's revealed later on that he is not guilty, it makes you root for him even more. He had his chance to get out of prison as a free man but the warden eliminated that opportunity. The only way Andy was able to leave that prison was on his own terms. Set in 1947, Shawshank Redemption stays true to its timeframe. There are not any special effects or elaborate film techniques that wouldn't have been seen during this time. At no time is the story overshadowed by theatrics or surroundings. The lighting and sound effects appear as natural as if watching it all from across a room. The small details are what make this movie so believable. Shawshank Redemption can be compared to The Green Mile. Another film set in a 1930's prison. Both movies force the audience to look beyond the crimes the men have been convicted of and look at the man himself. Both movies have strong actors and strong supporting roles. Both movies are made with careful detail allowing the story to take center stage. While there are many prison movies out there to choose from, Shawshank Redemption tops the list. What makes this movie great is that it's not about the escape but it's about the relationships formed leading up to the escape. The real treat is seeing these friends reunited against all odds later in life.

9.title: The most effective prison movies in cinematic history
9.content: The Shawshank Redemption has certainly earned its reputation as one of the most effective prison movies in cinematic history - as the film, written and directed by Frank Darabont, contains virtually all of the tropes and devices that the genre has come to be associated with. The ensuing inclusion of such familiar elements as the Evil Warden and the Sadistic Guard are undeniably put to brilliant use by Darabont, with the end result a piece of work that - aside from a midsection that's almost egregiously episodic - manages to hold the viewer transfixed virtually from start to finish. The Shawshank Redemption works not only as an excellent prison drama,but as a metaphor for overcoming our own private prisons.

Frank Darabont clearly wanted to go out a create a masterpiece, and truly succeeded. There is no way this film can ever be forgotten, see for yourself.

9.title: Shawshank Review - A True Modern Classic
9.content:
There are thousands of written reviews for this film on this website and the majority of them positive. I know I am just adding to this long list of positive reviews, but I feel this film deserves to be my first review on this website.

While this film may not be my favourite film, it is most definitely a film I respect. When I was young and watching 'The Goonies' and 'Back to the Future' I thought films were only made to entertain and were not made to convey a clear message about humanity. This film was the first film I watched that made me understand that the film medium could provide the world with such philosophical messages and could teach young people, like me, that life must be valued. Pretty deep right? Well this is the message that the film carries.

Red values Andy's friendship and life. He does not want him to die and wants him to survive and when I was watching this film I thought... wow! Two prisoners, one who definitely killed another person, can be so rational and kind. I learnt from this film that the world is a horrible place and emotions can get the better of people; but through it all, it is about moving on and making sure that one is not affected by the emotional trauma that has arrived at their front door and instead take that trauma and improve themselves and other people like Andy did throughout the film. By the end, when Red and Andy are embracing on the beach, free, I see two men who have been through years of pain and self-pity clear of all negative thoughts; I see two friends that through all the emotional trauma that we see them going through are still strong.

Now I can talk about themes and the impact that this film had on me all day long, but I have to praise everyone involved in this film. Tim Robbins and Morgan Freeman embody their characters perfectly and when I watch it now as a 17 year old who has seen his fair share of great performances these stick out as real people and not simply a performance. Frank Darababont, who not only directed the film but also wrote it, crafts a film that is very entertaining to watch but that also conveys these themes effortlessly and writes some very memorable lines that really affect one's perspective on human nature. The scene with Brooks is a scene that had me close to tears and that showed me the impact of being 'institutionalized'.

Anyway, I have said enough about this film. It is very good and really pushed me into seeing films in a different light. If you want to read any more reviews or my list on my favourite films of all time please check me out. Thank you for reading this.

Having heard about Morgan Freeman's stunning performance, I would even go as far as saying it might be his best performance in a feature film. The film focuses on Morgan Freeman's retelling of a story about a bond of two imprisoned men, finding hope when they could not believe into anything anymore.

The film is set in prison and therefore anyone watching should be prepared for some harsh scenes and animalistic behaviour that is expected from the 'cliché' prison inmates. The film tries to accomplish a unique feat, humanising the inmates and trying to make it out to the audience that everyone is human and always has a part of humanity in them. It shows it by breaking the characters will and leaving them in despair, only grasping for the last glimmer of hope that helps them survive in the disturbing prison situations.

Morgan Freeman's performance plays a substantial part in the whole film, surely presenting itself as one of his best narrated works, however it is the interaction between him and Tim Robbins that really stands out, the contrast between them is what makes the movie interesting to watch, which lead to me not pausing once during the whole movie. Despite showing us the world full of unfairness, cruelty and greed, it delivers a powerful message of kindness and hope, making you want to change something in your life after watching the film. 9.title: Good Movie

Really I loved this movie

Forget about what others (including myself) might suggest you'll discover in "The Shawshank Redemption;" when you watch it, you'll identify something very personal in your own life with a scene, a character, or a moment in this uncomplicated movie. When you need hope, you'll look for Shawshank. When you want to believe in the will of overcoming even the greatest obstacles, Shawshank will uplift you in ways that you can't find in movies today.

Some liken the film to some kind of spiritual awakening. Of course, some can go to a church or mosque to find enlightenment and Faith in humanity, but most places of worship are open only certain days or times. But when you need affirmation of the lasting bond of friendships that prevail over the most dire circumstances, Shawshank will give it to you. It makes grown men (like me) cry, still. I wonder whether Shawshank was truly meant for viewing in the privacy of the home, because it is a personal experience that really makes you look inward. Nominated for seven, this is the best film that never one a single Oscar.

How ironic that an innocent man winds up being surrounded by the corruption of the legal system. Shawshank itself is similar to the character of Andy Dufresne. Prejudging this classic film, critics couldn't get past the title. The public followed suit, initially dismissing Shawshank, which failed in the box office just like "It's a Wonderful Life" and "Citizen Kane." It could have just whithered away on the store shelves, like Andy Dufresne could have in his own cell. But the characters prevailed, because Andy -- And Shawshank -- stayed true. Now, these movies are right up there as the most popular films of all time.

9.title: A Timeless Masterpiece
9.content:
There aren't a whole lot of films as hopeful and unyielding as The Shawshank Redemption. Director Frank Darabont's adaptation of Stephen King's novella, Rita Hayworth and The Shawshank Redemption, is a drama as heartbreaking as it is relentless. Much of the emotion comes from convicted banker Andy Dufresne (Tim Robbins) and his lifelong camaraderie with inmate Ellis "Red" Redding (Morgan Freeman).

Darabont's pacing is slow but amply rewarded, and each shot is able to take root in the viewer's mind. Roger Deakins' cinematography elegantly captured the claustrophobia of prison life with the aspirations of freedom and hope. Thomas Newman's haunting score also contributes greatly.

Robbins and Freeman give fine performances, and Freeman's voiceover narration helps to make the movie quite intimate. The themes of determination, friendship, and resilience of humans showcased in the film stays with audiences long after the final credit disappears.

The Shawshank Redemption might have bombed at the box office, but it's now one of the best films ever produced-worthy of its number one ranking on IMDb list. It is a film every movie buff must watch.

9.title: More than a movie, an experience
9.content:
*spoilers* In The Shawshank Redemption, Andy Dufresne is presented as an aspirational figure, an innocent man who's put in a horrible situation for decades but who, despite it all, continuously projects hope. True hope comes to fruition only in continuity, as is the case for Andy. Through life's struggles it is vital to keep your mind occupied with activities that give you hope and dreams that fuel that hope, even while you're being dragged through the mud.

While the movie is narrated to us entirely through Red's perspective, and we never see Andy's thoughts, what we do see is his influence over Red. Symbolically, Brooks Hatlen is what would have become of Red without Andy, without hope. He shows us that freedom means nothing without hopefulness, you may as well be dead.

Another important component in the brilliance of this film is the importance of human connection. We see this through the contrast that the warden represents. Despite having his faith, the warden becomes extremely corrupt over the years, even committing murder and finally, suicide. His trajectory can be considered the opposite of Andy's. He's a regular man who becomes very lucky in a matter of years and doesn't deserve it one bit. The movie shows us how easy it is to fly off the handle when we lose our humanity and give in to ego. His final moments indicate finally that he has lost all hope, unlike his counterpart Andy, despite their severely differing situations.

The Shawshank Redemption is a beautiful and moving film that will send chills down your spine. It's original screenplay, incredible performances and astounding music will make for an experience you won't soon forget.

9.title: The Shawshank Redemption: A Timeless Masterpiece
9.content:
The Shawshank Redemption is a film that has captivated audiences since its release in 1994. Directed by Frank Darabont and based on Stephen King's novella, this cinematic gem has become a beloved classic and is often hailed as one of the greatest movies of all time. Some essential things make The Shawshank Redemption a must-watch and explore its enduring appeal.

The Plot: At its core, The Shawshank Redemption follows the story of Andy Dufresne, a banker who is wrongfully convicted of murder and sentenced to life in Shawshank State Penitentiary. Within the confines of this harsh environment, Andy befriends a fellow inmate, Ellis "Red" Redding, portrayed brilliantly by Morgan Freeman. Through their unlikely bond, the narrative unfolds, weaving a tale of hope, resilience, and the power of friendship. The film takes the audience on an emotional rollercoaster as they witness Andy's relentless pursuit of freedom and eventual redemption.

Cinematic Excellence: One cannot discuss The Shawshank Redemption without acknowledging the impeccable execution of its various elements. From the compelling performances to the seamless direction, every aspect of the film contributes to its brilliance. Tim Robbins delivers a powerhouse performance as Andy, effortlessly portraying the character's intelligence, strength, and unwavering determination. The chemistry between Robbins and Freeman is palpable, enhancing the authenticity of their friendship and making it the heart of the movie.

The Shawshank Redemption also stands out for its visually stunning cinematography. The deliberate use of color palettes and lighting techniques adds depth and symbolism to each scene, effectively immersing the viewer into the world of Shawshank. The hauntingly beautiful score by Thomas Newman complements the narrative perfectly, evoking a wide range of emotions that stay with the audience even after the credits roll.

Themes of Hope and Redemption: One of the main reasons The Shawshank Redemption resonates with audiences is its exploration of profound themes. The film depicts the indomitable power of hope amidst despair and the transformative nature of redemption. Through the character of Andy, we witness his unwavering belief in the possibility of a better future, inspiring others around him to hold onto their own dreams. The movie serves as a reminder that no matter how dire the circumstances may be, the human spirit can triumph against all odds.

Movie's importance: The Shawshank Redemption may not have achieved commercial success upon its initial release, but it garnered widespread critical acclaim and has since gained a dedicated following. Its enduring popularity can be attributed to its universal themes, nuanced storytelling, and exceptional performances. Over the years, the film has been celebrated for its profound messages of hope, friendship, and the resilience of the human spirit.

The Shawshank Redemption is a cinematic masterpiece that continues to captivate audiences and inspire viewers around the world. Its timeless tale of hope, friendship, and redemption resonates with audiences of all generations, making it a truly remarkable film. From the stellar performances to the expert direction, every aspect of this movie contributes to its enduring legacy. Whether you are a fan of drama, crime, or simply appreciate storytelling at its finest, The Shawshank Redemption is a must-watch that will leave a lasting impact on your heart and mind.

9.title: Shawshank Redemption
9.content:
Imagine that you are an ordinary law-abiding citizen. It will not be difficult for most of us to imagine this, since we are law-abiding citizens (if anything, I won't extradite it). It is also not difficult to imagine that you are married to a rather beautiful woman. There are some of us. Your wealth is above average, right? Do you live in the USA?

Yes, gradually this impromptu sociological survey narrows the circle; more and more people drop out of it: some do not have a wife, others have a prestigious job in a bank, others live in China, Uruguay or the village of Malye Gryazyuki. But the tragedy of Andrew Dufresne touches everyone.

Can it happen that under the influence of stress, intoxication and resentment, you use a weapon, pointing it at your beloved wife and her lover? After that, you can repent of the crime, you can imagine that all this is a dream, or you can try to deceive the investigation. One way or another, the first half of the film does not give a clear answer to the question: is Andy guilty? He may be a victim of circumstances, or he may be a cold-blooded maniac. But the judge has absolutely no doubts. His sentence is not severe, but cruel. Two life sentences in Shawshank Prison.

How would you feel? At first, the full horror of the situation does not reach you, there is hope that someone will stand in the courtroom and protect you, present some evidence of innocence ... but no. The bus with the same people as you is loaded to the eyeballs and goes to the hospitable monastery of convicts. Newcomers are welcomed with open arms (in every sense of the word), rarely let go, and for many, leaving a correctional facility is a tragedy only comparable to entering it. Tests begin immediately - when the prison gates swing open - and do not stop for a second. And when you enter the cell on stiff legs, you understand that now this is your home. And you have plenty of time to think about how you got here. Despair, you say? Oh yeah! And only a few not only think about how they got here and put up with it, but also think about how to get out of here. Preferably until the end of the sentence. This is Andy Dufresne.

How many films have we seen where the setting was a prison? It seems that there is nothing more to say in this topic - pain, trials, hopelessness, longing for freedom, for relatives and friends, male friendship, enmity, cruel guards ... - a standard set. But King's adaptation is taking its toll. The hero is weak. He does not have a mountain of muscles to survive in prison, like the heroes of some Stallone and Van Damme. He has no influential acquaintances. He has no one outside the prison walls at all. Everything he had was taken away. First on the killer of his wife, then on the verdict of the court.

Andy, that tall, stooping banker, couldn't survive in prison. Shouldn't have. But against all laws and theories of probability, he began to fight for his life. The strongest spirit was imprisoned in this clumsy weak body. So strong that the confines of the prison could not hold him forever. Did he think about running away from the very beginning? Unlikely. He just fought for his life, throwing small brushwood into the weakening fire of hope.

Hopelessness manifests itself in the simplest, but extremely effective ways. A voice-over informs that five years have already passed ... ten ... fifteen ... and in the life of prisoners everything goes on as usual, only the beauties on the posters in the cell replace each other. Time cuts you like a sharp razor. How can you keep hope for so long? Is it even possible? How is unknown, but what is possible, Andy proved. Despite the attacks of the head of the prison and other prisoners, despite the fact that no one believed in him.

Hope is a dangerous thing. Hope can drive a person crazy. (c) Red

How can you talk about a movie like The Shawshank Redemption? Any words will not be enough. Here and friendship, and survival, and questions about justice, willpower and the meaning of life. What is freedom? Can a prisoner feel the wind of freedom, and a free person languish in the conclusion of the stereotypes of life? Freedom is an ephemeral concept. If you are free to go anywhere, but still go to your boring job every day, and this will continue until retirement, are you free? Hardly. Only by earning freedom can one learn to appreciate it. And only then you will feel its true taste. And a prison can become an excellent school for survival ... or maybe life?

The prison in Escape is the whole world. There is a Leader here, there is an army, there is a handful of rebels, but most of this world consists of a gray mass of hopeless inhabitants. This is what makes them so gray, identical and not at all shabby prison uniforms.

The film does not provide answers to the questions "Why do we live?" and "How to live?". He just puts them right. So after watching, I want to scroll through all these events in my head again and think. Despite the gloomy surroundings of the picture, it evokes only bright feelings. And for this paradox alone, I want to applaud.

Does it make sense to analyze this film, like all the others, using hackneyed clichés like acting or composing? Do I need to say how hard the cameraman tried and how wisely the director managed the shooting? Hardly. This film is striking in its integrity - everything is in its place, ideally suited to each other. Each episode harmoniously complements the other, making the characters of the film not just living people, but family people. When the film ends, its magic is still working on the viewer. The history of Man remains in his soul. The aftertaste is like a glass of aged red wine, slightly tart, but still sweet. Unlike most "prison movies" (that's what many disrespectfully call "Escape..."), this aftertaste lasts surprisingly long. And even years later, remembering the final scene, you will be sure that there is no happier person in the world than Andy Dufresne.

Hope is the best thing in the world. She doesn't let us die. (c) Andy.

Keep your "tens" and other marks with you. The rating scale for this film has not yet been invented. If cinema could be compared to a winery, then I would say about Darabont's film that you don't want to drink this bottle, but to drink it.

9.title: A Testament to Friendship and Hope
9.content:
Derived from Stephen King's bestselling novel, "Shawshank Redemption" is an inspirational film that delves deep into the essence of true friendship. Set against the backdrop of a daunting prison, viewers are captivated by the brilliance of Frank Darabont's directorial prowess. In essence, the movie narrates the experiences of a renowned banker, Andy Dufresne, who finds himself incarcerated for the murder of his own wife. His encounter with a fellow inmate named Ellis 'Red' Redding transforms his prison life for the better.

The captivating narrative of "Shawshank Redemption" unfolds as Andy Dufresne, portrayed brilliantly by Tim Robbins, navigates the challenges of imprisonment following a wrongful conviction. Amidst the harsh realities of prison life, Andy forms an unlikely yet profound friendship with Red, played by Morgan Freeman, which serves as the cornerstone of the film's emotional depth and resonance.

One of the central themes of "Shawshank Redemption" is the journey of redemption and resilience. Through Andy's unwavering determination and intelligence, coupled with Red's wisdom and loyalty, the film showcases the transformative power of friendship in the darkest of circumstances. The bond forged between Andy and Red transcends the confines of prison walls, offering hope, solace, and ultimately, redemption.

The dynamic between Andy and Red is intricately woven, depicting a relationship built on trust, mutual respect, and unwavering support. Andy's strategic mind and ability to navigate complex situations not only earn him respect among fellow inmates but also instill a sense of hope and purpose within the bleak prison environment. Red, known for his resourcefulness and connections, becomes Andy's confidant and ally, showcasing a profound evolution in character as the story unfolds.

Under Frank Darabont's masterful direction, "Shawshank Redemption" transcends the typical prison drama genre, captivating audiences with its poignant storytelling and emotional depth. Darabont skillfully captures the nuances of human relationships within the confines of incarceration, highlighting themes of friendship, loyalty, and the enduring quest for freedom.

Since its release, "Shawshank Redemption" has achieved iconic status in popular culture, resonating with audiences worldwide and earning critical acclaim for its stellar performances, compelling narrative, and timeless themes. The film's enduring legacy lies in its ability to evoke profound emotions and provoke introspection, making it a timeless classic that continues to inspire and captivate new generations of viewers.
